a_rows_sample.anchor: Eight-type drift taxonomy: distribution, conditional, label, structural, parameter, semantic, governance, architectural
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines eight drift types: concept/conditional drift P_t(Y|X)!=P_{t+1}(Y|X) (the X-Y relationship changed, potentially more consequential than input drift); distribution drift P_t(X)!=P_{t+1}(X) (input population changed); label drift P_t(Y)!=P_{t+1}(Y) (outcome prevalence changed); structural drift (a causal edge A->B present before a redesign no longer holds, A-not->B); parameter drift (A->B structure persists but strength beta_t != beta_{t+1}); semantic drift (Meaning(Approved,t1) != Meaning(Approved,t2)); governance drift (Policy_t1 != Policy_t2, historical decisions remain historical); architectural drift (Architecture_2025 != Architecture_2026, claims about one should not automatically apply to the other). Consolidates: Drift in {Distribution, Conditional, Label, Parameter, Structural, Semantic, Governance, Architectural} -- useful because different drift types require different responses.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Drift detection threshold; statistical drift versus operationally material drift; materiality-gated local adaptation
a_rows_sample.statement: A generic drift detector evaluates divergence D(P_t,P_{t+1}) > delta for a chosen threshold delta, but a huge dataset can make tiny changes statistically significant (p<0.001) without operational relevance, so drift detection must distinguish StatisticalDrift from OperationallyMaterialDrift; defines Material(D,d) (drift D materially affects decision d) so a detected drift need not trigger global recomputation. If drift affects only BC_A, only K_A should be updated without unnecessarily invalidating K_B, K_C -- 'this follows directly from bounded-context isolation'.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Drift-triggered investigation; DriftDetected does not imply ModelInvalid
a_rows_sample.statement: If DriftScore > delta, KnowledgeOS can generate an InvestigationRequest, but DriftDetected does not automatically imply ModelInvalid -- it triggers investigation, not automatic invalidation.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Twelve falsification experiments for Step 45 adaptive-learning model (all PASS)
a_rows_sample.statement: Runs twelve falsification tests, all PASS: (1) new evidence contradicts an old interpretation => interpretation revised, original evidence unchanged; (2) a model becomes obsolete => historical decisions retain the old model version; (3) a new model performs better => does not automatically replace the active model unless promotion policy allows it; (4) input distribution changes but decision-relevant behavior does not => distribution drift recorded without declaring causal/model failure; (5) statistically significant drift has negligible operational impact => no automatic critical escalation from statistical significance alone; (6) a model predicts poorly despite good historical calibration => performance reevaluated, calibration alone does not protect the model; (7) a successful outcome follows a poor decision => outcome success does not automatically validate decision quality; (8) a justified decision produces an adverse low-probability outcome => not automatically classified as irrational; (9) a governance policy changes => future decisions use the new policy, historical decisions retain the old policy version; (10) a new interpretation of old evidence is created => both historical and current interpretations remain traceable; (11) a model trained on one bounded context detects drift => impact stays scoped to relevant contexts unless evidence supports broader generalization; (12) a candidate model performs well in shadow mode but violates a safety constraint => cannot be promoted.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Parameter drift, distribution/covariate shift (DistributionShift⇏ModelFailure), concept drift, calibration decay with a model-status lifecycle (experiments 1-4)
a_rows_sample.statement: Experiment 1: P_t0(Y|X) != P_t1(Y|X) detected as parameter drift needing possible recalibration, given tracked temporal model performance -- PASS. Experiment 2: P_train(X) != P_prod(X) detected as DistributionShiftDetected -- PASS; but explicitly DistributionShift ⇏ ModelFailure since P(Y|X) may remain unchanged -- 'a warning condition', not automatic failure. Experiment 3: P_t(Y=1|X=1) changing from 0.8 to 0.4 while the model keeps using the old relationship is detected as ConceptDrift -- PASS. Experiment 4: calibration monitored by temporal window; predictions remaining P=0.8 while realized success drops from ~80% to 55% is CalibrationDecay, and performance deteriorating beyond tolerance sets ModelStatus=Degraded -- PASS. Suggests a model lifecycle Experimental -> Validated -> Production -> Degraded -> Suspended -> Retired as domain/governance states, not mathematical truths.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 96.13 — Concept drift ... D_t distribution of reality. D_{t1}≠D_{t2}. A model that was accurate under D_{t1} may become inaccurate under D_{t2}.
a_rows_sample.statement: Restates concept drift: reality's distribution D_t can change (D_{t1}≠D_{t2}), degrading a previously accurate model.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 96.14 — Experiment 7 ... Model accuracy 95% during t1. After organizational change: 70%. Expected: KnowledgeOS detects possible model degradation rather than assuming historical performance continues. Result: PASS
a_rows_sample.statement: Experiment 7: a model's accuracy dropping from 95% to 70% after organizational change must be detected as possible degradation, not assumed continued; result PASS.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 96.15 — Model validity is temporal ... Valid(M,t,C) rather than simply Valid(M). A model may be valid only within a declared context.
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines model validity as Valid(M,t,C) — temporal and context-scoped, not a context-free Valid(M).

a_rows_sample.anchor: 96.16 — Experiment 8 ... Model was validated for Domain=A. It is applied to Domain=B. Expected: applicability is not automatically established. Result: PASS
a_rows_sample.statement: Experiment 8: applying a Domain-A-validated model to Domain B does not automatically establish applicability; result PASS.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 96.19 — Data quality changes model assurance ... if Quality(D)↓ then potentially Confidence(M)↓. Not necessarily linear, but must be represented where relevant.
a_rows_sample.statement: States Quality(D)↓ potentially implies Confidence(M)↓ (not necessarily linearly), requiring explicit representation.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 96.20 — Experiment 10 ... Training dataset contains systematic bias. Model achieves excellent benchmark accuracy. Expected: benchmark accuracy does not prove real-world validity. Result: PASS
a_rows_sample.statement: Experiment 10: high benchmark accuracy on a systematically biased dataset does not prove real-world validity; result PASS.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 96.52 — Knowledge regression ... A new model may reduce knowledge quality. Precision(M_1)>Precision(M_2). But aggregate performance may hide failures in a critical domain.
a_rows_sample.statement: Warns aggregate model performance can hide domain-specific regression, even when Precision(M_1)>Precision(M_2) is not the case overall.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 96.53 — Experiment 26 ... Overall accuracy 96%. Critical architecture classification accuracy 72%. Expected: overall metric alone is insufficient. Result: PASS
a_rows_sample.statement: Experiment 26: 96% overall accuracy masking 72% critical-domain accuracy shows the overall metric alone is insufficient; result PASS.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 96.54 — Domain-specific assurance ... Assurance(M,D,C) rather than merely Assurance(M).
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines domain-specific assurance Assurance(M,D,C), not merely Assurance(M).

b_rows_sample.anchor: Steps 91-95 established Refinement→Concurrency→Failure→Security→Privacy. But KnowledgeOS is not static; it must evolve. Evolution ⇏ Semantic Corruption.
b_rows_sample.statement: States Step 96's requirement Evolution ⇏ Semantic Corruption: KnowledgeOS must learn and evolve without silently changing the meaning or validity of existing knowledge/decisions.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 96.1 — Learning is a state transition ... K_t. New evidence E_{t+1} produces K_{t+1}=Update(K_t,E_{t+1}). Learning is itself a mathematical transition.
b_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes learning as an explicit state transition K_{t+1}=Update(K_t,E_{t+1}) rather than a vague 'the system learns'.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 96.2 — Experiment 1 ... K_0: Policy P is active. E_1: P was revoked. Expected: K_1=Update(K_0,E_1) must represent the new state without rewriting the historical fact that P was previously active. Result: PASS
b_rows_sample.statement: Experiment 1: updating knowledge after a policy revocation must not rewrite the historical fact that the policy was previously active; result PASS.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 96.3 — Learning must not rewrite history ... CurrentKnowledge ≠ HistoricalKnowledge. If new evidence changes what we currently believe, it does not necessarily change what was known or believed earlier.
b_rows_sample.statement: States CurrentKnowledge ≠ HistoricalKnowledge: updated current belief does not retroactively change what was known/believed earlier.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 96.4 — Experiment 2 ... At t1: K(P)=True. At t2: E(P)=False. Expected: KnowledgeOS retains P(t1)=True and P(t2)=False. Result: PASS
b_rows_sample.statement: Experiment 2: both P(t1)=True and P(t2)=False must be retained rather than overwritten; result PASS.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 96.5 — Revision versus contradiction ... Revision, Correction, Contradiction, Refinement, ScopeChange. These must not be collapsed.
b_rows_sample.statement: Distinguishes five non-collapsible categories of knowledge change: Revision, Correction, Contradiction, Refinement, ScopeChange.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 96.6 — Experiment 3 ... Old statement SystemSupports(X). New evidence: SystemSupports(X) only under condition C. Expected: the new knowledge may refine the old statement: SystemSupports(X|C). Result: PASS
b_rows_sample.statement: Experiment 3: new conditional evidence refines rather than contradicts an old unconditional statement (SystemSupports(X)→SystemSupports(X|C)); result PASS.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 96.7 — Knowledge evolution is versioned ... K^(1), K^(2), K^(3) rather than one mutable blob called Knowledge.
b_rows_sample.statement: States knowledge evolution must be versioned (K^(1), K^(2), K^(3)...) rather than treated as one mutable blob.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 96.8 — Experiment 4 ... An architecture decision from 2025 references KnowledgeVersion=7. Current knowledge is Version=12. Expected: the historical decision remains linked to version 7. Result: PASS
b_rows_sample.statement: Experiment 4: a 2025 decision referencing KnowledgeVersion=7 remains linked to version 7 despite current Version=12; result PASS.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 96.9 — Model evolution ... M_1 is replaced by M_2. A prediction produced under M_1 must not be silently represented as though it came from M_2.
b_rows_sample.statement: States a model-generated prediction under M_1 must not be silently attributed to a later model M_2.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 96.10 — Experiment 5 ... Prediction Y_1 was generated using M_1. Current model M_2. Expected: Model(Y_1)=M_1. Result: PASS
b_rows_sample.statement: Experiment 5 confirms Model(Y_1)=M_1 is retained regardless of the current model version; result PASS.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 96.11 — Model provenance ... Result=(InputVersion,ModelVersion,Configuration,Timestamp,Agent,PolicyVersion). This extends Step 92's decision snapshot.
b_rows_sample.statement: Extends Step 92's decision snapshot tuple to model-generated Result=(InputVersion,ModelVersion,Configuration,Timestamp,Agent,PolicyVersion).

b_rows_sample.anchor: 96.12 — Experiment 6 ... AI produces 'architecture is compliant.' But the system cannot determine which model, policy, evidence, prompt/context. Expected: the result has weak reproducibility and weak assurance. Result: PASS
b_rows_sample.statement: Experiment 6: an AI compliance claim without traceable model/policy/evidence/context has weak reproducibility and assurance; result PASS.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 96.17 — Training data provenance ... M←trainedOn—D. An AI model is also a derived artifact.
b_rows_sample.statement: States a trained model is itself a derived artifact requiring training-data provenance M←trainedOn—D.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 96.18 — Experiment 9 ... Model is deployed. Training data provenance is unknown. Expected: the system cannot make strong claims about DataCoverage or DataQuality. Result: PASS
b_rows_sample.statement: Experiment 9: a model deployed without training-data provenance cannot support strong DataCoverage/DataQuality claims; result PASS.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 96.21 — Learning from outcomes ... Error=Loss(p,O). This produces new evidence about model performance.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines model-performance evidence via Error=Loss(prediction,ObservedOutcome).

b_rows_sample.anchor: 96.22 — Experiment 11 ... AI predicts Risk=0.2. Observed outcome indicates high risk. Expected: the mismatch becomes evidence for future model evaluation. Result: PASS
b_rows_sample.statement: Experiment 11: a prediction-outcome mismatch (Risk=0.2 predicted vs high risk observed) becomes evidence for future model evaluation; result PASS.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 96.23 — Feedback loop ... Prediction→Action→Outcome→Observation→ModelEvaluation→ModelRevision. This is the learning loop of KnowledgeOS.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines the KnowledgeOS learning loop Prediction→Action→Outcome→Observation→ModelEvaluation→ModelRevision.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 96.27 — Experiment 13 ... 'The incident would have occurred without intervention.' Expected: unless supported by an appropriate causal model, this remains a counterfactual inference, not an observed fact. Result: PASS
b_rows_sample.statement: Experiment 13: an unsupported counterfactual claim ('the incident would have occurred') remains an inference, not an observed fact, absent a supporting causal model; result PASS.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 96.28 — Model updates need governance ... M_1→M_2 may affect decisions, workflows, risk, compliance, authorization, outputs. Model evolution itself may become a governance event.
b_rows_sample.statement: States a model update can affect decisions/workflows/risk/compliance/authorization/outputs, making model evolution itself a governance event.

a_rows_sample.statement: Chapter II.4's four claims: the 3C pass's procedural rules are a ruling [R]; the boundary-vs-formal conformance profile is evidence [E]; the seams and their dispositions are evidence/method [E/M]; and the generalized 'findings must survive to ruling' lesson is marked as interpretation [IN].

a_rows_sample.anchor: a scope plan approved before any testing; five verdicts only (CONFORMANT, PARTIALLY CONFORMANT, NON-CONFORMANT, NOT ESTABLISHED, OUT OF SCOPE); *no silent upgrade* of NOT ESTABLISHED; evidence ⟦E⟧ separated from interpretation ⟦INT⟧ with verdicts resting on evidence alone; and the cardinal rule — 3C
a_rows_sample.statement: The 3C conformance-pass protocol: a scope plan pre-approved before testing begins; exactly five allowed verdicts (CONFORMANT, PARTIALLY CONFORMANT, NON-CONFORMANT, NOT ESTABLISHED, OUT OF SCOPE); a rule against silently upgrading a NOT ESTABLISHED verdict; strict separation of evidence from interpretation, with verdicts resting on evidence alone; and the cardinal rule that the pass tests the model but never repairs it -- difference is a finding, not a defect.

a_rows_sample.statement: 3C's result: the running repository conforms to the ratified model at its boundaries (human-act authority assignment, adoption/authorization separation, no-skip in practice, fail-closed authorization code) but not at the formal layer -- no executable counterpart exists for any formal object -- stated at exactly that strength, explicitly not read as 'the model is wrong'.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Detecting a contradiction != resolving a contradiction. KnowledgeOS must be able to detect and preserve unresolved conflict without inventing an answer
a_rows_sample.statement: States the central principle distinguishing contradiction detection from resolution.

a_rows_sample.anchor: K_i. The organization therefore has mathcal K = {K_1,K_2,...,K_n}. There is no requirement that K_1=K_2
a_rows_sample.statement: Formally defines the multi-context knowledge collection with no equality requirement between contexts.

a_rows_sample.anchor: A in K_1 and B in K_2. We cannot immediately say A and B is contradictory. We first need semantic translation T_{1->*}(A) and T_{2->*}(B)
a_rows_sample.statement: Requires semantic translation before evaluating cross-context contradiction.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Compatible(A,B,C). Possible values: {Compatible, Contradictory, Conditional, Unknown, NotApplicable}. This is preferable to a binary relation
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines a graded five-value compatibility relation, preferable to binary contradiction.

a_rows_sample.anchor: A genuine contradiction occurs when, under a common semantic interpretation and compatible conditions, A=>P and B=>not P. Then A perp B under the relevant context
a_rows_sample.statement: Formally defines genuine contradiction requiring common interpretation and compatible conditions.

a_rows_sample.anchor: A perp B under C_1 but not under C_2. Therefore contradiction must carry Context
a_rows_sample.statement: States contradiction is itself contextual.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The service is available vs The service is unavailable ... Availability_Production and Availability_Test ... A not-perp B. The apparent contradiction was caused by missing context
a_rows_sample.statement: Worked production-vs-test availability example showing an apparent contradiction dissolved by context.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Before declaring contradiction, KnowledgeOS should attempt ContextResolution. This is another epistemic investigation
a_rows_sample.statement: Requires context disambiguation as an epistemic investigation prior to declaring contradiction.

a_rows_sample.anchor: ServerIP=10.61.133.85 at t_1. ServerIP=10.61.133.90 at t_2. These are not contradictory if t_1 != t_2 and the state changed. TemporalAlignment must precede contradiction detection
a_rows_sample.statement: Worked temporal-alignment example requiring time alignment prior to contradiction evaluation.

a_rows_sample.anchor: A(t_1)=True and B(t_2)=True. This demonstrates Truth can be indexed by time
a_rows_sample.statement: States truth can be time-indexed, both statements can be simultaneously true at their respective times.

a_rows_sample.anchor: System supports TLS1.3 under Configuration=C_1. System does not support TLS1.3 under Configuration=C_2. the apparent contradiction disappears when conditions are represented
a_rows_sample.statement: Worked TLS-configuration example of conditional (non-genuine) contradiction.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Align(A,B) = (Entity, Time, Context, Scope, Semantics, Conditions). Only after sufficient alignment should contradiction be evaluated
a_rows_sample.statement: Formally defines the six-dimension alignment required before contradiction evaluation.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Claim A -> Context/Time/Entity/Scope/Semantics -> ALIGNMENT <- Claim B/Translation -> Compatibility Analysis -> Yes/No/Unknown -> OK/Conflict/Investigate
a_rows_sample.statement: Presents a contradiction-detection pipeline diagram.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Two contexts can conflict operationally without making logically contradictory statements ... DeployImmediately and DeployOnlyAfterApproval. These are conflicting prescriptions. But they are not necessarily factual contradictions
a_rows_sample.statement: Distinguishes operational/normative conflict from factual contradiction, worked with a deployment-policy example.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Factual conflict: P versus not P. Semantic conflict: Same term, incompatible meanings. Normative conflict: Different rules prescribe incompatible actions. Conflict != Contradiction
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines three conflict classes (factual/semantic/normative) distinct from logical contradiction.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Rule_1: A->Action_1 and Rule_2: A->Action_2 where Action_1 != Action_2. Then there is a policy conflict
a_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes normative conflict as incompatible rule-prescribed actions.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Rule_A comes from ArchitectureBoard and Rule_B comes from ProjectTeam. They may have different authority levels. Authority(Source,Rule,Context) becomes relevant
a_rows_sample.statement: Introduces source-and-context-relative authority for resolving normative conflicts.

a_rows_sample.anchor: A senior authority can issue an incorrect factual statement. Authority != Truth. Authority determines what is binding, not necessarily what is factually true
a_rows_sample.statement: States the crucial distinction that authority determines bindingness, not truth.

a_rows_sample.anchor: TruthStatus and BindingStatus. TruthStatus=Unknown while BindingStatus=Mandatory. A governance rule may be mandatory even while its underlying assumptions remain uncertain
a_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes separate truth-status and binding-status dimensions for a claim.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Architecture Board mandates All production changes require approval. Even if someone argues that approval provides little technical value, the rule remains binding ... KnowledgeOS should represent Binding=True. It should not silently override the rule based on an optimization calculation
a_rows_sample.statement: Worked governance-mandate example warning against silently overriding binding rules via optimization.

b_rows_sample.anchor: An enterprise does not have only one uncertainty ... U_1,...,U_n ... resources are finite ... How should KnowledgeOS allocate limited epistemic resources across competing uncertainties and decisions?
b_rows_sample.statement: Generalizes NextBestEpistemicAction (single decision) to organization-wide resource allocation across many competing uncertainties.

b_rows_sample.anchor: mathcal U={u_1,...,u_n} unresolved knowledge problems ... mathcal R={r_1,...,r_m} available resources ... Allocate(mathcal R,mathcal U) to maximize decision quality
b_rows_sample.statement: Formally defines the central resource-allocation problem Allocate(R,U).

b_rows_sample.anchor: A conventional backlog might assign Priority=High/Medium/Low. That is insufficient ... Cost(U_1)=1 and Cost(U_2)=100. Their resource efficiency differs dramatically
b_rows_sample.statement: Rejects simple High/Medium/Low prioritization as insufficient once cost varies dramatically.

b_rows_sample.anchor: EU(u) as the expected improvement in decision quality resulting from resolving uncertainty u ... Efficiency(u)=EU(u)/Cost(u). But we need more dimensions
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines epistemic utility and a first cost-efficiency ratio, noting it is insufficient alone.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Priority(u)=f(Risk,DecisionImpact,VOI,Urgency,Dependency,Freshness,Cost). We should resist collapsing these prematurely into one scalar
b_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes a multi-dimensional priority function and warns against premature scalar collapse.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Priority=0.83. What does that mean? It hides why the item matters ... Score != Explanation. KnowledgeOS should preserve the underlying vector
b_rows_sample.statement: States a single priority score hides explanatory information, giving the principle Score != Explanation.

b_rows_sample.anchor: P(u)=(Impact,Risk,VOI,Urgency,Dependency,Freshness,Cost,Authority) ... Only at the optimization boundary may we derive a ranking
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines the epistemic priority vector as the preserved, informative representation, deferring scalar ranking to the optimization boundary.

b_rows_sample.anchor: C(d) in {Low,Medium,High,Critical}. This is domain/governance information. KnowledgeOS should not decide what Critical means
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines decision criticality as domain/governance-owned information, not KnowledgeOS-decided.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Impact(u,d) ... unknown backup restorability may have Impact(u_1,d_migration)=High
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines uncertainty impact on a specific decision, worked with a backup-restorability example.

b_rows_sample.anchor: u_1 -> A -> M -> D_1,D_2,D_3 ... u_1 influences several decisions. This gives Centrality(u_1) high value
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines dependency centrality of an uncertainty influencing multiple decisions.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Degree(u), Betweenness(u), Reachability(u) ... graph-theoretic indicators. But they are not automatically epistemic importance. A highly connected irrelevant node can still be irrelevant
b_rows_sample.statement: Warns that raw graph-theoretic centrality measures are not automatically epistemic importance.

b_rows_sample.anchor: DWC(u) = sum_d Criticality(d)*Impact(u,d). This is a conceptual formulation
b_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes decision-weighted centrality combining decision criticality and per-decision impact.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Urgency(u,t) ... Deadline(d)-t may approach zero. Then the value of resolving u can increase sharply
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines urgency as a time-dependent factor that can sharply increase resolution value near a deadline.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Freshness(u,t) ... InfrastructureState decays quickly ... ArchitecturalPrinciple decays slowly. freshness is domain-specific
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines knowledge freshness as domain-specific, contrasting fast-decaying infrastructure state with slow-decaying architectural principles.

b_rows_sample.anchor: HL(u) as the characteristic time over which knowledge becomes stale ... useful for scheduling revalidation
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines a conceptual knowledge half-life for scheduling revalidation.

b_rows_sample.anchor: EpistemicDebt is accumulated unresolved uncertainty that can impair future decisions ... undocumented infrastructure; stale architecture decisions; unverified assumptions; unresolved conflicting requirements; missing provenance
b_rows_sample.statement: Introduces Epistemic Debt as accumulated unresolved uncertainty impairing future decisions, with five worked examples.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Technical debt: ShortTermSpeed->FutureCost. Epistemic debt: UnresolvedUncertainty->FutureDecisionRisk. EpistemicDebt=DeferredKnowledgeWork with future decision consequences
b_rows_sample.statement: Analogizes epistemic debt to technical debt and formalizes it as deferred knowledge work with future decision consequences.

b_rows_sample.anchor: D_E(t+1)=D_E(t)+NewUncertainty-ResolvedUncertainty+Staleness. This is conceptual rather than a universal accounting equation
b_rows_sample.statement: Proposes a conceptual debt-accumulation recurrence, explicitly not a universal accounting equation.

b_rows_sample.anchor: U_1 remains unresolved. It becomes an assumption in M_1 ... an assumption in D_1. The original uncertainty now propagates. Unresolved uncertainty can compound
b_rows_sample.statement: States unresolved uncertainty can compound as it becomes embedded as an assumption in downstream models and decisions.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Blocker(u) ... u -> D_1,D_2,D_3,D_4, then resolving u may unlock substantial work. This is an epistemic bottleneck
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines an epistemic bottleneck as an uncertainty blocking many downstream activities.

a_rows_sample.statement: Confirms that defining closure over the boundary B rather than the value repairs D-0 (contradiction-invisible-to-Zero) in 6 of 6 tested cases under all three contradiction models, explicitly correcting Experiment G's earlier claim that the contradiction-codomain choice and the closure question could not be separated.

a_rows_sample.anchor: the four Zero readings are not total over the value domain ... Any value outside {top,bot,U} is invisible to every reading, and every reading CLOSES on it. ... a contradictory state is declared epistemically closed.
a_rows_sample.statement: D-0: re-running Phase D under three-valued/four-valued/delegated contradiction models produces identical Zero readings across all seven suite cases, but the identical result is itself a defect -- none of strict/weak/reasoned/Kleene can see any value outside {top,bot,U}, so a contradictory state closes under every reading.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Boundary closure is identical across all three contradiction models -- CONFIRMED. Choosing among three-valued / four-valued / delegated is unnecessary for closure, which removes a blocker Experiment G had declared load-bearing.
a_rows_sample.statement: Re-confirms with the typed vocabulary (who-can-act derived from type, not free text) that boundary-based Zero closure is invariant across all three contradiction models, reconfirming Artifact I's earlier finding at higher rigor.

a_rows_sample.anchor: D-0's agreement was attributed to the readings testing only F and U. True but incomplete. The models are separable in isolation — one unrelated U anywhere in the state masks the difference completely, in any bucket.
a_rows_sample.statement: Corrects and sharpens D-0's earlier finding: the models ARE separable in isolation, but one unrelated U anywhere in the epistemic state masks the difference completely in any bucket, because Zero_weak/Zero_kleene are existential quantifiers that absorb at U; with 5 of 8 Sat_c classes non-executable, this masking saturation is the normal regime, not an edge case -- the sixth instance of the recurring projection-vs-structure diagnosis, and the first found in the readings rather than a value or metric.

Validates the Zero Lens claim UNKNOWN≠ABSENT with a concrete formal witness: if Contr(p) and NoAssessment(p) both map to U, the representation has collapsed two semantically distinct situations, and this Representation_Collapse(Contr,Unknown) is now measurable.

Gives the precise masking-mechanism table: models are separable (2 distinct reading profiles) when zero other requirements are at U, but become inseparable (1 profile) as soon as even one other requirement is at U, regardless of its bucket -- caused by Zero_weak/Zero_kleene being existential quantifiers over the state (absorbing at the first U encountered), which Zero_reasoned inherits through Zero_weak; since 5 of 8 Sat classes are non-executable, saturation is the normal regime, not the edge case, meaning the contradiction-model choice is unobservable in exactly the regime KnowledgeOS actually occupies.

a_rows_sample.anchor:
| `Contradiction ⇒ ¬Zero` | **FALSE** |
| `Zero_weak` on a contradictory state, under **A** and **B** | **closes** (`true`) |...> `[NEG]` **NEG-7. Contradiction does not merely fail to imply Zero — under both A and B a contradictory state CLOSES.**
a_rows_sample.statement: Tests Zero interaction directly rather than assuming it: Contradiction does NOT imply not-Zero (false), and under both A and B, Zero_weak on a contradictory state actually closes (true) -- NEG-7, stronger than originally anticipated: contradiction doesn't merely fail to imply Zero, it actively produces closure. This reproduces D-0 in a new setting, confirming it is not an artifact of one model, and connects to KR-CONTR-MODELS' finding that the readings saturate.

a_rows_sample.anchor: > `[EXP]` **`Zero` cannot be defined before evaluation semantics are expressive enough to answer "`U` because *what*?"** The dependency is **`Sat → Zero`**, never the reverse.
a_rows_sample.statement: Retrospectively explains why Zero resisted definition: the old Zero(K,I,EC)⟺Δ=∅ was underspecified because Sat itself was -- when Sat(r)=U one must ask 'U because what?' since U_unobservable is epistemically different from U_not-assessed; the dependency is Sat->Zero, never the reverse, confirmed from two independent directions (this experiment's §8, and KR-CONTR-MODELS §6's saturation finding).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Q1 — what problem was the model created to solve? ... "this model says what decisions an Engineer resolves with them"
a_rows_sample.statement: The Engineering Decision Model was created because standards say what the rules are, while the model says what decisions an engineer resolves with them: rules existed but the decisions they answer were unindexed. Its anti-problem: it is a decision INDEX, never a second rulebook (ARB, 2026-07-11) — created to prevent duplicated authority, not to add a layer. Its birth act included a vocabulary correction (2026-07-11): a DDD Domain Service is executable, a decision is a specification. Its adoption bar: one real engineering cycle must show consistent resolution through the model; it is DRAFT until earned.

Verdict: the ontology supplies the vocabulary the catalog's procedures presuppose; the catalog supplies the purpose the ontology elements must serve — they interlock, neither extends the other.

a_rows_sample.statement: A second decision model would violate ubiquitous language three times over: (1) the model's charter states it is 'a decision INDEX, never a second rulebook' — a v2 is exactly what it exists to prevent; (2) I-5, lint-enforced, requires one authoritative artifact per topic+context, so a second model is a literal violation; (3) ES-005.4 requires one rule -> one home. A competing 'KnowledgeOS Decision Model' would have been the UL violation and was not created; the Discovery and Validation passes are readings of the one model, not rivals to it.

a_rows_sample.anchor: U-EDV-1 | Does the DA intend the anticipated PKS-class Knowledge Decision catalog (§5) to be the home of the knowledge-governance decisions this programme surfaced?
a_rows_sample.statement: U-EDV-1: does the Decision Authority intend the anticipated PKS-class Knowledge Decision catalog to be the home of the knowledge-governance decisions this programme surfaced — waits on the ARB, natural companion to D-8.

a_rows_sample.statement: U-EDV-2: the model's adoption test (one real cycle of conscious use) is unevenly met (U-DM-4, carried forward), waiting on EP-02 of the next real cycle.

a_rows_sample.anchor: DP-n as a distinct layer between principle and capability ... UNIQUE HYPOTHESIS — needs operational proof
a_rows_sample.statement: DP-n as a distinct architectural layer between principle and capability has no direct external counterpart found (policy-as-code practice is only adjacent); it remains a unique hypothesis requiring operational proof.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Canonical concept glossary — the 14 examined, plus 3 the corpus forces in
a_rows_sample.statement: A 17-row glossary assigns each term (KnowledgeOS, PKS, Engineering Knowledge, Engineering Capability, Engineering Method, Engineering Governance, Engineering Runtime, Runtime Adapter, Engineering Evidence, Engineering Ontology, Documentation Ontology L-A, Platform Ontology L-B, Product Ontology L-C, Knowledge Graph, Engineering Kernel, Knowledge Space, Design Policy DP-n, Execution Asset AST-nnn) one meaning, owner, protected invariant, place, and verdict (KEEP/REJECTED-MERGED/SPLIT/CANDIDATE). a_rows_sample.anchor: RESULT: THE MODEL DOES NOT SURVIVE INTACT. One claim FALSIFIED · two WEAKENED · two SURVIVED · two unchanged
a_rows_sample.statement: Overall falsification result: of the domain model's claims, one is falsified, two weakened, two survived, two unchanged; the strongest claim in the model (D-2) was among those weakened, by evidence the model itself had cited. Method: every test executed against artifacts, not reasoned from the model, using the repository's own instruments (Round47-OP's nine admissible justifications, the R16 Workbook Strong/Medium/Weak scale); four falsifiers were sought, three landed.

a_rows_sample.anchor: W-1 · D-2's "own decision series" is a shared authority — two of four grounds fall
a_rows_sample.statement: D-2's claim of 'its own decision series, ADR-M distinct from ADR-AIP' is weakened: Round39-D6's header states decision authority for all ADRs is 'sponsor + ARB' and amendment requires sponsor+ARB approval, so ADR-M is a scoping device under a shared authority, not a separate authority. Its claim of 'independent evolution' is falsified: Round39-D6 states the ADRs 'were authored together on 2026-06-25' — a series written in one sitting evidences independent subject, never independent evolution over time. This matches the ARB Chair's named falsifier 'ADR separation is historical rather than semantic' — half true: separation is real in subject, absent in time.

a_rows_sample.anchor: S-1 · D-2 survives on a ground I had not weighted — an explicit mutual scope exclusion
a_rows_sample.statement: D-2 survives on a new ground: Round39-D6's verbatim rule 'Governance discoveries (constitutional/capability) MUST NOT appear here. No DDD concepts here' is a deliberately maintained boundary (not an accident of filing), bidirectional in effect (ADR-M excludes governance, ADR-AIP carries no methodology rules), and survives the shared-authority finding since a shared authority that forbids itself from mixing two subjects is evidence FOR two models, not against. D-2 remains a boundary, but on subject exclusion, not on decision-series separation or independent evolution.

a_rows_sample.anchor: S-3 · D-1 survives every falsifier
a_rows_sample.statement: D-1 survives every falsifier sought: no multiple owners of the same concept found (DA/ARB throughout), no changes that fail to co-occur (ES set moves under STANDARDS_INDEX), no forced co-evolution with a product (ratification and freeze are product-independent), no absent invariants (append-only rulings, R-46).

a_rows_sample.anchor: U-1 | Was Round39-MC adopted by sponsor authority BECAUSE D-2 is independent, or DESPITE it being part of D-1?
a_rows_sample.statement: U-1: was Round39-MC adopted because D-2 is independent, or despite it being part of D-1 — the artifacts record the act but never the reason; only the sponsor and ARB know, and the model's validity turns on it.

a_rows_sample.anchor: U-4 | Is Round39-D6's scope exclusion still enforced, or was it stated once?
a_rows_sample.statement: U-4: is Round39-D6's scope exclusion still enforced or was it stated once — stated 2026-06-25, no subsequent enforcement event found.

a_rows_sample.anchor: U-6 | Does D-1 authorize D-2, or are they peers?
a_rows_sample.statement: U-6: does D-1 authorize D-2, or are they peers — carried forward, now sharper: shared ARB suggests peers-under-one-authority, not hierarchy.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Confidence — R16 Workbook scale, scored independently ... falsified ≠ unevidenced
a_rows_sample.statement: Per-domain confidence after falsification (R16 Strong/Medium/Weak scale): D-1 Strong->STRONG; D-2 Strong->MEDIUM; D-3 Strong->WEAK; D-6a (Evidence Protocol) new->MEDIUM; D-6b (Product Evidence) new->STRONG; D-5 (Engineering Capability, not a context) Medium->MEDIUM (unchanged, H-CAT-1 stands); D-4 (Workflow, rejected) ->STRONG as a rejection; D-7 (PKS, a context type) new->WEAK. Distinction drawn: falsified is worse than unevidenced — D-3 and D-7 carry contradicting evidence (falsified); D-6a carries no evidence (unevidenced).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Recommendation — per domain ... The model as a whole | REVISE, then re-test ... NOT canonical
a_rows_sample.statement: Per-domain recommendations: D-1 ACCEPT; D-2 REVISE (restate the boundary on the one surviving ground, Round39-D6's scope exclusion; delete 'own decision series' and 'independent evolution' as grounds); D-3 DEFER (untestable at n=1, revisit when a second runtime adapter exists); D-6a DEFER, D-6b ACCEPT; D-5 ACCEPT the demotion (do not promote until ARB overturns H-CAT-1 on evidence); D-4 ACCEPT the rejection; D-7 REVISE (restate as an observation of one instance, record PKS-as-projection as falsified). Overall the model as a whole: REVISE then re-test, NOT canonical — 2 of 8 accept, 3 revise, 2 defer, 1 accept-as-rejection.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Platform Lifecycle (Idea→Knowledge→PKS→Implementation→Evidence→Evolution) ... B-1 correction: software→evidence OBSERVED · back-edge n≈3 informal / ≈2 formal · KnowledgeOS→PKS n=0 · Genesis has NO route
b_rows_sample.statement: The platform lifecycle is graded link-by-link: software-to-evidence is observed; the back-edge is n≈3 informal / ≈2 formal; KnowledgeOS-to-PKS generation is n=0; and the Genesis stage has no route at all. Individual grades are confirmed; the loop as a whole remains a hypothesis.

b_rows_sample.anchor: PKS Boundary — P1 method/binding/evidence ... I-7 (PKS never contains reusable method — stated AND breached)
b_rows_sample.statement: P1 defines PKS content as method/binding/evidence (cognate of Round38C-04); I-7 states a PKS never contains reusable method, yet this rule is both stated and breached in the current corpus. PKS contains artifacts; a projection claim is falsified for existing artifacts (authored, ARB-endorsed 9.9/10). The boundary rule is confirmed; the breach remains open, routed to D-8.

b_rows_sample.anchor: What does not survive — registers' contents · all records/reports · every PKS instance · Round-corpus case law · governed-registers.yaml · .claude/settings.json · election domain knowledge
b_rows_sample.statement: Elements that do NOT survive removal of the single product: registers' contents, all records/reports, every PKS instance, Round-corpus case law, governed-registers.yaml, .claude/settings.json, and election domain knowledge.

b_rows_sample.anchor: R-6 | KnowledgeOS —creates→ PKS | UNIQUE — the loop's first edge is unproven inside and outside
b_rows_sample.statement: Relationship R-6: KnowledgeOS creates PKS. External support: scaffolding/generators (Spring Initializr-class) are implementation guidance only; context-engineering platforms that auto-assemble context are adjacent. Challenge: no external instance of generating a governed knowledge space is found; internally n=0. Confidence: UNIQUE — the loop's first edge is unproven both inside and outside the corpus.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Corrections applied to the concept matrix — PKS = Context Engineering softened
b_rows_sample.statement: Three corrections applied to the (external) concept matrix: (1) 'PKS = Context Engineering' softened to 'PKS addresses the same problem space as context engineering and extends it with governance, lifecycle, authority and engineering semantics' — not an identity claim, since the governed form has no demonstrated external instance; (2) Jansen & Bosch elevated to primary validation, since it validates the PROBLEM (knowledge vaporizes), and problem validation outranks solution fashion (Gartner-era context engineering); (3) the admission rule adopted as a standing header rule on both matrices.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The relationship pass sharpens the concept pass's conclusion: the platform's EDGES are almost all standard engineering — what is uniquely unproven is ONE edge (creates → PKS) and ONE layer name (DP-n)
b_rows_sample.statement: Aggregate result: externally supported (>=HIGH) relationships are R-3, R-4, R-5, R-8, R-10, and R-2's separation; medium relationships are R-1, R-7, R-9; the unique, operationally-unproven items are R-6 (creates->PKS) and DP-n as a named layer. The distinctive bet of KnowledgeOS is now precisely locatable as R-6; everything else is either validated or a naming choice, and R-6 is exactly what the charter's gated stages and the docket's doors already refuse to assume.

b_rows_sample.anchor: REV 2 — R-6 BROADENED per review: the bet is the INTEGRATION, not one edge
b_rows_sample.statement: Challenge accepted: 'KnowledgeOS is not merely a generator. It is the platform that governs the ENTIRE PKS lifecycle.' R-6 is restated as a composite chain: KnowledgeOS discovers/models/governs/generates/evolves PKS, guides PRODUCT ENGINEERING (the actor — work, not magic), which engineers software, collects evidence, and improves KnowledgeOS. The actor (product engineering) was already implicit in the work-execution progressions (P-7/P-8) and 'the producing track' as records-owner, but the composite chain had omitted it.

b_rows_sample.anchor: PKS — governed, machine-readable context for AI ... "context engineering" 2025–26
b_rows_sample.statement: PKS as governed, machine-readable AI context converges with industry 'context engineering' (Gartner July 2025: 'context engineering is in, prompt engineering is out', predicted in 80% of AI tools by 2028); enterprise practice defines governed, machine-readable context any AI agent can use reliably. Challenge: the field is platform-vendor-led, young, terminology unstable. Confidence: HIGH for the need; the governance framing (authority, lifecycle, bindings) remains rarer and partially ours.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The enforcement finding (governed context + advisory capabilities) ... 86% of enterprises are assembling rich, semantically grounded context — and handing it over with no governance
b_rows_sample.statement: The industry-wide finding that 86% of enterprises assemble rich context but hand it over with no governance over agent actions, and 89% say governance is critical while ~50% have it, is convergent with this platform's own governed-context-plus-advisory-capabilities gap. Confidence: HIGH.

b_rows_sample.anchor: KnowledgeOS→PKS generation (n=0) ... UNIQUE HYPOTHESIS — operational proof only
b_rows_sample.statement: KnowledgeOS generating a PKS (n=0) has only adjacent external support (context-engineering platforms generate context from metadata, not the same as generating a governed PKS); it remains a unique hypothesis needing operational proof only.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Canonical concept glossary — the 14 examined, plus 3 the corpus forces in
b_rows_sample.statement: A 17-row glossary assigns each term (KnowledgeOS, PKS, Engineering Knowledge, Engineering Capability, Engineering Method, Engineering Governance, Engineering Runtime, Runtime Adapter, Engineering Evidence, Engineering Ontology, Documentation Ontology L-A, Platform Ontology L-B, Product Ontology L-C, Knowledge Graph, Engineering Kernel, Knowledge Space, Design Policy DP-n, Execution Asset AST-nnn) one meaning, owner, protected invariant, place, and verdict (KEEP/REJECTED-MERGED/SPLIT/CANDIDATE). Success criterion: every major engineering term gets one meaning, one owner, one place.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Concept relationships — the reviewer's example chain, validated ... KnowledgeOS creates PKS contains Engineering Knowledge organized by Ontology used by Capabilities executed through Runtime produces Evidence improves KnowledgeOS
b_rows_sample.statement: The proposed chain is validated edge by edge: 'KnowledgeOS creates PKS' is a hypothesis (n=0, every PKS is authored by a person); 'PKS contains Engineering Knowledge' is WRONG, violating I-7 (a PKS contains product knowledge and bindings; reusable method must not live in it — the current breach is the exception that proves the rule); 'knowledge organized by Ontology' holds with the precision that L-A organizes artifacts/carriers, not knowledge itself (I-1); 'used by Capabilities' holds (capabilities may read across space boundaries, never own — H-1); 'Capabilities executed through Runtime' is imprecise (capabilities are advisory scripts invoked on demand; the runtime executes Execution Assets/ASTs; 41 enforced controls live runtime-side while every capability is advisory — the drawn edge hides this finding); 'Runtime produces Evidence' should attribute production to WORK (P-7/P-8), the runtime only hosts the work; 'Evidence improves KnowledgeOS' is only partly true (n≈3 informal, B-1's fact).

b_rows_sample.anchor: Two corrections to the Addendum's own positioning ... "KnowledgeOS is a Core Domain" ... Contradicts a DA ruling
b_rows_sample.statement: Two corrections to an Addendum's positioning: (1) 'KnowledgeOS is a Core Domain' contradicts AIP-14/DA ruling 2026-07-27 that the Election System is the Core Domain and the platform is a Supporting Subdomain; the Reference Model records only the conditional (engineering knowledge would be Core Domain if the gate opened, and it has not). (2) 'PKS is a generated projection' was falsified last round: existing PKS artifacts carry Status: ACCEPTED WITH REFINEMENTS, a Commission, and ARB endorsement 9.9/10 — they are authored, not derived.

b_rows_sample.anchor: W-3 · "PKS is a projection" — FALSIFIED for every existing PKS artifact
b_rows_sample.statement: The claim 'PKS is a projection' is falsified for every existing PKS artifact: examined fields (Authority: Generated, human-asserted; Status: ACCEPTED WITH REFINEMENTS; a Disposition History with ARB reviewer endorsement 9.9/10; a Commission) are incompatible with a projection, which would carry authority:derived (machine-checkable), no acceptance (regenerated, not accepted), a source and regeneration command, and no Commission. A mechanical grep for authority:derived|generated across docs/pks, docs/knowledgeos, docs/implementation returns 10 files, every one a prose mention of the vocabulary, not an application of it — those paths sit outside knowledge-schema.yaml's declared scope.include. This sharpens a prior Ontology Classification finding ('blocked in practice') to stronger: existing PKS artifacts are positively authoritative — authored, commissioned, reviewed, disposed, and accepted — incompatible with 'derived'.

b_rows_sample.anchor: W-4 · D-7 "Context Type" was inferred from a single instance
b_rows_sample.statement: D-7's 'Context Type' claim (one PKS instance per product) was inferred from a single instance (PublicDigit's), with zero instances generated from the type; 'one instance per product' is an observation of one case restated as a rule — a type never instantiated is a description, not a discovered construct.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Confidence — R16 Workbook scale, scored independently ... falsified ≠ unevidenced
b_rows_sample.statement: Per-domain confidence after falsification (R16 Strong/Medium/Weak scale): D-1 Strong->STRONG; D-2 Strong->MEDIUM; D-3 Strong->WEAK; D-6a (Evidence Protocol) new->MEDIUM; D-6b (Product Evidence) new->STRONG; D-5 (Engineering Capability, not a context) Medium->MEDIUM (unchanged, H-CAT-1 stands); D-4 (Workflow, rejected) ->STRONG as a rejection; D-7 (PKS, a context type) new->WEAK. Distinction drawn: falsified is worse than unevidenced — D-3 and D-7 carry contradicting evidence (falsified); D-6a carries no evidence (unevidenced).

b_rows_sample.anchor: 2. CANDIDATE — supported by evidence, awaiting ruling or more evidence (K-1..K-15)
b_rows_sample.statement: Fifteen candidate concerns, each citing its supporting commission and what it waits on: K-1 dimensional-with-archetypes meta-model; K-2 the archetype set (strong: DOMAIN/PROCESS/CAPABILITY/KNOWLEDGE/ARTIFACT/RUNTIME ASSET/PROJECTION; weaker: CONTAINER; weakest: PURPOSE); K-3 the four partial orders (authority, production, realization, containment); K-4 11 invariant relationships vs 8 implementation choices; K-5 DP-n as capability anchor; K-6 Knowledge Space = declared boundary+owner+constitution; K-7 authority = provenance x standing, four progression kinds; K-8 the strategic domain set PD-1/2/3/5; K-9 viewpoints as presentation; K-10 decision-readiness as the platform's product; K-11 FREEZE/RETIRE as insufficiency evidence; K-12 PKS extends context-engineering with governance; K-13 the canon-track reference artifacts themselves; K-14 the mission is enacted via 8 artifacts; K-15 ownership splits (candidate-unowned=ladder working, operating-unowned=defect, sole instance Runtime Adapter).

b_rows_sample.anchor: 3. HYPOTHESIS — plausible, insufficient evidence (H-1..H-9)
b_rows_sample.statement: Nine hypotheses with evidence state: H-1 the space map is the platform's real ownership/context map (n=1, downgraded); H-2 GOVERNANCE as a fifth viewpoint (asset found, framing undecided); H-3 PURPOSE more fundamental than CONTAINER (n=0); H-4 KnowledgeOS as a 'Knowledge Architecture Platform' (n=1); H-5 'generates -> PKS', the loop's head edge and the platform's distinctive bet (n=0 inside and outside); H-6 capability may read across a space boundary, never own (n=1 capability); H-7 space nesting (unevidenced); H-8 DOMAIN's decision-silence is dormant not permanent (untestable at n=1); H-9 EVIDENCE-STATUS/OPERATIONAL-STATE as meta-model dimensions (proposed, undocketed).

b_rows_sample.anchor: 5. REJECTED — falsified, with the falsifying pass cited (R-1..R-12)
b_rows_sample.statement: Twelve rejected/falsified claims listed with falsifying pass: R-1 the flat A-G category list as a meta-model; R-2 Governance/Product as kinds, Knowledge Asset as one thing; R-3 Domains own Capabilities; R-4 the single-stack hierarchy (Purpose->...->Artifact); R-5 KnowledgeOS is the Core Domain/the real product; R-6 the MVK 15-file extraction boundary; R-7 'two missions'/'mission layer vacant'/the INTENDED evidence grade; R-8 '0 of 11 responsibilities enforcing'; R-9 '0 traversals' of the evidence back-edge as a generalization; R-10 I-4 as falsified, and LG-1; R-11 a second Engineering Decision Model; R-12 'one owner => one context' as stated.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The six concepts ... MISSION · ENGINEERING KNOWLEDGE · ENGINEERING CAPABILITY · ENGINEERING ARTIFACT · PRODUCT KNOWLEDGE SPACE · PRODUCT
b_rows_sample.statement: Six concepts defined by responsibility/lifecycle/owner/dependencies, none defined by a folder: MISSION (why the platform exists; enacted->candidate->ratified, currently enacted-unratified; owner: sponsor; depends on nothing, the root); ENGINEERING KNOWLEDGE (rules/methods/decisions that transfer between products; ES-006.1 ladder; owner DA for policy, sponsor+ARB for method; depends on MISSION); ENGINEERING CAPABILITY (protect exactly one invariant; observed->...->promoted; shape frozen under PGP-01..05; depends on MISSION+KNOWLEDGE); ENGINEERING ARTIFACT (carry knowledge in a representation, never the knowledge itself; statuses.yaml 8 states lint-enforced; owner field; depends on KNOWLEDGE); PRODUCT KNOWLEDGE SPACE (hold one product's concepts/language/contexts/bindings; authored today, generated as hypothesis n=0; owner product team; depends on KNOWLEDGE method + PRODUCT subject); PRODUCT (deliver business value; own delivery lifecycle; owner product team; depends on PKS + CAPABILITY).

group_evidence.why_grouped: labels co-occur in the same contribution's labels[] 5 separate times across the corpus

a_rows_sample.anchor: A decision-ready state is a Knowledge State that is sufficiently complete, coherent, and adequate for the current purpose, such that the Knower can make an informed decision with acceptable confidence.
a_rows_sample.statement: Original Q23 definition: a decision-ready state is a Knowledge State sufficiently complete, coherent and adequate for the current purpose, such that the Knower can make an informed decision with acceptable confidence. Boxed: Decision-Ready ≠ Complete; Decision-Ready = Sufficient for Purpose; Stop Condition = f(Sufficiency, Cost, Urgency, Risk, Policy).

a_rows_sample.anchor: ShouldStop(S_t, P_t, C_t, Policy_t) \in \{\text{True}, \text{False}\}
a_rows_sample.statement: The Stop Condition Framework: ShouldStop(S_t,P_t,C_t,Policy_t) is a boolean function of six criteria (Sufficiency S_u, Diminishing Returns D_r, Time/Cost T_c, Urgency U_r, Risk R_i, Policy P_o), combined as ShouldStop = Sufficient(S_t,P_t) ∨ BudgetExhausted(S_t,T_c) ∨ UrgencyThreshold(S_t,U_r) ∨ PolicyStop(S_t,P_o).

type_signature.domain: system state x purpose x context x policy

a_rows_sample.anchor: Sufficient(S_t, P_t) = \text{KnowledgeSufficient}(K_t, I^K_t) \land \text{UnderstandingSufficient}(U_t, I^U_t) \land \text{DomainSufficient}(X_t, I^D_t)
a_rows_sample.statement: Sufficiency is decomposed into Knowledge, Understanding and Domain sufficiency: Knowledge sufficient requires all ideal dimensions represented (D_I ⊆ D_Kt), all critical values known, all critical epistemic states meeting a threshold Σ_I, all critical relationships represented, and coherence maintained. Understanding sufficient requires conceptual understanding, implications understanding, uncertainty and conflict-resolution each meeting thresholds. Domain sufficient requires reality meeting constraints (X_t ⊨ C_I) and performance meeting a threshold.

a_rows_sample.anchor: \text{DiminishingReturns}(S_t) = \text{ExpectedValue}(\text{NextInvestigation}) < \text{Cost}(\text{NextInvestigation})
a_rows_sample.statement: Diminishing returns occur when the expected value of the next investigation step is less than its cost; ExpectedValue(d) = Impact(d) x Probability(d is actionable) x Severity(d); Cost(d) = Time(d) + Effort(d) + Resources(d).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Readiness = w_K \cdot K_c + w_U \cdot U_d + w_C \cdot C_r + w_{U_l} \cdot (1 - U_l) + w_D \cdot D_i + w_R \cdot R_t
a_rows_sample.statement: Original Readiness function: a weighted scalar in [0,1] over six factors (Knowledge Completeness K_c, Understanding Depth U_d, Conflict Resolution C_r, Uncertainty Level U_l, Decision Impact D_i, Risk Tolerance R_t); DecisionReady(S_t,P_t) iff Readiness(S_t,P_t) >= Threshold(P_t).

a_rows_sample.anchor: 8. The Arjuna Example: Stop Decision
a_rows_sample.statement: Walkthrough of Arjuna's decision states S0 (insufficient knowledge/understanding/domain, continue), S1 (partially sufficient after observation, continue), S2 (sufficient after moral resolution, STOP and present decision-ready state); stop criteria table shows sufficiency, diminishing returns, urgency and risk all favoring Stop.

a_rows_sample.anchor: DecisionReady \neq ShouldStop
a_rows_sample.statement: Correction to Q23: the original equation ShouldStop = Sufficient ∨ BudgetExhausted ∨ UrgencyThreshold ∨ PolicyStop is 'too permissive' because it implies exhausting budget or reaching urgency can make a state decision-ready, which is not epistemically correct. Fundamental distinction established: DecisionReady ≠ ShouldStop, and a forced stop does not mean the system is decision-ready (Stop ⇏ DecisionReady). Three outcomes of investigation identified: Decision-Ready→STOP, Not Ready→Continue, Not Ready→Forced Stop.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Unknown \neq Not\ Decision\ Ready
a_rows_sample.statement: Correction: the requirement that all critical dimension values be 'known' is too strong — some values can remain unknown while the decision is still valid if the uncertainty is decision-irrelevant (example: not knowing whether a probability is 17% or 18% when both lead to the same decision). Replaces with DecisionRelevantUncertainty(S_t,D) ≤ T_D, a policy-defined tolerance T_D.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Case C — Decision-critical unresolved conflict
a_rows_sample.statement: Refines 'conflicts resolved or accepted' into three ConflictStatus cases: (A) Resolved; (B) Accepted as unresolved (Knower explicitly accepts the uncertainty/conflict); (C) Active and decision-critical unresolved conflict, in which case DecisionReady = False. 'Accepted' therefore cannot automatically mean readiness.

a_rows_sample.anchor:
Knowledge = 95%
Understanding = 95%
Conflict Resolution = 95%
Critical unresolved safety conflict = YES
a_rows_sample.statement: The weighted-average Readiness score assumes all dimensions are compensable: a hypothetical case with 95% knowledge/understanding/conflict-resolution but an unresolved critical safety conflict could still average to Readiness=0.9 and incorrectly declare the state decision-ready. Presented as the counterexample motivating replacement of the scalar formula.

a_rows_sample.anchor: DecisionReady = \bigwedge_i G_i \land SoftCriteriaSatisfied
a_rows_sample.statement: Replaces the compensable weighted scalar with a hard-gates-plus-soft-indicators architecture: non-negotiable hard constraints G_1..G_n (e.g. G1=Coherent(K_t), G2=NoDecisionCriticalConflict, G3=CriticalEvidenceSatisfied, G4=CriticalDimensionsSatisfied) must all hold, DecisionReady = (⋀_i G_i) ∧ SoftCriteriaSatisfied. Readiness is redefined as a structured triple (HardGates, SoftIndicators, RemainingDeficiencies) rather than a scalar in [0,1]; a scalar R_score=f(SoftIndicators) may still be derived for UI purposes but must never override hard constraints. States the principle: 'Structured state is fundamental; scalar measurements are derived,' attributed as following from Q19/Q22.

a_rows_sample.anchor: EVSI = Expected\ Value\ of\ Information
a_rows_sample.statement: Corrects the diminishing-returns formula to account for decision impact via the Expected Value of Sample/Information (EVSI): EVSI(a) = E[decision quality after information] − decision quality now; continue investigation when expected decision benefit exceeds cost/risk. Flagged as an optional decision-theoretic mechanism, not a universal mathematical truth.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Status = ForcedStopNotReady
a_rows_sample.statement: Urgency must not produce false readiness: 'Not sufficient + Urgent = STOP' is operationally fine but must produce Status = ForcedStopNotReady, not DecisionReady = True.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Discrepancy \rightarrow Findings \rightarrow Resolution Opportunities \rightarrow Prioritization \rightarrow Investigation \rightarrow Decision Sufficiency \rightarrow Decision Posture
a_rows_sample.statement: Overall assessment gives the original Q23 scores Conceptual 8/10, Mathematical 6.5/10, DDD 7.5/10, expecting 9.5/9/9.5 after corrections. States the central architectural insight: KnowledgeOS does not decide when 'enough knowledge' exists in the abstract, but whether enough decision-relevant knowledge exists for this Knower, this purpose, this context, and this decision — giving a progression chain from Discrepancy through Findings, Resolution Opportunities, Prioritization, Investigation, Decision Sufficiency, to Decision Posture (Q19→Q22→Q23).

a_rows_sample.anchor: A decision-ready state exists before presentation.
a_rows_sample.statement: Corrected definition: 'A decision-ready state is an evaluated system state in which the knowledge relevant to a specific decision satisfies the applicable decision criteria. Presentation is the projection of that state into a form usable by the Knower.' Formalized as DecisionReady(S_t,D,P,C) followed by P_t = Present(DecisionReadyState, Knower, Format), preserving the Q23 distinction.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Resolution \neq \Delta=\emptyset
a_rows_sample.statement: Rejects the previous Arjuna example's claim 'After Moral Resolution -> Δ=∅' as a very important correction: even after normative resolution, uncertainty/risk/incomplete domain knowledge/emotional difficulty/consequences may remain, so Resolution ≠ Δ=∅; DecisionReady(Δ,P) may hold even though Δ≠∅. Generalized to abandon 'Δ=∅ ⇒ Success' entirely: DecisionReady=CriteriaSatisfied, not DecisionReady=NoRemainingGaps, so CompleteKnowledge is unnecessary for action — 'a very important property for a real engineering system'.

a_rows_sample.anchor: DecisionReady(S,C) \iff DecisionCriteria(S,C)
a_rows_sample.statement: Clarifies that 'DecisionReady does not require Δ=∅' remains architecturally correct but is the theory's own engineering inference, not a theorem Chapter 3 itself establishes: DecisionReady(S,C) ⟺ DecisionCriteria(S,C), not DecisionReady ⟺ Δ=∅ — a design principle derived from the case, not a claim about the text.

b_rows_sample.anchor: A decision-ready state is the Knowledge State presented to the Knower in a form that is comprehensible, actionable, and faithful to the underlying epistemic structure, enabling the Knower to make an informed decision.
b_rows_sample.statement: Original Q24 definition (later corrected): a decision-ready state IS the Knowledge State presented to the Knower in comprehensible, actionable, faithful form. Key boxed claims: Presentation ≠ Dump of Raw Data; Presentation = Structured, Epistemically Qualified, Purpose-Tailored View; Presentation must preserve the epistemic status of each assertion.

b_rows_sample.anchor: P_t = \text{Present}(K_t, I_t, U_t, \Delta_t, Q_t, C_t, N_t, \text{Format})
b_rows_sample.statement: The Presentation Function: Present maps (K,I,U,Δ,Q,C,N,F) to a presentation P_t; nine presentation components listed (State Summary, Key Findings, Gaps and Conflicts, Ideal Comparison, Risks and Implications, Recommendations, Epistemic Status, Provenance, History); five presentation layers (Executive Summary, Epistemic State, Comparison with Ideal, Risks and Implications, Recommendations), each with purpose/content/format.

b_rows_sample.statement: Presentation formats illustrated with the Arjuna case: Natural Language Summary, Structured View (assertion/status/evidence/conflict table), Visual View (graph with a conflict warning), and Comparative View (dimension/current/ideal/gap table); repeated in section 8 as 'The Arjuna Example: Presentation' with an executive summary, epistemic state view and comparative view.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Q(P_t) = w_F \cdot \text{Fidelity} + w_C \cdot \text{Comprehensibility} + w_A \cdot \text{Actionability} + w_M \cdot \text{Completeness}
b_rows_sample.statement: Original presentation quality criteria (Fidelity, Comprehensibility, Actionability, Completeness, each in [0,1]) combined into a single weighted Presentation Quality Score Q(P_t); four original invariants: Presentation ≠ Raw Data; must preserve epistemic status; must be comprehensible; must be actionable.

b_rows_sample.anchor: This is the complete mathematical specification of KnowledgeOS.
b_rows_sample.statement: Original document's closing claim, later retracted: a 24-item list of the 'complete KnowledgeOS model' (Observation, Dimension, Proposition, Assertion, Evidence, Epistemic State, Knowledge State, Understanding State, Domain State, Ideal State, Coherence, Conflict, Gap, Distance, Zero/Lord/Sārathi Lens, Transition, History, Complete System State, Discrepancy, Prioritization, Decision-Ready State, Presentation) is declared 'the complete mathematical specification of KnowledgeOS'.

b_rows_sample.anchor: S_t \xrightarrow{\text{evaluate}} D_t \xrightarrow{\text{project}} P_t
b_rows_sample.statement: Fundamental correction: presentation must not become part of the epistemic state itself; it is a projection for a Knower/purpose/decision/format. Pipeline corrected to S_t --evaluate--> D_t --project--> P_t, where S_t is the complete internal state, D_t the decision-ready assessment/posture, P_t the human-facing projection. Establishes P_t ≠ D_t and P_t ≠ S_t: presentation is a view/projection, not another knowledge object.

b_rows_sample.anchor: A decision-ready state exists before presentation.
b_rows_sample.statement: Corrected definition: 'A decision-ready state is an evaluated system state in which the knowledge relevant to a specific decision satisfies the applicable decision criteria. Presentation is the projection of that state into a form usable by the Knower.' Formalized as DecisionReady(S_t,D,P,C) followed by P_t = Present(DecisionReadyState, Knower, Format), preserving the Q23 distinction.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Presentation = Epistemically\ Qualified\ Projection
b_rows_sample.statement: Deeper DDD point: Present() must not be understood as 'turn database objects into UI' but as a semantic projection that decides what is relevant, critical, uncertain, conflicting, missing, evidenced, recommendation-vs-fact, and inference-vs-observation. Presentation = Epistemically Qualified Projection.

b_rows_sample.anchor: \Pi_{N,D,P,C,F}
b_rows_sample.statement: New concept: Presentation Projection Π_{N,D,P,C,F} parameterized by Knower N, Decision D, Purpose P, Context C, Format F, giving P_t = Π_{N,D,P,C,F}(S_t). Enables two different Knowers to receive different presentations of the same underlying state without KnowledgeOS holding two different Knowledge States.

b_rows_sample.anchor: CriticalEpistemicDistinctions(S_t) \subseteq Preserved(P_t)
b_rows_sample.statement: Presentation is loss-aware: as a projection it may lose information but must not lose epistemically important distinctions — e.g. Observed/Reported/Inferred/Assumed must not all collapse into 'FACT', and Strong/Weak/No evidence must not all collapse into 'CONFIDENT'. Defines EpistemicFidelity(P_t,S_t) and requires CriticalEpistemicDistinctions(S_t) ⊆ Preserved(P_t) as one of the most important invariants of the presentation architecture.

b_rows_sample.anchor: ConfidenceIndicator = DerivedView(\Sigma)
b_rows_sample.statement: Recommends removing 'Confidence' (Very Strong/Strong/Moderate/Weak/None) as the primary presentation model because it risks collapsing the multidimensional epistemic state established in Q16 (Acquisition ≠ Support ≠ Uncertainty ≠ Validity). A table example shows presenting each claim's Acquisition/Support/Uncertainty/Validity separately; a UI may then derive a simplified indicator: ConfidenceIndicator = DerivedView(Σ), not Confidence = Σ.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Fidelity(P_t,S_t)=Required
b_rows_sample.statement: Rejects the original weighted Presentation Quality Score Q(P_t) as formal theory because it again permits compensation: a presentation could score 95% comprehensibility/actionability/completeness while misrepresenting one critical epistemic status, and still get a high score — unacceptable. Replaces with hard presentation invariants: Fidelity(P_t,S_t)=Required, CriticalEpistemicStatusPreserved(P_t,S_t), DecisionRelevantInformationPreserved(P_t,D); optional metrics may still assess quality afterward.

b_rows_sample.anchor: CompleteForDecision(P_t,D)
b_rows_sample.statement: Completeness should be formalized as decision-relative, CompleteForDecision(P_t,D), not generic Complete(P_t), since a presentation can deliberately omit decision-irrelevant information; expressed generally as Relevance = f(Knower, Purpose, Decision, Context).

b_rows_sample.statement: Keeps the five presentation layers but re-semanticizes them: Layer 1 Decision (what decision is supported), Layer 2 Evidence/Knowledge (what do we know), Layer 3 Epistemic qualification (how do we know it), Layer 4 Discrepancy/Risk (what remains uncertain/problematic), Layer 5 Guidance (what should the Knower consider next) — giving the progression Decision→Knowledge→Evidence→Discrepancy→Action.

b_rows_sample.anchor: CurrentState \neq History
b_rows_sample.statement: History should not be dumped into the main presentation but disclosed progressively: primary view answers 'what is the state now?', user can expand to 'how did we arrive here?'. CurrentState ≠ History, but History -> ExplanationOfCurrentState.

b_rows_sample.statement: Introduces three bounded responsibilities/contexts: KnowledgeOS Core (owns K,Σ,E,G,C,Δ,I,S), Epistemic Orchestration (owns Zero, Lord, Sārathi, Prioritization, Transition), and Presentation/Interaction (owns Projection, View, Format, Explanation, Interaction), with a layered diagram Core -> Epistemic Assessment -> Decision State -> Presentation Projection -> (Executive/Detailed/Graph views).

b_rows_sample.anchor: D_t = Evaluate(S_t,P,D,C,Policy)
b_rows_sample.statement: Revised mathematical model: D_t = Evaluate(S_t,P,D,C,Policy); P_t = Π(S_t,D_t,N,F); with P_t ≢ S_t and P_t ≢ D_t, and P_t defined as 'human-oriented projection of S_t under D_t'.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Presentation \neq RawData
b_rows_sample.statement: Nine new presentation invariants recommended to be frozen: Presentation ≠ RawData; Presentation ≠ KnowledgeState; Presentation ≠ Decision; Recommendation ≠ Fact; Candidate ≠ Knowledge; Presentation must preserve critical epistemic distinctions; Presentation must preserve provenance for decision-relevant claims; Presentation completeness is decision-relative; Presentation is a projection, not a mutation of the Knowledge State.

b_rows_sample.statement: Retracts the original document's closing claim that the 24-question model is 'the complete mathematical specification of KnowledgeOS'; proposes calling it instead 'KnowledgeOS Epistemic Model — Conceptual and Formal Specification', listing items still needing formalization: exact ontology/type system, proposition semantics, evidence model, inference semantics, conflict algebra, gap detection semantics, Ideal State construction, discrepancy semantics, decision criteria, transition semantics, authorization/governance, persistence semantics, concurrency/versioning, presentation projection semantics. States ConceptualCompleteness ≠ FormalCompleteness.

b_rows_sample.anchor: EXP-01: four candidate aggregation operators against seven adversarial properties
b_rows_sample.statement: Both I-5 and I-6 come from the corpus's one genuine experiment, EXP-01: four candidate aggregation operators (MAX, weighted mean, saturating, Bayesian-like) run against seven adversarial properties on a shared normalized evidence universe. The recorded verdict was negative and precise: no simple scalar operator is sufficient as the epistemic foundation; the strongest single lesson was I-6 -- three apparent pieces of evidence may be one observation and two derived representations, so dependencies must be resolved before anything is combined.

b_rows_sample.anchor: What the experiment did not do
b_rows_sample.statement: Two candidates survived all seven listed properties, but survival is not selection: the model deliberately selects no aggregation operator (OQ-3, open by ruling); any implementation claiming 'the KnowledgeOS evidence formula' is claiming something the architecture refuses to claim.

b_rows_sample.anchor: An adjudicated discrepancy, disclosed
b_rows_sample.statement: The repository contains a CSV export of the EXP-01 property matrix that disagrees with the experiment's own prose record in three cells. The governance track adjudicated it (GN-27): the prose record prevails -- internally consistent under its own normalization footnote, while the CSV is inconsistent under any single reading and carries no generator or provenance. The CSV is graded unreliable-standalone; the negative verdict is unaffected under either source. Reported because the book's provenance rules require every seam the programme found to be findable.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Convergence across traditions
b_rows_sample.statement: The constitutional layer arrived at the same prohibition from a different direction: a 'knowledge quality' scalar is a forbidden surrogate (Article 2's failure signature is literally 'Knowledge Quality = 0.87'). One prohibition, two independent derivations -- treated as evidence, while still refusing to call it proof.

b_rows_sample.statement: Omega enters on 2026-08-24 -- not in the measure-theory crisis where a reader of Part III might assume it was born, but in the typed-model and Bayesian-mind readings, as the ambient space a mathematical epistemic model quietly presupposes; the crisis, when it came a day later, inherited Omega and then had to dismantle it. b_rows_sample.anchor: The experiment and the largest self-audit

The era's evidential temper -- test hard, claim little -- is the reason the final architecture can show TESTED grades at all.

a_rows_sample.statement: The ECS document's six primitives (Observation, Time Window, Synthesis, Snapshot, Publication Gate, Authority Pointer) are mapped onto KnowledgeOS concepts (Evidence/Observation, Temporal Dimension, Assessment/Interpretation, Published Knowledge State, Authority Boundary, Trusted Reference), independently rediscovering the existing (Semantic, Evidence, Authority, Temporal, Lifecycle) dimension set and additionally suggesting a Publication State.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Reality -> Observation -> Evidence -> Validation method -> Knowledge claim -> Authority decision -> Published knowledge

a_rows_sample.anchor: Reality -> Observation -> Pramana (valid method) -> Knowledge state -> Authority/publication
a_rows_sample.statement: Combined ECS+Vedanta pipeline restated in the placed document.

b_rows_sample.anchor: How does a knowledge system distinguish source, means, validation, and realization? ... Knowledge is not one entity -- it has an epistemic pipeline.
b_rows_sample.statement: The Veda-Upanishad-Vedanta analysis is framed as distinct from prior lenses (Topology/Vani/Zero/Gita-Tripuisi/ECS) because it asks how a knowledge system distinguishes source, means, validation, and realization -- introducing the claim that knowledge is not one entity but has an epistemic pipeline.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Source -> Essence extraction -> Interpretation / validation method ... A common mistake in AI systems: Document = Knowledge. Vedanta would reject that.
b_rows_sample.statement: The Veda->Upanishad->Vedanta structure is abstracted as Source->Essence extraction->Interpretation/validation method; warns against the common AI-system mistake of equating Document with Knowledge (better model: Expression->Meaning extraction->Understanding->Validated knowledge).

b_rows_sample.anchor: Pramata (Knower) / Pramana (Validation method) / Prameya (Object known) / Prama (Valid knowledge). This is almost a missing KnowledgeOS primitive.
b_rows_sample.statement: Pramana (means of knowledge) is proposed as the biggest useful concept from Vedanta: it separates Pramata (Knower), Pramana (Validation method), Prameya (Object known), Prama (Valid knowledge). Proposes a 'Knowledge Claim' primitive with fields Object (what is claimed), Source (origin), Method (how established), Validator (who/what validated), State (current epistemic status), replacing a naive Knowledge{content, metadata} structure.

b_rows_sample.anchor: KnowledgeOS may need: Operational Knowledge / Meta-Knowledge ... A system that only stores operational knowledge becomes a documentation system. KnowledgeOS needs knowledge about knowledge.
b_rows_sample.statement: Structural (not literal) borrowing of the Apara Vidya (lower knowledge: facts/sciences/methods/texts) vs Para Vidya (higher knowledge: knowledge of underlying principle) distinction, yielding Operational Knowledge vs Meta-Knowledge; warns that a system storing only operational knowledge degenerates into a documentation system.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Reality -> Observation -> Evidence -> Validation method -> Knowledge claim -> Authority decision -> Published knowledge
b_rows_sample.statement: Combines ECS ('epistemic systems govern belief, not reality') with Vedanta ('knowledge requires a valid means of knowing') into a stronger seven-stage pipeline: Reality->Observation->Evidence->Validation method->Knowledge claim->Authority decision->Published knowledge.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Vedanta adds: Meaning != Valid Knowledge. Because a statement can have meaning but still not be valid. Example: "The server is healthy"
b_rows_sample.statement: Extends the Vani lens (Expression != Meaning) with a Vedanta addition (Meaning != Valid Knowledge). Worked example: "The server is healthy" separates Expression (text exists), Meaning (a health condition is described), Validation (monitoring evidence confirms it), Authority (authorized person/system accepts it) as four distinct, separable layers.

b_rows_sample.anchor: INV-KOS Candidate: Knowledge Requires Provenance of Knowing. A KnowledgeOS knowledge state SHALL preserve not only what is known, but the means by which it became knowable. Forbidden collapse: Statement -> Truth / Source document -> Valid knowledge. Strength: Candidate.
b_rows_sample.statement: New candidate invariant proposed (not yet established): 'Knowledge Requires Provenance of Knowing' -- a KnowledgeOS knowledge state should preserve not only what is known but the means (Claim/Evidence/Method/Validator/Authority) by which it became knowable; forbids collapsing a Statement into Truth or a Source document into Valid knowledge.
