a_rows_sample.anchor: The Kernel owns everything necessary to protect the aggregate invariant during admission, and nothing more... the criterion's own key term ('the aggregate invariant', singular) is not specified
a_rows_sample.statement: S1-F009's 'equilibrium criterion' for Kernel membership contains a free variable: law carries eleven invariants (INV-KOS-IDENTITY-001 through HISTORY), and the criterion's output is entirely determined by which is substituted -- ranging from a near-minimal rule-evaluator to 'everything in' (the god-object F007 warns against). The criterion is therefore a schema, not a decision procedure, and its apparent power to reconcile the small-Kernel/large-Kernel dispute (S1-F007 vs S1-F008) is an artifact of underspecification, not resolution: 'compatibility with two opposed positions is not resolution of them; it is silence wearing a decision's clothing.'

a_rows_sample.anchor: The Kernel is a domain boundary, not a component... Then, in the same finding: 'Its implementation may be in the aggregate' and 'the Kernel is the part of the aggregate...'
a_rows_sample.statement: S1-F009 asserts the Kernel is 'a domain boundary, not a component' but then elaborates in component language ('the part of the aggregate...'), an unflagged type error: a set of rules is not a part of an aggregate, it is a constraint the aggregate satisfies. This means related findings (S1-F011's 'not a thing', S1-F012's 'domain space') may agree with F009's assertion while disagreeing with its elaboration, so any convergence claim must specify which half it converges on.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The equilibrium criterion itself... Verdict -> PRESERVE AS KNOWLEDGE ONLY, and per .1 only once its invariant is bound.
a_rows_sample.statement: Implementation verdicts for S1-F009: identity uniqueness/immutability -- DO NOT IMPLEMENT (already protected by INV-KOS-IDENTITY-001); admission event-completeness -- NEEDS FURTHER EVIDENCE (open question, not adjudicated); the equilibrium criterion itself -- PRESERVE AS KNOWLEDGE ONLY, useful as a review prompt but not implementable in any form until its invariant is bound; no new Kernel membership is supported by this artifact.

a_rows_sample.anchor: A member-list is a proposal about what the Kernel contains, and S2-F024.1 shows the corpus has no bound criterion for deciding such lists.
a_rows_sample.statement: Kernel-test verdict: DO NOT IMPLEMENT -- a member-list is a proposal, not a capability; implementing from a member list would repeat the exact failure S1-F007 diagnoses (membership by capability enumeration with no invariant named). The two lists survive fully as data; only the 'instability' interpretation and the intersection's informativeness are challenged; zero implementation consequence, the appropriate outcome for a finding about competing proposals rather than a required capability.

a_rows_sample.anchor: an admitted object must be fully accountable: its identity, state, confidence, justification, evidence, and history must be co-consistent and recoverable.
a_rows_sample.statement: S1-F012's conjunctive co-consistency-and-recoverability invariant (across six components) is shown to be the maximal substitution into S1-F009's unbound equilibrium-criterion schema: substituting the conjunctive invariant for 'the aggregate invariant' yields the six-component God Aggregate S1-F007 diagnoses and S1-F011's Q4 asks how to prevent -- so F009 and F012 are not two independent formulations but one completing the other in the god-object direction; the document half-concedes this itself, flagging 'Accountability' as non-standard DDD vocabulary that might translate to 'invariant protection.'

a_rows_sample.anchor: the boundary question is twelfth, not first... a sequence that would have prevented its own eight competing formulations
a_rows_sample.statement: S1-F015's twelve-question discovery sequence (with the boundary question ordered twelfth, project-endorsed as 'the correct discovery sequence') is confirmed as the sharpest methodological result reviewed: every earlier Kernel formulation answered the boundary question first and worked backwards, deriving different boundaries from differing assumptions about commitment/identity/evidence/change; this sequence inverts that, and S2-F024.1's free-variable finding is a direct instance -- S1-F009's criterion could not bind its invariant because it never asked questions 1-9 first.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Confidence (if derivable) and Supersession/contestation (if separate lifecycle)... this member list is not a list -- it is a list parameterised by two open questions.
a_rows_sample.statement: The document's conditional-exclusion technique (declaring member-list items conditional on named open questions rather than asserting them outright) is confirmed as the most sophisticated single move in the Session-1 record: it directly answers the free-variable criticism made of S1-F009 elsewhere, by declaring its free variables instead of hiding them -- a genuine methodological advance arising from inside the corpus, judged worth preserving strongly.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Four kinds: absolute . prior . subsequent . locus-relative, each requiring its pratiyogi... a negative claim without its counter-correlate is not well-formed. "This was never proposed" and "this was proposed and refused" have different counter-correlates and are different assertions.
b_rows_sample.statement: The Tarka-derived four-way absence typology (absolute, prior, subsequent, locus-relative absence, each requiring its pratiyogi/counter-correlate) supplies a principled vocabulary for S2-F024 Candidate B's finding that S1-F009's source treats "produce nothing" and "produce a rejection event" as interchangeable outcomes: without its counter-correlate, "this was never proposed" (prior absence) collapses into indistinguishability from "this was proposed and refused" (subsequent absence), which is a malformed negative claim under the typology; this connection is the reviewer's own inference, not drawn by either Session 1 or the source, and strengthens but does not change Candidate B's verdict.

Note: S2-F024's finding (Candidate B) that S1-F009's source treats "produce nothing" and "produce a rejection event" as interchangeable admission outcomes, so a refused admission becomes indistinguishable from one never attempted; S2-R-F023.2 supplies the Tarka absence-typology vocabulary (prior vs subsequent absence, each needing its pratiyogi) as this finding's principled form.

a_rows_sample.anchor:
### `[PROP] Evaluation Masking`

A model distinction at local semantic level may become unobservable after composition with an absorbing aggregation operator... $$
\boxed{
Observable(ModelDifference)
\neq
ModelDifference
}
$$
a_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes a new [PROP] methodological phenomenon, Evaluation Masking: a model distinction at the local semantic level may become unobservable after composition with an absorbing aggregation operator -- formally, if f(a,b)=U for sufficiently many b, then a1≠a2 may still yield f(a1,b)=f(a2,b)=U; yields the invariant Observable(ModelDifference)≠ModelDifference: a model difference can exist yet become invisible under an aggregation operator.

a_rows_sample.anchor:
> **Never validate a semantic distinction only at the final aggregate output.**

We need at least:

```text
atomic representation
        ↓
local operation
        ↓
composition
        ↓
aggregation
        ↓
final observable
```
a_rows_sample.statement: Connects the masking discovery to the Hilbert-space experiment (different summaries of the same joint structure gave very different answers) to derive a standing experimental rule: never validate a semantic distinction only at the final aggregate output; test at every level of a pipeline (atomic representation -> local operation -> composition -> aggregation -> final observable).

a_rows_sample.anchor:
### `[PROP] Evaluation Masking`

A model distinction at local semantic level may become unobservable after composition with an absorbing aggregation operator.
a_rows_sample.statement: Duplicate (verbatim) of S2486's formalization of the Evaluation Masking phenomenon: f(a,b)=U for sufficiently many b can hide a1≠a2 behind f(a1,b)=f(a2,b)=U, yielding Observable(ModelDifference)≠ModelDifference.

b_rows_sample.anchor: P9 REFUTED as stated. Golog's semantics is defined relative to a basic action theory — SSA + preconditions + unique names + S0. KnowledgeOS has none of these, and 04 shows the SSA is blocked behind Contr and DECISION-02. ... Golog is UNREACHABLE from the current state, and the distance is measurable: it needs delta, which needs Contr, which needs the evaluation representation, which needs R_req.
b_rows_sample.statement: P9 refuted as stated: Golog presupposes a basic action theory KnowledgeOS lacks, and is UNREACHABLE (not merely unhelpful) via a precise, measurable dependency chain: Golog needs delta, delta needs Contr, Contr needs the evaluation representation, the evaluation representation needs R_req.

b_rows_sample.anchor: KnowledgeOS ran its own composition experiment (KR-COMP), and its result is stronger and independent: composition over evidence within and across frames ... the load-bearing parameter phi superset-eq {time,context} ... the criteria select a FRAME QUALIFIER, not a rule. These are not competing answers to one question. They are answers to different questions, and conflating them would import a sequencing model where the corpus has an evidential one. KnowledgeOS-DERIVED; Reiter neither corroborates nor challenges it.
b_rows_sample.statement: Sharply distinguishes Golog's action-sequence composition from the project's own prior, independent KR-COMP experiment's evidence composition (within and across frames, governed by the frame qualifier phi ⊇ {time,context}, whose result selects a frame qualifier rather than a composition rule) -- these answer different questions and must not be conflated, since doing so would import an action-sequencing model where the corpus needs an evidential one.

a_notations: f(a,b)=U for many b ⇒ f(a1,b)=f(a2,b)=U even if a1≠a2
b_notations: phi ⊇ {time,context} selects a frame qualifier, not a composition rule

group_evidence.why_grouped: explicit agent-stated uncertainty: 'kr-comp-frame-qualifier-result' POSSIBLY relates to 'evaluation-masking-phenomenon' (batch B0061). Note: A prior, independent KnowledgeOS experiment (KR-COMP) composing evidence within and across frames, whose criteria select a FRAME QUALIFIER (the load-bearing parameter phi ⊇ {time,context}) rather than a composition RULE; explicitly a different question from Golog's action-sequencing composition, not a competing answer to the same question -- conflating them would import a sequencing model where the corpus has an evidential one. KnowledgeOS-DERIVED; Reiter neither corroborates nor challenges it.

a_rows_sample.anchor: This is the right next step because we now need to connect evidence aggregation with the question: When is acquiring another piece of evidence actually useful? This is the mathematical bridge between Evidence -> Zero -> Lord.
a_rows_sample.statement: Frames Step 25C.3's purpose as the mathematical bridge Evidence→Zero→Lord: when is acquiring more evidence actually useful.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Suppose KnowledgeOS currently has K_t and is considering an investigation action a ... The action may produce E_a. We need to calculate whether obtaining E_a is worthwhile. The first quantity is InformationGain(E_a|K_t) and eventually ValueOfInformation(a|K_t,G).
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines the two central quantities to be formalized: InformationGain(E_a|K_t) and ValueOfInformation(a|K_t,G) for an investigation action a.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Suppose KnowledgeOS already knows E_1: NexusVersion=3.69. Now Lord proposes: Read the exact same inventory file again. The resulting evidence is E_2=E_1. The new information should be IG(E_2|E_1)=0. This is a very desirable property. It means KnowledgeOS can recognize: 'I am about to spend resources
a_rows_sample.statement: First experiment: duplicate-information retrieval must give IG(E2|E1)=0, letting KnowledgeOS recognize it is about to spend resources re-learning something already known.

a_rows_sample.anchor: For a hypothesis H, Shannon information is I(H)=-log P(H) ... IG(E;H)=Ent(H)-Ent(H|E) [renaming entropy Ent to avoid clash with hypothesis H].
a_rows_sample.statement: Adopts Shannon entropy-reduction as the formal InformationGain measure: IG(E;H)=Ent(H)-Ent(H|E), renaming entropy notation to avoid clashing with the hypothesis symbol H.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Suppose P(H)=0.5. The uncertainty is Ent(H)=1 bit. Now an observation gives P(H|E)=0.9. The posterior entropy is lower. Therefore IG(E;H)>0. The observation has reduced uncertainty.
a_rows_sample.statement: Worked numerical example confirming IG(E;H)>0 when a posterior of 0.9 reduces entropy from the 1-bit prior.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Suppose E_2=f(E_1). Then even though E_2 is technically another artifact: IG(E_2;H|E_1)=0 or approximately zero. Therefore the more useful quantity is IG(E_2;H|K_t). This asks: How much does this new evidence tell us that we do not already know?
a_rows_sample.statement: Shows a derived-copy artifact E2=f(E1) gives IG≈0 conditional on E1, motivating the conditional quantity IG(E2;H|K_t) as what KnowledgeOS actually needs (novel information relative to current knowledge, not raw artifact count).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Suppose E_1 is one restore test. A second independently executed restore test E_2 can provide IG(E_2;H|E_1)>0. This is the mathematical explanation for why independent corroboration can be valuable.
a_rows_sample.statement: Shows independent corroborating evidence yields IG(E2;H|E1)>0 — the formal information-theoretic explanation for why independent corroboration is valuable.

a_rows_sample.anchor: If E_2=f(E_1) then IG(E_2;H|E_1)≈0. This gives us a rigorous interpretation of the earlier qualitative rule: Don't count copied evidence twice. It isn't merely a governance convention. It has an information-theoretic interpretation.
a_rows_sample.statement: Establishes that the earlier 'don't count copied evidence twice' rule has a rigorous information-theoretic interpretation (IG≈0 for derived copies), not merely a governance convention.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The interesting case is 0 < IG(E_2;H|E_1) < IG(E_2;H). This means E_2 contains some new information, but part of its information was already contained in E_1. This is likely to be extremely common in KnowledgeOS. Vendor documentation -> Internal architecture document -> Human report -> LLM summary.
a_rows_sample.statement: Identifies partially-dependent evidence (0<IG(E2;H|E1)<IG(E2;H)) as the common case in practice, illustrated by a documentation-lineage chain (vendor doc→architecture doc→human report→LLM summary), none of which can be treated as fully independent.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Define NovelInformation(E|K) as the information not already represented by the current knowledge state. Conceptually NovelInformation ≈ IG(E;Target|K). This should become one of the quantities available to Lord.
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines NovelInformation(E|K) ≈ IG(E;Target|K) as a candidate quantity to be made available to Lord.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Suppose Lord can run Action A: a five-second database query, expected information gain 0.1 bit. Action B: a two-week migration test, expected information gain 1.0 bit. Simply maximizing information would select B. That would be absurd. Therefore InformationGain != Value.
a_rows_sample.statement: Counterexample showing naive information-maximization would irrationally select a costly two-week test over a cheap query merely for higher bit-count, establishing InformationGain≠Value.

a_rows_sample.anchor: We need something like ValueOfInformation = ExpectedBenefitFromInformation - Cost. But there is another important term: Risk. Therefore a preliminary formulation is VOI(a) = ExpectedDecisionValueAfter(a) - CurrentDecisionValue - Cost(a) - Risk(a).
a_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes a preliminary Value-of-Information equation VOI(a)=ExpectedDecisionValueAfter(a)-CurrentDecisionValue-Cost(a)-Risk(a).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Current best decision a* = argmax_{a in A} EU(a|K_t). Now consider information-gathering action q. After receiving evidence E_q: a*(E_q) = argmax_a EU(a|K_t,E_q). Then VOI(q) = E_{E_q}[max_a EU(a|K_t,E_q)] - max_a EU(a|K_t) - Cost(q). This is a much more rigorous definition.
a_rows_sample.statement: Gives the rigorous decision-theoretic Value-of-Information formula VOI(q)=E_{E_q}[max_a EU(a|K_t,E_q)]-max_a EU(a|K_t)-Cost(q), the standard expected-utility VOI definition applied to Lord's action selection.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Lord can now distinguish: Question A: Can I learn something? from Question B: Is learning it worth doing? The first is information theory. The second is decision theory. Thus Lord = InformationAcquisition + DecisionValue.
a_rows_sample.statement: Distinguishes 'can I learn something' (information theory) from 'is learning it worth doing' (decision theory), decomposing Lord = InformationAcquisition + DecisionValue.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Suppose our goal is G: Determine whether Nexus rollback is safe. Lord considers: Search the company's office seating plan. It may contain enormous information. But IG(E;G)≈0. Therefore VOI≈0. Lord should reject the action. InformationQuantity != GoalRelevantInformation.
a_rows_sample.statement: Falsification test: irrelevant-but-information-rich evidence (office seating plan) has IG(E;G)≈0 against the actual goal, so VOI≈0 and Lord correctly rejects it — InformationQuantity≠GoalRelevantInformation.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Now consider: Execute a restore test against the actual backup. Expected information gain about H: RollbackSafe=True is potentially very high. Therefore IG(E;H|K_t) >> 0. And if the result can change the migration decision: VOI(q) >> 0. This is exactly the type of action Lord should prioritize.
a_rows_sample.statement: Falsification test: a directly goal-relevant restore test yields IG>>0 and VOI(q)>>0, correctly prioritized by Lord.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Suppose the migration has already been formally prohibited by governance. Even if we could learn whether Rollback=True the answer cannot change the current authorized decision. Then VOI(q)≈0. ... The same evidence can have HighInformationValue in one context and ZeroDecisionValue in another. Therefo
a_rows_sample.statement: Falsification test: information that cannot alter an already-governance-prohibited decision has VOI≈0 regardless of its Shannon information content, establishing VOI is goal- and decision-context dependent.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Suppose migration must happen tomorrow. A test requiring three weeks has potentially useful information. But operationally VOI_effective≈0 if the result arrives after the decision deadline. Therefore time is part of the value calculation.
a_rows_sample.statement: Falsification test: information arriving after the decision deadline has VOI_effective≈0, establishing time-to-delivery as part of the value calculation.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Suppose a test could reveal valuable information but requires risking production availability. Then InformationGain>0 but Risk>>0. Therefore Lord should potentially reject it. This gives SafeInformationAcquisition as a governance constraint.
a_rows_sample.statement: Falsification test: high-information but high-risk acquisition should potentially be rejected, giving SafeInformationAcquisition as a governance constraint on Lord.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Suppose Lord can ask an infrastructure expert: Is port 8081 reachable from the target network? The answer could be highly informative. But HumanAnswer is itself evidence. Therefore Question -> HumanResponse -> Evidence -> Assessment. The human answer must not bypass the evidence model.
a_rows_sample.statement: States that a human answer to an information-gathering question is itself Evidence and must flow through Question→HumanResponse→Evidence→Assessment, never bypassing the evidence model.

b_rows_sample.anchor: When several pieces of evidence support the same proposition, how should KnowledgeOS combine them? We must avoid the very tempting but incorrect rule: more sources \Rightarrow more certainty. That is only true under specific assumptions.
b_rows_sample.statement: Frames Step 25C.2's question, warning against the tempting-but-incorrect rule 'more sources ⇒ more certainty', true only under specific assumptions.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Start with a controlled proposition ... H="Rollback will succeed if executed." P(H)=0.5. This is an experimental prior, not a KnowledgeOS principle. ... Evidence E_1 ... P(E_1\mid H)=0.95 and P(E_1\mid\neg H)=0.10. LR_1=9.5. O(H)=1. O(H\mid E_1)=9.5. P(H\mid E_1)\approx90.5\% under this specific sta
b_rows_sample.statement: Works a fully numerical Bayesian likelihood-ratio calculation (LR1=9.5) yielding P(H|E1)≈90.5% under an explicit experimental prior, explicitly not a KnowledgeOS principle.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Important observation ... We have not said "KnowledgeOS now knows rollback will succeed." We have established P(H\mid E_1)\approx0.905 under the assumptions of the model. That is statistical inference, not epistemic truth. Probability\neq KnowledgeState. This confirms the layered architecture from 2
b_rows_sample.statement: Confirms via the numerical example that Probability≠KnowledgeState — a computed posterior is statistical inference under model assumptions, not epistemic truth, validating the layered architecture from 25C.1.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Add genuinely independent evidence ... E_2 is an independently performed restore test. P(E_2\mid H)=0.90 and P(E_2\mid\neg H)=0.20. LR_2=4.5. Under the conditional-independence assumption LR_{12}=LR_1LR_2=42.75. P(H\mid E_1,E_2)\approx97.7\%. This demonstrates the legitimate case where independent e
b_rows_sample.statement: Computes the legitimate independent-evidence-combination case: LR12=LR1·LR2=42.75 yielding P(H|E1,E2)≈97.7%, demonstrating substantial legitimate confidence increase under genuine independence.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Now attack the independence assumption ... E_2 is simply a report generated from E_1. E_2=f(E_1). If we nevertheless calculate LR_{12}=LR_1LR_2, we manufacture certainty. This is mathematically wrong. IndependentEvidence must be established, not assumed.
b_rows_sample.statement: Shows that applying LR1·LR2 to a copied (E2=f(E1)) evidence pair manufactures false certainty mathematically — IndependentEvidence must be established, not assumed.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Perfect duplicate experiment ... E_2=E_1. Then P(H\mid E_1,E_2)=P(H\mid E_1). There should be no additional information. Aggregate(E,E)=Aggregate(E) for duplicate evidence. This confirms the idempotency requirement.
b_rows_sample.statement: Numerically confirms the idempotency requirement: a perfect duplicate provides zero additional posterior shift.

b_rows_sample.anchor: A surprising consequence ... the real input to inference is not \{E_1,E_2,\ldots,E_n\}. It is closer to Evidence Graph where we know relationships such as E_1\perp E_2 or E_2=f(E_1). This is not an implementation detail. It changes the mathematics of aggregation. ... Three cases ... Case A duplicate
b_rows_sample.statement: States that the true input to inference is the Evidence Graph (relationships, not a bare set), classifying three information-gain cases (duplicate=0, dependent=less than naive, independent=>0) as the beginning of an evidence-combination theory.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Experiment — contradictory evidence ... E_3: Rollback test failed. P(E_3\mid H)=0.05 and P(E_3\mid\neg H)=0.80. LR_3=0.0625. 42.75\times0.0625=2.671875. P(H\mid E_1,E_2,E_3)\approx0.728. So the statistical model says approximately 72.8\%. ... But KnowledgeOS must not say merely "72.8%" ... Support=\
b_rows_sample.statement: Computes contradictory-evidence-adjusted posterior P(H|E1,E2,E3)≈72.8% while requiring the epistemic Support/Challenge structure be retained alongside the scalar — the critical result that the statistical result and qualitative epistemic state must coexist.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The statistical result and epistemic state coexist ... EpistemicAssessment + StatisticalInference. Proposition: Rollback will succeed. Evidence: E1 supports, E2 supports, E3 challenges. Conflict: true. Statistical model: P(H|E) = 0.728. Inference model: Bayesian. Dependency assumptions: E1 ⟂ E2. Thi
b_rows_sample.statement: Constructs a worked full record combining EpistemicAssessment and StatisticalInference (evidence roles, conflict flag, model, dependency assumptions), far richer than a bare confidence percentage.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Experiment — source reliability ... E_3 comes from an uncalibrated test. We should not simply discard it. Instead its statistical model should represent P(E_3\mid H) and P(E_3\mid\neg H) appropriately. Reliability belongs in the model, not as an arbitrary score.
b_rows_sample.statement: States that source reliability belongs inside the statistical likelihood model (P(E|H), P(E|¬H)) rather than as an arbitrary bolt-on score.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Experiment — one very strong evidence item versus many weak ones ... E_1 is a direct successful restore test. Then ten weak human statements. Naive counting says 10>1. KnowledgeOS must not use source count. EvidenceCount\neq EvidenceStrength.
b_rows_sample.statement: Reaffirms EvidenceCount ≠ EvidenceStrength using a strong-single-test-vs-ten-weak-statements experiment.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Experiment — common-cause dependence ... Infrastructure report, Operations report, Manager report all generated from the same monitoring dashboard. E_1,E_2,E_3 are highly correlated. There are three artifacts but approximately one underlying information source. This is exactly why lineage matters. .
b_rows_sample.statement: Contrasts a common-cause-dependent evidence set (three reports from one dashboard, one underlying source) with a genuinely independent evidence set (three separate physical systems), showing only the latter legitimately increases support.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The crucial requirement ... KnowledgeOS therefore needs to distinguish ArtifactMultiplicity from InformationMultiplicity. Three documents can represent one underlying fact. One experiment can generate several genuinely distinct observations. This is an epistemic identity problem, not merely a databa
b_rows_sample.statement: Distinguishes ArtifactMultiplicity from InformationMultiplicity as an epistemic identity problem, not merely database deduplication.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Experiment — evidence arriving sequentially ... After E_1: P(H)=0.905. After E_2: P(H)=0.977. After contradictory E_3: P(H)=0.728. This demonstrates Knowledge/evidence evolution can be non-monotonic. The numerical inference can increase and decrease as evidence arrives. ... But the evidence history
b_rows_sample.statement: Traces the full sequential posterior evolution (0.5→0.905→0.977→0.728), confirming non-monotonic inference alongside cumulative evidence history — InferenceState is revisable, EvidenceHistory is cumulative, matching 25A.3's earlier result.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Experiment — retraction ... E_3 is later determined to be invalid. We do not erase the historical fact that at t_3, KnowledgeOS received E_3. Instead Status(E_3)=Invalid. Then recompute P(H\mid E_1,E_2,E_3^{invalid}). The inference can return toward 97.7%. But the history records why the inference c
b_rows_sample.statement: Works a retraction experiment where E3 is invalidated (not erased), triggering a recomputed posterior returning toward 97.7% while the history records why.

b_rows_sample.anchor: This produces an important invariant ... I_{t+1}=Infer(K_{t+1},M). If evidence is retracted K_{t+1}=Revision(K_t,E^{invalid}). Then I_{t+1} must be recalculated. Inference is a projection of KnowledgeState, not the KnowledgeState itself. This is an important architectural principle.
b_rows_sample.statement: States the invariant Inference is a projection of KnowledgeState, not the KnowledgeState itself — requiring recalculation whenever the underlying KnowledgeState is revised (e.g. via retraction).

b_rows_sample.anchor: This changes how we should model probabilities ... We should not store only P(H)=0.728. We should store InferenceResult=(H,Probability,Model,ModelVersion,InputKnowledgeSnapshot,Assumptions). Hypothesis: H, Probability: 0.728, Model: Bayesian, ModelVersion: 1.2, KnowledgeSnapshot: K17, Assumptions: E
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines a full reproducible InferenceResult=(H,Probability,Model,ModelVersion,InputKnowledgeSnapshot,Assumptions) record instead of storing a bare probability.

b_rows_sample.anchor: This is extremely important for KnowledgeOS ... Why did KnowledgeOS say rollback had a 72.8% probability? We should be able to answer Because K_{17} + Model_{1.2} + Assumptions_{X} \Rightarrow0.728. This is much stronger than "The AI estimated 72.8%."
b_rows_sample.statement: Argues the InferenceResult record enables answering 'why did KnowledgeOS say 72.8%?' with a precise reconstruction (snapshot+model+assumptions), far stronger than 'the AI estimated it'.

a_rows_sample.anchor: L1 CONSTITUTIONAL prohibitions... L2 FORMAL MODEL descriptions... L3 REPOSITORY ARCH boundaries... L4 IMPLEMENTATION behavior... L5 GOVERNANCE acts... and OUTSIDE: the historical corpus: evidence of discovery, authority over nothing
a_rows_sample.statement: States the five-layer architecture separating kinds of authority, not kinds of function: L1 Constitutional (prohibitions, ratified law -- "this collapse must never happen"), L2 Formal Model (descriptions, authorized model -- "this is the epistemic process"), L3 Repository Architecture (boundaries, proposed realization -- "this structure makes L1 unbreakable"), L4 Implementation (behavior, evidence of practice -- "this code actually runs"), L5 Governance (acts, the authority itself -- "this ruling made X authoritative"), plus the historical corpus explicitly outside all five layers, holding authority over nothing; a functional layering (storage below logic below interface) would leave the programme's recurring authority-confusion failures expressible, while this layering makes them type errors.

a_rows_sample.anchor: each article was failure-tested at selection: the ratifying record names, per article, the corruption that opens if it is removed... 1 Identity | Document = Knowledge . vector match = identity... 3 Authority | a recorded reference self-authorizes . assessment becomes binding . sensor = expert = AI ... 6 Verification | AI output = reality . unsupported claim = knowledge . hallucination = evidence . black-box inference
a_rows_sample.statement: Reproduces the eleven-article failure-tested guard table pairing each constitutional article with the named corruption/forbidden-collapse that opens if the article is removed (e.g. Identity: Document=Knowledge, vector match=identity; Authority: a recorded reference self-authorizes, sensor=expert=AI; Verification: AI output=reality, hallucination=evidence, black-box inference; History: new truth overwrites old, freshness=truth); frames the constitution as a census of ways real systems routinely counterfeit knowledge, with each counterfeit individually outlawed, and notes the articles are prohibitions, never mechanisms, which is what keeps the layer stable under free mechanism replacement below it.

a_rows_sample.anchor: of the model's twelve invariants, exactly two are computationally TESTED... eight are READ... and two are REQUIRED-BY-COHERENCE... This census was corrected under GN-45 after the hostile pass caught its first version omitting Evidence's TESTED grade -- finding AF-F-7.
a_rows_sample.statement: States the L2 formal model's full epistemic-grade census (two invariants computationally TESTED from a single recorded experiment; eight READ -- verified against corpus sources by systematic reading, establishing assertion/argument but not experimental confirmation; two REQUIRED-BY-COHERENCE -- entered by ruled repair after a falsification pass), discloses this census itself was corrected under a later governance act (GN-45) after a hostile review pass caught its first version omitting Evidence's TESTED grade (finding AF-F-7), and states the disclosure discipline itself is L2 content under invariant I-8 (no architectural assertion without evidence).

a_rows_sample.statement: States L4 (executable implementation) at its true, exhaustive strength: only a session bootstrap (resolving process authority from the governed record, refusing to conflate identity/role/eligibility/authorization/ownership/continuation, failing closed on any unresolved fact), a read-only operating-model presenter, and check-only observation-pipeline diagnostics actually run; no L2 formal object (Zero engine, EC deriver, ladder datatype, DC executor) is implemented, per conformance-pass finding CF-015, with the ruled conclusion that substantial evidence exists for boundaries/governance principles but implementation-level correspondence for the formal layer is not established.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Take the AcceptancePolicy -- the object whose mis-layering caused more recorded trouble than any other. As content, a policy draft is L2 material... a_rows_sample.statement: Traces the AcceptancePolicy (the object whose mis-layering caused the most recorded trouble in the programme) through all five layers as a worked example: as content it is L2 material at rest in K_t; as the governor of admission it is an L2 object with an L1 shadow (Article 3 forbids self-authorization, I-11 forbids ungoverned change); any enforcement would be L4 code that must first consult the governance record; and the failure the layering prevents is the programme's most-sighted defect (the policy that governs while nothing governs it, sighted independently four times, per Chapter III.8).

b_rows_sample.statement: Proposes a six-layer architecture: Layer 0 Lenses (instruments, never domain objects: Zero, Yoni, Lord, Sarathi, Buddhi, Krishna, Sanjaya); Layer 1 Structures (E_t epistemic state, 𝓑_t boundary, AF_t argument field, M_t models/assumptions); Layer 2 Projections (all derived, none primitive: Sat_c, Gap, U, Zero, Balanced); Layer 3 Attribution (A_t=Γ(E_t,Q,C,EC), not knowledge); Layer 4 Transition+Event (δ, ClosureEvent->History); Layer 5 History (append-only, written by the kernel, never read).

b_rows_sample.anchor: | **`𝓑_t`** | nine epistemic conditions distinct at the boundary, **all `U` under projection** | `KR-ZERO-H`: 9 distinct, 36/36 pairs |...**But 37 of 41 typed distinctions are currently unsupported**
b_rows_sample.statement: Restates the evidence for each Layer-1 structure being primary (E_t: truth not in Γ's domain; 𝓑_t: 9 boundary conditions collapse to U; AF_t: 6 conditions identical under scalar cancellation; M_t: model fit and causal validity independent), and that 37 of 41 typed distinctions in 𝓑_t remain evidentially unsupported (carried marked, not silently).

b_rows_sample.anchor: | **L1** | **No projection is primitive.**... | **L2** | **Every projection declares its kernel**... | **L3** | **The kernel writes history and never reads it.**... | **L4** | **A lens never appears on the RHS of a domain equation.**
b_rows_sample.statement: States four statically-checkable structural laws derived from measured failures: L1 no projection is primitive (define structure, derive projection; caught 5 failures); L2 every projection declares what it discards (caught the 9->1 U collapse); L3 the kernel writes history and never reads it, any reading operation is a proposal to move the boundary requiring adjudication (KR-HISTORY: 0 reads); L4 a lens never appears on the RHS of a domain equation (11 live violations, one pattern accounting for 6); plus a proposed but not-yet-enforceable L5: every claim of progress names its ordering (83% of 1793 claims specify none).

b_rows_sample.anchor: | **`⪰`** | `L5` unenforceable... | **`Contr`** | `Sat_content` is not a function on contradictory states...| **5 facet gaps** | `ZI-07`...
b_rows_sample.statement: States what the model explicitly does not solve, in six named places, each with a next step: the progress ordering ⪰ (L5 unenforceable, 1491 claims unfalsifiable), Contr (fourth-value question coupled to the one clean contradiction repair), ≡_sem (kernel minimality inadmissible, 13 and 8 both minima under different algebras), factivity (relocated not resolved), five named facet gaps, and 37 unsupported typed distinctions.

b_rows_sample.anchor: **Invariant custody.** Reduction is not free: eliminating `Challenge` moved custody of *"a verdict must be challengeable"* from **one** operator to **two**. Any reduction must report `custody(I, 𝒦)` for every invariant it claims to preserve
b_rows_sample.statement: Illustrates invariant custody with a concrete worked example: eliminating the Challenge operator did not remove the 'a verdict must be challengeable' invariant, it moved its custody from one operator to two -- any claimed kernel reduction must report custody(I,𝒦) for every invariant it claims to preserve, not merely report a smaller operator count |𝒦|.

b_rows_sample.anchor: | 1 · **Declare the lens register** ... | 4 · **Define `Contr`** with the fourth value **and** the `Zero` readings in one step | research | `Sat_content` totality; 4 open items collapse to 1 |
b_rows_sample.statement: Proposes a cheapest-first six-step migration plan: (1) declare the lens register (vocabulary decision), (2) decide factivity rename-vs-externalize (architecture decision), (3) decide whether Delta is a count or ordered (scopable separately from ⪰), (4) define Contr with the fourth value and Zero readings together (research, collapses 4 open items to 1), (5) define ⪰ (research), (6) test or drop the 37 unsupported distinctions -- noting steps 1-3 are decisions requiring no simulation.

b_rows_sample.anchor: So I would change: "the primary objects" to: **"candidate primary structures."**
b_rows_sample.statement: Downgrades the claimed status of E_t/𝓑_t/AF_t/M_t from 'the primary objects' to 'candidate primary structures', arguing the evidence is suggestive but not sufficient to establish these as fundamental (e.g. 𝓑_t or AF_t might themselves be derived from a more fundamental state).

Warns against constitutionalizing the empirical 'kernel writes history, never reads it' (0 reads in the tested implementation) into a general theoretical law, since some epistemic systems legitimately perform retrospective revision (later evidence changing interpretation of earlier evidence); proposes the safer formulation that history access by the kernel is an explicit architectural capability requiring adjudication, not a settled prohibition.

Refines L4 from a syntactic rule ('never on the RHS') to a semantic one: a lens cannot be used as a domain object or as the ontological producer of the object it examines -- catching K=Yoni and KnowledgeOS=Yoni×Zero×Sarathi while permitting legitimate expressions like Boundary=ZeroLens(K).

Corrects the wording '1,491 claims unfalsifiable' as imprecise Popperian usage; recommends 'not currently testable as progress claims' unless each claim has actually been individually analysed for falsifiability -- a statistical/methodological precision issue.

b_rows_sample.anchor:
If the semantics of $$
K_t
$$ change from $$
K_t=\Gamma(E_t,\ldots)
$$ to $$
A_t=\Gamma(E_t,\ldots),
$$ then something **has changed semantically**, even if no paragraph is physically deleted... Therefore the correct statement is: **The proposal does not modify v1.2; it proposes a possible restructuring of v1.2 based on experimental findings.**
b_rows_sample.statement: Rejects the proposal's claim 'nothing is deleted from v1.2, six items repositioned, one retired' as lacking version-diff discipline: renaming K_t's semantics to A_t is a semantic change even without deleting text, and retiring Zero⟺Δ=∅ is a genuine theoretical change; the correct statement is that the proposal proposes a possible restructuring of v1.2, not a non-modification of it.

b_rows_sample.anchor: But I would **not yet call them bounded contexts**. They are currently better described as: **candidate bounded contexts / conceptual responsibilities.**
b_rows_sample.statement: Downgrades the proposal's six DDD 'bounded contexts' (Epistemic Core, Attribution, Verification, History, Governance, Lenses) to 'candidate bounded contexts / conceptual responsibilities', since bounded-context status requires actual linguistic, ownership, consistency-boundary and integration evidence not yet demonstrated.

b_rows_sample.anchor:
$$
Custody(I)=\{c\mid c\text{ is responsible for preserving invariant }I\}.
$$ A reduction is valid only if: $$
\forall I\in I_{required},
\quad
Custody_{before}(I)\neq\varnothing
\Rightarrow
Custody_{after}(I)\neq\varnothing.
$$
b_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes invariant custody as a reduction-validity criterion: Custody(I)={c | c is responsible for preserving invariant I}; a kernel reduction is valid only if, for every required invariant I, a non-empty custody before reduction implies a non-empty custody after -- proposed as a much better kernel-reduction criterion than counting operators.

Commissions KR-PROJ-2026-09-02 (Projection, Information Loss and Invariant Preservation) to systematically test what distinctions a projection collapses, whether they matter/are recoverable, which invariants survive, whether Zero can be defined as a boundary-analysis lens over losses, whether Gap/Sat/Balanced/DetectGap are correctly understood as projections, and explicitly instructs the experiment to try to falsify the proposal's four candidate primary structures rather than assume them.

Proposes a tentative post-review research architecture S_t --πi--> R_i,t (a candidate rich structure with a family of representations/projections), with ZeroLens(S_t,πi) examining lost distinctions and Θ:S_t×Input_t->S_{t+1} defining transformation separately from History_t recording it -- yielding the five-way separation Structure≠Projection≠Lens≠Transformation≠History.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Evidence\neq Inference ... E_1+R_1\vdash UpgradeRequired
a_rows_sample.statement: States Evidence ≠ Inference (evidence supports an assertion; inference derives one proposition from others), worked with E1+R1 ⊢ UpgradeRequired.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Derivation=(Premises,Rules,Substitutions,Assumptions,Conclusion) ... itself a knowledge artifact
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines Derivation as a first-class five-field object (Premises,Rules,Substitutions,Assumptions,Conclusion), itself a knowledge artifact, worked with a SecurityPolicyTriggered example.

a_rows_sample.anchor: SecurityPolicyTriggered=true alone ... destroys auditability ... Conclusion\leftarrow Derivation\leftarrow Premises must remain traceable
a_rows_sample.statement: Warns storing only a bare conclusion destroys auditability (loses why/from-which-evidence/which-rule/which-version/which-assumptions) — Conclusion<-Derivation<-Premises must remain traceable.

a_rows_sample.anchor: \Gamma\vdash\phi ... modus ponens \frac{A\rightarrow B, A}{B}
a_rows_sample.statement: Introduces classical entailment Gamma⊢phi and modus ponens as the base logical case.

a_rows_sample.anchor: uncertain facts; incomplete information; temporal facts; conflicting observations; probabilistic assertions; causal models; policies; exceptions; permissions ... should not force everything into classical Boolean logic. We need a typed inference framework
a_rows_sample.statement: Argues real enterprise knowledge (uncertain, incomplete, temporal, conflicting, probabilistic, causal, policy, exception, permission facts) cannot be forced into classical Boolean logic alone, requiring a typed inference framework.

a_rows_sample.anchor: A: Type=EmpiricalAssertion ... GovernanceRule ... DerivedAssertion ... ProbabilisticAssertion ... the inference engine must know what kind of proposition it is handling
a_rows_sample.statement: Requires propositions to carry an explicit Type (EmpiricalAssertion, GovernanceRule, DerivedAssertion, ProbabilisticAssertion, etc.) so the inference engine knows what kind of proposition it handles.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Rule=(PremisePattern,Condition,Transformation,ConclusionPattern) ... should have a machine-readable representation
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines an inference Rule as a four-field structure (PremisePattern,Condition,Transformation,ConclusionPattern), worked with an Approved+ArchitectureRelevant=>Authorized example, requiring machine-readable representation.

a_rows_sample.anchor: SoftwareChangeBC may define its own rules ... The bounded context owns the semantics
a_rows_sample.statement: Requires domain-specific rule ownership: a generic universal rule is rejected in favor of bounded-context-owned rules (e.g. a SoftwareChangeBC-owned ArchitectureReviewRequired rule).

a_rows_sample.anchor: RuleID and RuleVersion ... ARCH-CHG-017 v2.1 ... if the rule changes, an old derivation must not magically acquire the new meaning
a_rows_sample.statement: Requires every important rule to carry RuleID+RuleVersion+effective date, so a subsequent rule change cannot silently reinterpret an old derivation.

a_rows_sample.anchor: R_1 valid in 2025 ... R_2 replaced it in 2026 ... Derivation=Premises(t)+Rules(t)+Context(t)
a_rows_sample.statement: Requires temporal rule evaluation via Derivation=Premises(t)+Rules(t)+Context(t), evaluating historical conclusions using the rule version effective at that time — 'crucial for auditability.'

a_rows_sample.anchor: Proof\neq EvidenceSupport ... The server is currently running 3.70 is not mathematically proved from axioms. It is established through observation/evidence
a_rows_sample.statement: Distinguishes formal mathematical Proof (Gamma⊢phi) from empirical EvidenceSupport(phi), illustrated by a server-version claim resting on observation, not proof.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Proof=(p_1,\ldots,p_n) ... a proof checker can then independently verify ValidProof=True ... deterministic
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines a formal Proof as a step sequence checkable deterministically by a proof checker producing ValidProof=True.

a_rows_sample.anchor: ProofCarryingAssertion ... a machine-checkable derivation ... sharply reduces dependence on the LLM's reasoning text
a_rows_sample.statement: Introduces ProofCarryingAssertion: a conclusion accompanied by a machine-checkable derivation the verifier can independently step through, sharply reducing dependence on LLM reasoning text.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Therefore the migration is safe ... not a proof ... CandidateDerivation ... Verify(Derivation)=True/False ... LLM proposes derivation; Verifier validates derivation
a_rows_sample.statement: Establishes the LLM-proposes/verifier-validates pattern: an LLM's prose conclusion is not a proof; it should produce a CandidateDerivation that a deterministic verifier checks — 'entirely consistent with our earlier deterministic-assurance architecture.'

a_rows_sample.anchor: A\rightarrow B but the LLM concludes A\rightarrow C ... InvalidDerivation ... the system does not need to determine whether the LLM is lying ... not derivable from the supplied premises/rules
a_rows_sample.statement: Worked hallucinated-inference example: an unsupported conclusion the rules don't derive returns InvalidDerivation, without needing to judge LLM intent — 'the conclusion is not derivable from the supplied premises/rules.'

a_rows_sample.anchor: NotDerivable(A)\neq Derivable(\neg A) ... connects directly to 25O
a_rows_sample.statement: States open-world inference: NotDerivable(A) ≠ Derivable(¬A) unless the domain has an explicit closed-world rule — explicitly connected to Step 25O.

a_rows_sample.anchor: EmployeeHasRole(John,Architect) ... CanApprove(John,Change) ... RoleRevoked(John) ... conclusion must disappear or become invalid ... NonMonotonic/TemporalInference
a_rows_sample.statement: Worked non-monotonic-reasoning example: a role-based conclusion (CanApprove) must withdraw when the underlying role is later revoked, requiring non-monotonic/temporal inference beyond classical monotonic logic.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Observed: NexusVersion=3.70 ... Derived: SecurityReviewRequired ... DerivedFrom(Evidence,Rules) ... Observation\neq Derivation
a_rows_sample.statement: Distinguishes Observation from Derivation: a derived conclusion is DerivedFrom(Evidence,Rules), not itself another observation.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Conclusion=f(Premises,Rules,Context) ... same inputs and rule versions ... same result ... Deterministic Replay
a_rows_sample.statement: Requires derived-knowledge reproducibility Conclusion=f(Premises,Rules,Context), giving Deterministic Replay for identical inputs/rule versions.

a_rows_sample.anchor: R_1 produced C_1. Later R_2 replaces R_1 ... must not silently recompute history and overwrite C_1 ... Historical derivation is immutable
a_rows_sample.statement: States historical derivation immutability: an old conclusion C1 remains historically valid under R1; a new evaluation under a replacing rule R2 produces a separate C2, never overwriting C1.

b_rows_sample.anchor:
this is where KnowledgeOS could otherwise make its most dangerous mistake: confusing a generated statement with a logically derived statement. ... A_1,\ldots,A_n\vdash_ho A_{n+1} ... Deduction
eq Induction
eq Abduction
eq Calculation
eq Interpretation
b_rows_sample.statement: Frames Step 10's central danger as confusing a generated statement with a logically derived one, requiring the entailment notation A1,...,An⊢_ρ A_{n+1} to accommodate five distinct inference kinds.

b_rows_sample.anchor: First fundamental distinction ... Derivation \Gamma\vdash_\rho P ... Inference \Gamma\xRightarrow{\rho}P ... Generation LLM(\Gamma)\rightarrow P ... These are not equivalent. LLM(\Gamma)\rightarrow P \not\Rightarrow \Gamma\vdash P. This is one of the most important KnowledgeOS invariants.
b_rows_sample.statement: States the core invariant LLM(Γ)→P ⇏ Γ⊢P, distinguishing Derivation (formal rule-following), Inference (probabilistic/defeasible), and Generation (AI-produced statement) as non-equivalent.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The KnowledgeOS Derivation Object ... D=(P,\Gamma,R,M,\Pi,\Sigma,\tau) ... every derived proposition can answer: How did you get this?
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines the Derivation object D=(P,Premises,Rule,Method,Provenance,ResultingState,Validity) so every derived proposition can answer 'how did you get this?'.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Provenance becomes mathematical ... A_1,A_2\vdash A=C ... D1 Conclusion: A = C ... Premises: A1, A2 ... Rule: Transitivity ... Method: Deduction ... DerivedKnowledge = Rule + Premises + Derivation not merely A = C.
b_rows_sample.statement: Worked transitivity-derivation example showing DerivedKnowledge must record Rule+Premises+Derivation, never just the bare conclusion.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Five major inference families ... \mathcal M=\{Deduction,Induction,Abduction,Calculation,Interpretation\}
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines the five-member inference-method family M={Deduction, Induction, Abduction, Calculation, Interpretation}.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Deduction ... Production(x)\rightarrow RequiresBackup(x) therefore RequiresBackup(Nexus). This can be deterministic. ... Deductive inference has a crucial condition: the rule itself must be known and valid. KnowledgeOS therefore needs RuleRegistry. r=(Premises,Conclusion,Context,Version,Authority).
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines Deduction as the strongest deterministic form (worked with a Production⇒RequiresBackup rule), requiring a RuleRegistry with rules r=(Premises,Conclusion,Context,Version,Authority) so Γ⊢_r P is computable — connecting to rules/ADRs/manifestos/governance as sources of explicit inference rules.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Calculation ... Revenue=1000, Cost=700, Profit=300 ... f(1000,700)=300. The result is not an LLM opinion. It is ComputedEvidence with a deterministic provenance chain. ... Mathematical calculation ... C=\sqrt{A^2+B^2}=5. Computation \rightarrow Evidence \rightarrow DerivedAssertion.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines Calculation as deterministic derivation via a formula (revenue-cost example, Pythagorean example), producing ComputedEvidence with a deterministic provenance chain — Computation→Evidence→DerivedAssertion.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Induction ... Nexus_1=3.69, Nexus_2=3.69, Nexus_3=3.69 ... Nexus_{all}=3.69. But that does not follow deductively. Induction produces support, not logical certainty. ... Acquisition=Induced.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines Induction (generalizing from repeated observations, e.g. three Nexus instances all reading 3.69) as producing support, not logical certainty, tagged Acquisition=Induced.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Statistical inference ... \hat\theta=\frac{1}{n}\sum_iX_i ... confidence intervals, posterior distributions, hypothesis tests ... P(\theta\in I) has semantics defined by the statistical method. StatisticalInference\neq DeductiveTruth.
b_rows_sample.statement: Reaffirms StatisticalInference ≠ DeductiveTruth: statistical estimates/intervals have semantics defined by the statistical method, not deductive certainty.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Abduction ... Nexus unavailable. Possible explanations: E1 container stopped, E2 network failure, E3 DNS failure, E4 database failure. KnowledgeOS may rank E_1,E_2,E_3,E_4. But Observation\not\Rightarrow Explanation. Therefore abduction produces Hypotheses rather than facts. ... Hypothesis\neq Asser
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines Abduction (ranking candidate explanations, e.g. four causes of Nexus unavailability) as producing Hypotheses, not facts — Hypothesis ≠ AssertionOfFact, connecting to the earlier Candidate→Supported→Accepted lifecycle.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Interpretation ... This ADR implies that the architecture board intended X. This is not necessarily deduction. It may involve semantic interpretation; contextual understanding; domain knowledge; human intent. LLM(D,C)\rightarrow I but I=Interpretation not I=Fact. It should carry explicit provenance:
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines Interpretation (e.g. inferring an ADR's intent) as distinct from deduction, requiring the result be tagged I=Interpretation, never I=Fact.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Analogy ... This architecture resembles the previously approved pattern. That can be useful for Lord. But Similarity\neqIdentity. Therefore analogy generates a candidate inference, not a deterministic fact.
b_rows_sample.statement: Adds Analogy as a sixth method (similarity-based pattern matching useful to Lord), producing only a candidate inference since Similarity≠Identity.

b_rows_sample.anchor: LLM inference ... LLM(D)\rightarrow P. D_{LLM}=(P,\{D\},LLM,GenerativeInference,\Pi,\Sigma,\tau). This means: An LLM generated proposition P from document D. It does not mean D\vdash P.
b_rows_sample.statement: Formally places LLM output as its own GenerativeInference method producing D_LLM=(P,{D},LLM,GenerativeInference,Π,Σ,τ), never equated with D⊢P.

b_rows_sample.anchor: This solves the AI problem ... The LLM can perform extraction; classification; summarization; interpretation; hypothesis generation; semantic matching; candidate rule discovery; candidate relationship discovery. But KnowledgeOS distinguishes AI Output from Deterministic Derivation.
b_rows_sample.statement: Lists eight legitimate LLM uses (extraction, classification, summarization, interpretation, hypothesis generation, semantic matching, candidate rule/relationship discovery) while insisting AI Output is always kept distinct from Deterministic Derivation.

b_rows_sample.anchor: AI output itself becomes evidence ... e_{LLM} \rightarrow EvidenceAssessment. Its provenance says DerivedFrom(D). LLM output can be evidence, but it is not automatically independent evidence.
b_rows_sample.statement: States LLM output can itself become evidence e_LLM feeding EvidenceAssessment with provenance DerivedFrom(D), but is not automatically independent evidence.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Dependency propagation ... D\rightarrow LLM_1\rightarrow P_1 and then P_1\rightarrow LLM_2\rightarrow P_2. The second output does not become two independent confirmations. The provenance graph preserves D\rightarrow P_1\rightarrow P_2. This connects Step 10 directly to our evidence dependency axioms
b_rows_sample.statement: Traces a two-hop LLM chain (Document→LLM1→P1→LLM2→P2) showing the second output must not be counted as two independent confirmations, connecting to the evidence dependency axioms.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Inference provenance graph ... G_D=(V,E_D) ... nodes include evidence; assertions; rules; calculations; inference results. Edges represent supports; derives-from; contradicts; transforms; supersedes. Then KnowledgeOS can answer: Why does this assertion exist? by traversing P\leftarrow D\leftarrow \G
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines an inference-provenance graph G_D=(V,E_D) with typed node kinds (evidence/assertions/rules/calculations/inference results) and typed edges (supports/derives-from/contradicts/transforms/supersedes), traversable to answer 'why does this assertion exist?'.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Rule types ... Logical rule P,Q\vdash R ... Mathematical rule f(x)=y ... Statistical rule X\sim Distribution ... Domain rule Production software requires owner. ... Governance rule Architecture-relevant change requires architecture review. ... Policy rule Two independent sources required for accepta
b_rows_sample.statement: Classifies six rule types (Logical, Mathematical, Statistical, Domain, Governance, Policy) that must not be confused with one another.

a_rows_sample.anchor: a FOURTH disjoint vocabulary — and the first at PRIMITIVE level
a_rows_sample.statement: New gap G-86: Chapter 13's 'Type System - Solved' section gives seven types (Field, KnowledgeAtma, KnowledgeAtmaSupreme, AppliedKnowledge, plus a partial KnowledgeState) against the ratified eight primitives (Entity, State, Event, Observation, Proposition, Relation, Policy, Action; C-022/step-049, '50 attack classes, no counterexample'); only Observation clearly overlaps (via Prakrti -> Evidence/Observation/Context). Four Gita-only types exist, two of which (K_atma, K_supreme) are RX (refuted). A seven-type ontology missing Action, Policy, Event, Relation and Proposition cannot express admissibility, governance, transitions, or the assertion graph -- assessed as 'not a competing kernel; a different subject'.

a_rows_sample.anchor: the proposal adds three operation names not in any registry
a_rows_sample.statement: Audits S2219's 11 proposed kernel operations (Observe, Discriminate, ..., Contradict, Revise, Supersede, Remember, Forget/Withdraw, Act/Transform) against Step 291's 22-operation registry: Revise/Supersede/Withdraw/Transform are already registered (with 0 bodies/identity/ratification); Discriminate, Remember, Contradict (only Conflict exists as a Sigma axis) are NOT in the 22-operation registry; Qualify is already G1; Observe is a ratified primitive (Observation), not an operation. Concludes the proposal adds three unregistered operation names, confirming the G-83 'prose-only operations' shape recurring and constituting a further G-86-shaped vocabulary; cites Step 291's own ruling that '22 operations CURRENTLY IDENTIFIED' is not the operation universe.

a_rows_sample.anchor: SIX disjoint operation vocabularies in the estate
a_rows_sample.statement: Counts six disjoint operation vocabularies now in the estate: (1) 272A's O_sem, 19 operations; (2) external_research pseudo-algorithm, 43 functions; (3) the corpus registry (256.2/259.7/261.19), 22 operations; (4) Ch13's type ontology, 7 (primitives not operations); (5) Omega_K={Discriminate,Qualify,Transition} + 11 named (artifact 20); (6, new, this batch) {E,R,C,X,Q,Z} from S2226 -- registered as G-91 (was three vocabularies at G-68, four at G-86, now six). Notes Qualify appears in both the fifth and sixth vocabularies (G-92): two independently constructed minimal-ish algebras both contain the one irreducible gap, reinforcing artifact 20's finding that any minimal kernel algebra containing Qualify inherits G1. Also notes both new sources ask about closure/associativity/non-commutativity, matching the corpus's own prior non-law (25J.46: 'we should not yet impose universal commutativity').

a_rows_sample.anchor: Same source chapter. One lane declares three problems solved and a complete framework. The other produces a single inequality and calls it a candidate. The single inequality is the one with content.
a_rows_sample.statement: A controlled comparison (same input chapter, varying only discipline, more rigorous than artifact 19's cross-chapter measurement): the external_research reading of Ch16 (20260831-171736) frames itself as 'Part 3: The Missing Architecture -- Solved', claiming the Integrity Problem, Bias Problem, and Character Problem are each Solved, with Definition/Architecture/Derivation Gap all marked Solved, producing 'The Complete KnowledgeOS Integrity Framework' and 'The Complete Integrity Equation'. The kernel lane (this batch's Ch16 files, 20260901 01:30-01:38) explicitly states the chapter should NOT be converted literally, treats its output as 'another operator candidate' that 'could potentially become an actual KnowledgeOS invariant', and produces exactly one inequality. The single inequality is assessed as the one output with actual content.

b_rows_sample.anchor: All FOUR junctions are ill-typed. The composition is not merely unproven — it does not typecheck anywhere.
b_rows_sample.statement: Precisely diagnoses why Theta_total fails: the five operators are Theta_A:A_t->A_{t+1} (carrier N, the knower), Theta_T:T->T_detached (carrier T, transformations themselves), Theta_K:K_t->K_{t+1} (carrier K), Theta_I:A_t->K_atma (carrier N->K_atma, a different codomain), Theta_X:X_t->X_{t+1} (carrier W, the world). The claimed composition Theta_total = Theta_X o Theta_I o Theta_K o Theta_T o Theta_A requires codomain(f)=domain(g) at four junctions, all ill-typed: Theta_A->Theta_T needs N=T (knower vs transformations); Theta_T->Theta_K needs T=K (transformations vs states); Theta_K->Theta_I needs K=N, but N notin K is ratified (FA-4[E]), so this junction contradicts the lane's own strongest shared finding; Theta_I->Theta_X needs K_atma=W (an identity vs the world). Register upgrade: Theta_total moves from 'RX -- type-check failure across four carriers' to 'RX -- all four composition junctions ill-typed, one against a ratified result' -- a sharper statement of the same verdict, not a new one.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Two ORTHOGONAL classifications of \mathcal O. Crossing them gives a 2-D grid.
b_rows_sample.statement: Discarding the ill-typed composition but keeping the classification: the five Theta operators constitute a CARRIER taxonomy (what an operation acts on: N knower, T transformations, K state, identity, W world), orthogonal to Step 259.7's FUNCTIONAL taxonomy (what an operation does: state-transformations, assessments, governance, audit/history, observation). Since Step 291 established the missing piece is a mandatory-membership rule (not an enumeration), and a rule on one axis cannot see distinctions on the other, this sharpens gap N-4: the membership rule needs two indices. Example cells: Withdraw (functional: state-transformation, carrier: K, currently in registry); Authorize (functional: governance, carrier: unstated -- acts on N or W?); TraceOrigin (functional: observation, carrier: provenance, unregistered per 291 sec02); Theta_T-like (no functional class fits, carrier T, not in any registry). Explicitly: this sharpens N-4, it does not solve it; no membership is proposed.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Is \mathcal O closed under operations that take operations as arguments? The corpus has never asked.
b_rows_sample.statement: New gap G-93: Theta_T:T->T_detached is a transformation of a transformation (higher-order); nothing in Step 259.7's five functional kinds, the 22-operation registry, or Step 291's nine closure senses is higher-order, so the corpus has never asked whether O is closed under higher-order operations. But the corpus already contains a live instance unrecognised as such: Vairagya/Karma-phala-tyaga is T->T_detached, recorded as R6 via invariant I-V ('no Admissible conjunct reads the outcome'); I-V is a constraint ON a transformation, i.e. a higher-order predicate -- so the corpus already reasons about T at second order without having declared O admits it. This is not a philosophical import; the corpus's own I-V forces the question. The operation-membership rule N-4 must decide whether O contains higher-order operations.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Three independent sources converge on a ~5-slot decomposition of an operation
b_rows_sample.statement: Discards Ch18's (18.13-18) five-factor action mapping (Divine->K_atma is RX; Body->K_t misreads the state as an instrument) but keeps the arity and slot roles, finding a three-source convergence on a ~5-slot operation decomposition: Ch18 (instrument, doer, means/senses, endeavour, enabling source); H-290-1/Ch5 (intended act, acting subject, instruments, context, resulting transformation); and Step 259.7's own signature Authorize:Actor x Action x Policy -> Decision, which already contains 'doer' and 'enabling condition' slots. Two of the five slots are already present in an existing corpus signature -- assessed as completing a pattern the corpus started, not an import. Gives operation identity a SHAPE (id(o) over doer/instrument/means/endeavour/enabling-condition), addressing Step 291's finding that operation identity is OPEN (0 of 22), but not a RULE: which slots are identity-bearing is exactly Step 258.20's question (OperationalIdentity(x) iff exists T in T: changing id(x) changes T(K,c)), which quantifies over the unenumerated T, the same blocker. Registered O-Q1: T4-SHAPE, correctly shaped but unpopulated, like K=(K_t,Omega_K,I) in artifact 20; not promoted.

b_rows_sample.anchor: ZERO gaps discharged. TWO sharpened, ONE shaped. That is the honest yield, and it is not nothing.
b_rows_sample.statement: Updated gap-register optimization: of N-4 (membership), operation identity, equiv (minimal cut), Qualify (G1), delta (commit case), the metric (M-Q3prime), (Omega,F,P) (G-22), and canonical K -- none is discharged; N-4 and operation identity are sharpened/shaped; the rest unchanged or worsened by inspection (e.g. K_supreme=sup(Omega) presupposes a nonexistent order per artifact 19's E1; K=f(F,A_t) already refused per artifact 18). Confirms artifact 18's finding from the opposite direction: the Gita is rich in distinctions and empty of carriers; every gap in the register is a membership/procedure/carrier question, while every contribution this lane makes is a distinction -- distinctions sharpen questions, only carriers close them. Explicitly did not edit/correct/supersede any external_research artifact (a registry act per artifact 19), did not propose O-Q1/O-Q2 as architecture, and confirms Steps 288-291 remain unchanged, all R6.

b_rows_sample.anchor: the type-checking lane produced the usable result — and it is the one that claims less.
b_rows_sample.statement: Decisive contrast with artifact 22: the external_research Theta_total (5 operators) has 4 of 4 junctions ill-typed and flattens Sigma to 3 modes while self-declaring 'Complete'; this lane's composition (3 operators: Z:K_t->G_t, delta:(K_t,G_t,E_t,C_t)->D_t, tau:(K_t,D_t)->K_{t+1}, i.e. tau o delta o Z) has 0 of its junctions ill-typed, respects the ratified 5-axis Sigma, and self-declares 'must not yet be declared canonical'. Same source material, opposite discipline; the type-checking lane produced the usable result and is the one that claims less. Explicitly flags that type-correct is not the same as instantiable (developed further in sec5).
