b_rows_sample.statement: Distinguishes Zero from sufficiency/adequacy (built read-disjoint and measured independent per document 07) so a design reaching for Zero when it wants sufficiency will delete the wrong things.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Zero fails in both directions between the element level and the set level. It is therefore not an irrelevance relation in the graphoid sense ... [x,x] ... redundancy ... [+c,-c] ... emergent eliminability
b_rows_sample.statement: States that Zero fails both graphoid-axiom directions (composition: 131 violations; decomposition: 63 violations), with the two canonical counterexample shapes named as the whole concept: [x,x] (redundancy, a composition failure) and [+c,-c] (emergent eliminability under a cancelling contract, a decomposition failure).

b_rows_sample.anchor: A - Eliminated \equiv C in 1182/1182 -- exactly ... B is a different object. The transformation residual is not what the contract leaves unresolved.
b_rows_sample.statement: States the Remainder trichotomy's exact positive identity: 'not eliminated' equals exactly 'contract-relevant unresolved material' without exception in 1182/1182 tested cases, while the transformation residual (B) is a genuinely different object, separating the residue of the operation from the residue of the concern.

b_rows_sample.anchor: One elimination in six is blocked by boundary information alone ... the rule-based and counterfactual notions of eliminability agree only 55.75% of the time ... 1559 elements the rule would remove are not Zero, against 301 that are Zero but the rule keeps.
b_rows_sample.statement: Reports the asymmetric-bias finding as a concept-level warning: a rule-over-field-types eliminability heuristic is wrong far more often in the dangerous over-elimination direction than the safe direction, so eliminability must never be implemented as such a rule.

b_rows_sample.anchor: L is not a projection and not an interior operator. It is a terminating, non-confluent rewriting process. ... Which normal form you reach depends on the order you eliminate in.
b_rows_sample.statement: Establishes that repeated-elimination L is reductive, terminating and iteration-monotone-decreasing but non-confluent (11/1162 non-commuting) and only operator-relative idempotent; concludes 'eliminate everything eliminable' names no unique object unless an order is fixed and declared.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Is there a well-defined group/set formulation of Zero? OPEN -- H5+H6 show the element-wise formulation fails in both directions; they do not supply the replacement. This is the deepest open question about the concept.
b_rows_sample.statement: Names the deepest unresolved question about the Zero concept: no replacement group/set formulation exists even though the element-wise one is refuted in both directions; also leaves L's monotonicity, k>3 higher-order eliminability, and semantic equivalence explicitly open.

b_rows_sample.anchor: A representation R=T(D) realizes Q under decoder O iff O(R)=Q(D). ... O is fixed in advance, as part of the inquiry frame. ... If O may be chosen after seeing R, then "realization" is just adequacy restated.
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines Realization with the decoder O fixed in advance as part of the inquiry frame, stating that fixing is the entire content of the definition -- a claim about the decoder you actually have, not the existence of one.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Adequate \land \neg C(R) \Rightarrow not realizable, though the information is present. ... This is why C belongs in the frame and not in the transformation.
b_rows_sample.statement: Distinguishes Adequacy (does R determine Q, an existential/population-level question) from Realization (does this fixed decoder recover Q, a per-case question), showing they diverge for two independent reasons: a weaker-than-needed decoder, or a failing use-time constraint C.

b_rows_sample.anchor: KR-REP-REDUCTION's design failed to operationalize the adequacy/realization separation. ... the only adequate level, R5, has F=1.0000. ... this experiment could not exhibit it, and no experiment yet has.
b_rows_sample.statement: Names a specific design defect: the chain's transformations never dropped a record so C could never fail, and the decoder was strong enough at the one adequate level, so the experiment excluded its own target case by construction -- the separation is real by definition but was never exhibited.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Realization \Rightarrow Adequacy. ... What would refute it: a case set on which O(T(D))=Q(D) holds throughout while the fiber is Q-heterogeneous ... Not tested.
b_rows_sample.statement: States the one open conjecture in the document with an explicit refutation condition (a decoder right by luck on observed cases without being determined by R), noting the converse (Adequacy=>Realization) is already refuted.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Last adequate stage: R5. First inadequate: R4. Crossing transformation: T4 -- rounding to 3 significant digits. ... TEST reproduces TRAIN closely
b_rows_sample.statement: Reports the located adequacy boundary (R5 adequate at Hhat=0, R4 inadequate at Hhat=0.4299) reproduced closely on an independent test split (0.4408 vs 0.4299), confirming it is not a one-sample artifact.

b_rows_sample.anchor: We may NOT say: "Three significant digits is the universal preservation limit." We may say: for this carrier, this inquiry Q, this transformation chain, this contract and this value domain, rounding ... crossed the observed preservation boundary.
b_rows_sample.statement: States the scope-bound discipline the whole result exists to teach: the boundary is a property of the inquiry frame (carrier, Q, chain, contract, value domain), not a universal numeric limit; by the DPI corollary the boundary is unique and cannot be re-crossed back into adequacy along the sequential chain.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The Zero rate at the boundary crossing is not distinguishable from the rate at a non-crossing step, and is in fact lower. Eliminability carries no signal about where preservation fails.
b_rows_sample.statement: Reports the direct test of hypothesis H-RR2 (Zero marks the adequacy boundary): refuted -- the Zero rate at the actual boundary crossing (0.0377) is not higher than, and is in fact lower than, the rate at a non-crossing step (0.0426).

b_rows_sample.anchor: Rank conventions are NOT invertible. desc \neq (n+1) - asc when values tie -- 21369 violations ... this is NOT an instance of DECISION-01 ... The headline built on it was withdrawn -- both my wording and the review's replacement wording.
b_rows_sample.statement: Records an explicit retraction: a prior claim that a rank-direction finding instantiated DECISION-01 (non-evidential invariance) required an invertible recoding between rank conventions, which the audit refuted (21,369 tie violations); both the original and the review's replacement wording are withdrawn, though the underlying adequacy/realization sensitivity gap survives as the one place that distinction was visible at all.

group_evidence.why_grouped: explicit agent-stated uncertainty: 'theory-v1-2-fifteen-document-set-2026-09' POSSIBLY relates to 'knowledgeos-information-transformation-theory-consolidated-draft-2026-09' (batch B0065). Note: A structured 15-document (Document 00 through 14) KnowledgeOS Theory v1.2 write-up dated 2026-09-04, organizationally distinct from the earlier 50-section consolidated draft (knowledgeos-information-transformation-theory-consolidated-draft-2026-09) though covering overlapping Zero/adequacy/realization/representation-reduction ground -- flagged POSSIBLY the same underlying theory-writing effort pending confirmation. This batch (B0065) contributes four of the fifteen: Document 03a (the concept of Zero -- distinguishes Zero from sufficiency/adequacy, from invariance, from graphoid-style conditional-irrelevance (fails both composition and decomposition), and from an independence system/matroid; states the exact Remainder identity A==C in 1182/1182 cases with B a different object; documents the elimination process L as terminating but non-confluent; and records higher-order eliminability up to k=3 for n<=6); Document 05 (Realization vs Adequacy formally separated, but the separation was never experimentally exhibited -- a named design defect in KR-REP-REDUCTION -- with one open conjecture Realization=>Adequacy); Document 06 (the R5->R4 rounding-to-3-significant-figures representation-adequacy boundary, explicitly scope-bound to one carrier/inquiry/chain/contract; Zero does NOT mark the boundary; a prior rank-convention/DECISION-01 claim is explicitly withdrawn after the audit found rank conventions are not invertible under ties); and Document 12 (a DDD strategic architecture model over the Zero/adequacy/realization kernel research -- five candidate bounded contexts, a constitutional read-disjointness invariant no single context can own, an Evidence & Contradiction context with unresolved ownership blocked on DECISION-02, aggregate/event/port design forced by the data, and eight named anti-patterns).

a_rows_sample.anchor: The kernel creates the ecosystem; the company creates value around the ecosystem.
a_rows_sample.statement: Uses the Linux/Red Hat precedent to argue KnowledgeOS's moat is the kernel plus governance plus evidence model (not the AI model, which is commoditized), proposing a Community/Professional/Enterprise revenue-tier structure and a 10-year IPO roadmap.

a_rows_sample.anchor: KnowledgeOS Kernel = the minimal system responsible for creating, identifying, relating, governing, and preserving organizational knowledge objects.
a_rows_sample.statement: The proposed load-bearing definition of the 'KnowledgeOS Kernel', explicitly modeled after the Linux kernel's separation from applications: the kernel provides knowledge primitives (Identity, Lifecycle, Evidence, Authority) and must not know about specific technologies (SAP, Kubernetes, Jira).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Linus did not start by designing 'the operating system of the world.' He started by solving a concrete problem, created a small working kernel ... 'Can we create a trusted kernel that allows digitalization robots to operate safely?'
a_rows_sample.statement: Argues KnowledgeOS should not start with an AI-driven Digitalization Robot ambition; the correct starting question is the smallest trusted kernel that later allows robots to operate safely, mirroring Linux's incremental 0.01-kernel-first history.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Open-source the KnowledgeOS Kernel. Commercialize the Digitalization Robot Platform.
a_rows_sample.statement: Recommends an open-core business model (open KnowledgeOS Kernel for trust/ecosystem, commercial Digitalization Robot/Enterprise Platform for revenue), by analogy with Linux Kernel vs Red Hat Enterprise Linux.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Linux manages computer resources. KnowledgeOS manages organizational intelligence resources ... which knowledge is valid, who owns it, and how can it be trusted?
a_rows_sample.statement: States the deepest claimed difference between the Linux and KnowledgeOS kernel analogies: Linux answers 'which process can access which resource', while KnowledgeOS must answer 'which knowledge is valid, who owns it, and how can it be trusted.'

a_rows_sample.anchor: Rust for the KnowledgeOS Kernel, Kotlin/Spring for the Enterprise Runtime, Python for Intelligence, TypeScript for Experience.
a_rows_sample.statement: Recommends a multi-language technology stack (Rust kernel for memory-safety/correctness, Kotlin+Spring Boot enterprise runtime, Python intelligence layer, TypeScript studio/frontend) with an estimated 12-18 month timeline for a first Kernel v1.0 with a small expert team.

a_rows_sample.anchor: If you want IPO potential, do not position KnowledgeOS as 'AI chatbot' ... nor 'Documentation tool' ... Position as: The operating system for enterprise knowledge and digital transformation.
a_rows_sample.statement: Argues the commercial positioning category determines addressable market size; 'AI chatbot' is too easy to copy, 'documentation tool' is too small a category for IPO ambitions.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Kernel scope: 'minimal kernel, no AI' (S0167) vs the platform vision where an AI-driven Digitalization Robot is the top layer (S0171) — the corpus itself frames the robot as a distribution, keeping the kernel AI-free, so the tension is scope of the 'core' vs the 'product'.
a_rows_sample.statement: Surfaces T1: a minimal AI-free kernel proposal versus an AI-driven robot as the platform's top execution layer, resolved by the corpus's own framing (robot = distribution, kernel stays AI-free) but not formally decided.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Rust · Spring Boot · Gradle/Cargo · microservices · plugin architecture · Event Sourcing · Kafka are recommendations/hypotheses in the corpus, never adopted KnowledgeOS technology.
a_rows_sample.statement: Explicit preservation note keeping every named technology recommendation level-tagged as a hypothesis, never promoted to adopted architecture, while noting the existing PHP/Laravel + TypeScript/Vue platform is the ESTABLISHED current stack.

a_rows_sample.anchor: DI principle vs framework import: adopt the DI/composition-root principle without adopting Spring — the corpus wants the first, but the kernel file pairs the principle with the Spring runtime.
a_rows_sample.statement: Surfaces T4: the DI-principle proposal explicitly wants the principle without the Spring framework, yet the kernel-technology brainstorm pairs the same principle with a recommended Spring/Kotlin runtime.

a_rows_sample.anchor: KNOWLEDGEOS KERNEL protects: identity · evidence · provenance · lifecycle · authority · invariants · temporal state / higher layers provide: assurance · analytics · inference · simulation · AI · visualization · delivery ... a PROPOSED KERNEL BOUNDARY CANDIDATE, outline supported, provenance+temporal weak.
a_rows_sample.statement: H-10: tests the seven-concern kernel/higher-layer split against all three baselines per-concern; identity, evidence, lifecycle, authority, and invariants are supported, provenance and temporal state are weak, so the overall split is a candidate outline, not an established fact.

a_rows_sample.anchor: WHAT IS THE CORE DOMAIN ACT? ... Verification | Admission | Determination | Transformation | Epistemic Maintenance | Justification Preservation | Constitutional Transition
a_rows_sample.statement: Seven alternative formulations of KnowledgeOS's core domain act are compared (Verification, Admission, Determination, Transformation, Epistemic Maintenance, Justification Preservation, Constitutional Transition), each with its domain-meaning implication.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The core domain act is the constitutionally-gated transition from candidate to admissible knowledge state.
a_rows_sample.statement: Hypothesis: the Kernel's core domain act is the constitutionally-gated transition from candidate to admissible knowledge state, combining a candidate, a gate (constitutional rules), a verdict (admissibility), and a state change.

a_rows_sample.anchor: A knowledge claim cannot exist without: identity, evidence, justification, epistemic state, confidence, and history.
a_rows_sample.statement: Proposed aggregate invariant: a knowledge claim cannot exist without identity, evidence, justification, epistemic state, confidence, and history all present and consistent together; the Kernel is framed as 'the guardian of this aggregate invariant.'

a_rows_sample.anchor: Candidate -> Verification -> Admissibility -> Identity -> Epistemic State -> Knowledge
a_rows_sample.statement: Admission is modelled as a distinction chain (Candidate -> Verification[well-formed?] -> Admissibility[constitution?] -> Identity[stable anchor?] -> Epistemic State -> Knowledge) and as an 8-step process from candidate proposal to emission of KnowledgeCreated.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Identity assignment | ESSENTIAL ... Semantic interpretation | NOT ESSENTIAL ... Reasoning | NOT ESSENTIAL ... Workflow | NOT ESSENTIAL ... Projection | NOT ESSENTIAL
a_rows_sample.statement: A capability table classifies identity assignment, evidence admission, justification preservation, epistemic-state determination, confidence assignment, history recording, and constitutional evaluation as ESSENTIAL (each tied to a named invariant); candidate verification as SUPPORTING; and semantic interpretation, reasoning, workflow, and projection as NOT ESSENTIAL to the Kernel's minimum domain capacity.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Natural-language interpretation | Parsing | Normalization | Canonicalization | Reasoning | Candidate generation | Retrieval | Search | Ranking | Model inference | Orchestration | Workflow | Projection | UI | Infrastructure | Evidence acquisition
a_rows_sample.statement: A 15-item table enumerates responsibilities that belong OUTSIDE the Kernel, each with a DDD reason: natural-language interpretation, parsing, normalization, canonicalization, reasoning, candidate generation, retrieval, search, ranking, model inference, orchestration, workflow, projection, UI, infrastructure, and evidence acquisition -- summarized as the principle that the Kernel is representation-agnostic and does not perform semantic interpretation.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The Kernel is a domain boundary, not a component.
a_rows_sample.statement: Six candidate interpretations of what the Kernel 'is' are compared (aggregate boundary, domain decision boundary, admission boundary, consistency boundary, constitutional boundary, small domain core inside the aggregate); concludes the Kernel is best understood as the admission boundary + consistency boundary -- a conceptual domain boundary, not an implementation component, though it may be implemented inside the aggregate.

a_rows_sample.anchor: KnowledgeCreated is the domain event that signals the completion of admission.
a_rows_sample.statement: KnowledgeCreated is analyzed as the domain event signalling completion of admission -- the business moment the candidate becomes part of KnowledgeOS with identity, evidence, justification, epistemic state, confidence, and history all established; the Kernel's job is to produce this event on success and nothing/a rejection on failure.

a_rows_sample.anchor: KnowledgeOS is a governed knowledge-admission system.
a_rows_sample.statement: Four formulations of the knowledge/evidence relationship are compared (evidence registry, justified epistemic-state system, governed knowledge-admission system, constitutional knowledge machine); 'governed knowledge-admission system' is judged best supported -- evidence supports knowledge, knowledge requires evidence, evidence is admitted and preserved alongside knowledge, but evidence is not itself knowledge.

b_rows_sample.anchor: the adjudicated Kernel recorded precisely enough to be attackable — extent, contents, refusals, and the tests, each with the ruling that fixed it
b_rows_sample.statement: A second, separate research corpus (referenced but not detailed here) is confirmed sealed until the formal K-1 adjudication is finished, with its purpose being to attack the result rather than help manufacture it; a precondition is stated for that later falsification phase: the adjudicated Kernel must be recorded precisely enough to be attackable (extent, contents, refusals, and tests, each with the ruling that fixed it), since a falsification pass against a loosely-recorded boundary produces disagreement about whether it holds rather than useful findings -- work explicitly deferred to a post-adjudication consolidation step before the philosophical lenses (i.e. this batch's S0403 onward material) are brought to bear.

b_aliases: Wave 1 Kernel extent vs contents adjudication status

group_evidence.why_grouped: explicit agent-stated uncertainty: 'kos-kernel-adjudication-wave1-extent-contents' POSSIBLY relates to 'knowledgeos-kernel-concept' (batch B0011). Note: S0432's status update on a separate, formal K-1 Kernel-boundary adjudication process (KnowledgeAggregate + ConflictRecord with a Verification Port as sole inbound gate), introducing an extent-vs-contents distinction and confirming that a sealed second corpus (referred to as 'the lenses') -- plausibly this batch's own S0403-S0426 philosophical-lens material -- is held back for post-adjudication falsification rather than adjudication input. Relationship to knowledgeos-kernel-concept (B0005) and to the batch's own philosophical kernel proposals is unresolved.

a_rows_sample.anchor: An assertion contains a proposition. That does not mean P subset A. ... Containment \neq Set Inclusion ... P \xrightarrow{embedded in} A \xrightarrow{member of} K_t
a_rows_sample.statement: Rejects the K_P subset K_A subset K_J subset K_t subset Omega chain as a category error: propositions, assertions and knowledge states are different types of object, and containment (a proposition being embedded in an assertion) is not the same relation as set inclusion (an assertion being a member of a knowledge state's assertion set); replaces it with a typed composition chain (embedded-in / member-of / subset-of).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Instead of A=(P,Sigma,E,tau,Pi), use Supports(E,A) or EvidenceRelation(E,A,r) where r in {supports,contradicts,qualifies,weakens,contextualizes}
a_rows_sample.statement: Proposes moving Evidence out of the Assertion tuple into an explicit typed relation (Supports/Contradicts/Qualifies/Weakens/Contextualizes between Evidence and Assertion) rather than embedding it as a field, since one assertion may be supported or contradicted by several distinct evidence items with different relation types.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Zero and Lord should not be components of Knowledge... Zero is an operation: Zero: K -> Z. Lord is an operation: Lord: K -> L.
a_rows_sample.statement: Reaffirms and generalizes the earlier circularity concern (from S0784): Zero and Lord must be typed as operations Zero:K->Z and Lord:K->L over the Knowledge State type K, never as stored fields of K itself; their outputs may be persisted as derived artifacts but are not foundational components of knowledge.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Entity | Dimension | Value | Proposition | Evidence | Epistemic State | Assertion | Relationship | Knowledge State | Knowledge Space ... a type system defines: what kinds of objects exist, what properties each has, how types relate, what operations are valid
a_rows_sample.statement: Answers the posed Question 7A by producing a complete ten-type system for KnowledgeOS (Entity, Dimension, Value, Proposition, Evidence, EpistemicState, Assertion, Relationship, KnowledgeState, KnowledgeSpace) with formal set-builder definitions, a type hierarchy diagram, per-type well-formedness constraints, and operation signatures (Zero/Lord/Sarathi/Compare/Challenge/Update/Preserve, all typed as maps between these object types).

a_rows_sample.anchor: WellTyped(K) = WellTypedObjects(K) and WellTypedRelationships(K) and ValidCardinalities(K) ... Supports(Evidence,Assertion) valid; Supports(Person,Assertion) invalid
a_rows_sample.statement: Corrects WellTyped from a pure object-typing predicate to also require relationship typing and cardinality validity (e.g. Supports must relate Evidence to Assertion, not Person to Assertion), since syntactically valid objects can still violate relationship-type rules.

a_rows_sample.anchor: U = {E, D, V, P, A, R, E_v, Sigma, H, Z, L, K, I} ... this ontology is the foundation for all KnowledgeOS operations.
a_rows_sample.statement: Proposes a 13-type universe (Entity, Dimension, Value, Proposition, Assertion, Relationship, Evidence, EpistemicState, History, ZeroFinding, LordCandidate, KnowledgeState, IdealState) with formal set-builder definitions, well-formedness predicates for Proposition/Assertion/Relationship, and an explicit epistemic lattice claim over the 2240-state Sigma space.

a_rows_sample.anchor: You later define Relationship separately... Relationship in Entity and Relationship in Relationship could become possible. Entity != Relationship.
a_rows_sample.statement: Corrects the Entity definition (which included 'relationship' as an example subject) for creating an ontological ambiguity where a Relationship could also be typed as an Entity; a relationship may become the subject of a proposition without itself being classified as an Entity.

a_rows_sample.anchor: P=(E,D,V) ... too restrictive for the complete KnowledgeOS theory ... doesn't naturally represent 'Bhishma supports the Kaurava side' or 'Assertion A contradicts Assertion B' or 'Evidence E supports Assertion A' ... P=(S,rho,O,Gamma) ... AttributeProposition subset Proposition
a_rows_sample.statement: Corrects the Entity+Dimension+Value proposition model as too narrow to represent relational/meta propositions (assertion-contradicts-assertion, evidence-supports-assertion); generalizes Proposition to a subject-predicate-object-qualifiers form P=(S,rho,O,Gamma), with the earlier attribute proposition recovered as the special case rho=hasDimension, so AttributeProposition becomes a subtype of Proposition rather than the whole of it.

a_rows_sample.anchor: To call something a lattice mathematically, you need a partial order such that every pair has lub and glb. You haven't defined that... Replace Transition Lattice with Epistemic State Space or Epistemic Transition System.
a_rows_sample.statement: Rejects the claim that the epistemic state space (Sigma=A x S x R x V x C with a proposed preceq order) forms a mathematical lattice, since the required least-upper-bound/greatest-lower-bound structure was never established and the Resolution component (Open/InProgress/Resolved/Unresolvable) is not naturally ordered; downgrades the claim to an unstructured product state space pending proof of any lattice properties.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Supports(E_v,P) in [-1,1] ... epistemically dangerous... I recommend replacing the primitive scalar with Bearing(E,P) in {Support,Contradict,Neutral,Irrelevant,Unknown} and separately Strength(E,P) in [0,1].
a_rows_sample.statement: Rejects the signed [-1,1] evidence-support scalar (0 could mean neutral, irrelevant, insufficient, unknown, or not-assessed -- these are not equivalent), replacing it with a categorical Bearing (Support/Contradict/Neutral/Irrelevant/Unknown) plus an optional separate numeric Strength.

a_rows_sample.anchor: An Assertion without evidence must be representable, otherwise Zero cannot represent a missing-evidence condition... Evidence(A) subseteq E_v and |Evidence(A)| >= 0.
a_rows_sample.statement: Corrects the Assertion well-formedness rule that required a non-empty Evidence field, which would make MissingEvidence (an established Gap type) unrepresentable; an assertion's Evidence set must be allowed to be empty.

a_rows_sample.anchor: You use ~ for both Consistent (line 480) and Normative Conflict (line 488). That is unacceptable in a formal theory... A1 => A2 as causal... but => is conventionally logical implication. Causation != LogicalEntailment.
a_rows_sample.statement: Flags an actual notation error (the symbol ~ used for two different relationship types, Consistent and Normative Conflict, in the same table) and a symbol-overload error (=> used for causal implication when it conventionally denotes logical implication), recommending distinct notations and the explicit invariant Causation != LogicalEntailment.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Content != EpistemicStatus != Evaluation ... Ontology -> Formal Semantics -> State Model -> Evaluation Algebra -> DDD Model -> Implementation, not Graph Schema -> Call it Ontology.
a_rows_sample.statement: States the batch's summary methodological principle: Content, Epistemic Status, and Evaluation are three different mathematical objects that must never be collapsed, and warns against letting a convenient implementation/graph-database representation silently substitute for genuine formal ontology work (Ontology->Semantics->StateModel->EvaluationAlgebra->DDD->Implementation, never the reverse).

b_rows_sample.anchor: Proposition | A meaningful statement that can be true or false. | P=(Entity,Dimension,Value) ... Assertion | A proposition put forward as true, with a specific epistemic status... Knowledge | An assertion that satisfies the epistemic criteria for knowledge (justified true belief)
b_rows_sample.statement: Splits the Knowledge Atom into a three-level hierarchy Proposition subset-of Assertion subset-of Knowledge: Proposition=(E,D,V) is content without commitment; Assertion=(P,Sigma,Evidence,tau,Provenance) is a proposition put forward as true; Knowledge=(A,Justification,True) is a justified-true assertion; corrects the earlier Knowledge Atom to actually be an Assertion, not raw Knowledge.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Who determines True? KnowledgeOS observes, reconstructs, compares, challenges and guides. It generally cannot access Truth itself... Truth \neq Truth Assessment
b_rows_sample.statement: Rejects making absolute Truth an internal primitive of Knowledge, since KnowledgeOS cannot access Truth directly; replaces the three-level model with four levels (Proposition -> Assertion -> Epistemically Accepted -> Reality/Omega), where 'Knowledge' becomes K=(A,Justification,TruthAssessment) rather than requiring literal correspondence to reality.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Observation \rightarrow Candidate Proposition(s) ... because an observation can be ambiguous. ... 'Host responds on port 8081' -> P1/P2/P3
b_rows_sample.statement: Corrects 'Observe -> Proposition' to 'Observation -> Candidate Proposition(s)', since one observation (e.g. a host responding on a port) can support multiple distinct, non-exclusive candidate propositions requiring Zero/Lord/Semantic-Reconstruction to disambiguate.

b_rows_sample.anchor: K_t = \mathcal{E}_t(\mathcal{A}_t) ... Knowledge isn't necessarily one object. It is a state of knowledge over many propositions and assertions.
b_rows_sample.statement: Reframes Knowledge from a single giant tuple to a Knowledge State K_t = E_t(A_t), an epistemic evaluation function over the set of currently available assertions A_t, foreshadowing K_{t+1}=Update(K_t,Observation_t,Zero_t,Lord_t,Evidence_t).

b_rows_sample.anchor: X_t \rightarrow O_t \rightarrow R_t \rightarrow A_t \rightarrow K_t
b_rows_sample.statement: Corrects the too-simple Reality->Observation->Knowledge pipeline into X_t (domain/reality) -> O_t (observation) -> R_t (semantic reconstruction/interpretation) -> A_t (assertion) -> K_t (knowledge state), with the critical point Observation ≠ Interpretation ≠ Assertion ≠ Knowledge, illustrated with the Bhīṣma example (seeing him = observation; 'Bhīṣma is a person' = interpretation; 'Bhīṣma is Arjuna's grandfather' = assertion; the same claim with provenance and epistemic qualification = knowledge).

b_rows_sample.anchor: P = \text{a semantically evaluable claim about entities, relationships, states or events}
b_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes Proposition as a semantically evaluable claim (examples: IsOnBattlefield(Bhishma), GrandfatherOf(Bhishma,Arjuna), OpponentOf(Bhishma,Arjuna)), distinguished from Assertion: Proposition ≠ Assertion, and Assertion = Proposition + Epistemic Qualification + Provenance. Flagged as a distinction that 'should be frozen'.

b_rows_sample.anchor: A_3 = Inference( A_1,A_2,\ldots, Rule, Assumptions, Provenance )
b_rows_sample.statement: Extends Infer(A_1,A_2,Rule)->A_3 to require every derived assertion to carry Rule, Assumptions, and Provenance so KnowledgeOS can explain 'why do you believe this?': every derived assertion traceable to source assertions + inference rule + assumptions + context, called essential for deterministic assurance.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Document \neq Knowledge
b_rows_sample.statement: Rejects the naive Documents->Chunk->Embedding->VectorDB->RAG->LLM architecture as 'not KnowledgeOS' because it bypasses the epistemic model: a document is not knowledge but an information-bearing source from which observations/assertions may be constructed — Document ≠ Knowledge, Document ≠ Evidence — illustrated by Document->Observation->Candidate Assertion->Evidence->Knowledge State.

b_rows_sample.anchor: LLM\ Output \neq Knowledge
b_rows_sample.statement: Names three constitutional invariants for sources: (1) Source ≠ Knowledge (Document/API Response/Git Repository ≠ Knowledge); (2) LLM Output ≠ Knowledge — LLM Output -> Candidate Interpretation -> Epistemic Processing -> Knowledge; (3) Retrieval ≠ Knowledge Creation — Retrieve(Q) -> EvidenceCandidates -> Evaluate -> Knowledge. Overarching principle: 'Sources provide information; KnowledgeOS constructs governed knowledge from it. LLMs interpret; KnowledgeOS evaluates and governs. Retrieval supplies evidence candidates; it does not automatically create knowledge.'

b_rows_sample.anchor: Interpret: Observation \times Context \rightarrow CandidateMeaning
b_rows_sample.statement: Interpret:Observation×Context->CandidateMeaning is where the structural parser, semantic parser, domain model, and LLM participate, worked through 'those with whom I have to fight' -> structural parsing -> semantic parsing -> candidate semantic structure -> candidate dimensions {Actor,Target,Action,Relationship,Obligation,Context} — explicitly 'not yet accepted knowledge'. CandidateAssertion=(Proposition,Sources,Interpretation,Context), e.g. 'Bhīṣma is Arjuna's grandfather' becomes a candidate proposition via Interpret->CandidateAssertions.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Assess: CandidateAssertion \times Evidence \times Rules \times Context \rightarrow EpistemicAssessment
b_rows_sample.statement: Assess:CandidateAssertion×Evidence×Rules×Context->EpistemicAssessment produces Σ_A=(Acquisition,Support,Uncertainty,Validity) per explicit policy, contrasting e.g. (Acquisition=Reported,Support=Moderate,Uncertainty=Moderate,Validity=Current) against (Acquisition=AI-Generated,Support=None,Uncertainty=High,Validity=Unknown) depending on what actually supports the proposition. CandidateAssertion --Assessment--> Assertion=(P,E,Σ,Π,τ,C,ID); K_{t+1}=δ(K_t,A). Full acquisition chain: X->Artifact->Observation->Interpretation->CandidateAssertion->Assessment->Assertion->K_{t+1}, stated to be 'already a computable architecture'.

b_rows_sample.anchor: \mathcal P = \mathcal P_F \cup \mathcal P_N \cup \mathcal P_Q \cup \mathcal P_H \cup \mathcal P_I \ldots
b_rows_sample.statement: After ten tests, provisionally establishes 'Source Observation is computationally realizable' across documents, DB results, internet resources, human statements, LLM outputs, code, rules, ADRs, constitutions and instructions, preserving Source event ≠ Meaning ≠ Assertion. Surfaces two explicit unresolved theoretical points without deciding them: Open Point A — whether one Proposition abstraction P_F∪P_N∪P_Q∪P_H∪P_I∪... (factual/normative/definitional/instructional/question/hypothesis/interpretation) with an explicit semantic type suffices, versus needing genuinely distinct object types; Open Point B — whether the Observation model should stay unified (with acquisition method/type recording measurement vs statement vs database vs LLM etc.) rather than creating separate Observation concepts per source class.

b_rows_sample.anchor: one Proposition abstraction, with explicit semantic type.
b_rows_sample.statement: Poses two explicit architectural-fork questions to the domain authority rather than deciding unilaterally: Question 1 — should factual/normative/definitional/instructional/hypothetical/interrogative content be different TYPES of semantic proposition under one common Proposition abstraction (recommended: Yes — one Proposition abstraction with explicit semantic type, rather than unrelated objects)? Question 2 — should the observation model stay unified, with acquisition method/type recording whether it came from measurement/database/document/human/LLM/API/parser (recommended: Yes)? If both are agreed, proposes formally closing Observation and moving to 'Computational Closure 2 — Interpretation', testing whether parsing+ontology+rules+LLM+human interpretation can transform arbitrary source observations into candidate semantic structures 'without pretending that interpretation is truth'.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Should KnowledgeOS be allowed to create an Assertion with an explicitly unresolved epistemic state
b_rows_sample.statement: Poses and then answers the pivotal admission-boundary design choice: should an Assertion require passing a minimum admission threshold, or may it hold an explicitly unresolved epistemic state (Unknown/Hypothesized/WeaklySupported)? Recommends and then (in a 'Domain Authority' voice) DECIDES the latter: Assertion ≠ Proven Truth. Rationale given for rejecting the threshold alternative: it would remove Zero's ability to detect gaps (no representation for Unknown/Hypothesized), remove Lord's ability to generate candidates (no place for them to reside), sever the Observation->Interpretation->Candidate->Assertion provenance chain, damage auditability (no record of 'what we considered but did not accept'), make the incomplete-question problem unsolvable, collapse the Unknown-vs-Absent distinction, and break the learning trajectory Hypothesized->WeaklySupported->StronglySupported.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Truth = "This is what we currently represent, with this degree of support, uncertainty, and validity."
b_rows_sample.statement: Re-runs all eight test cases (DB result -> StronglySupported; unstructured document -> WeaklySupported; internet page -> WeaklySupported with caveats; human statement -> Reported; LLM output -> Hypothesized; incomplete question -> no assertion created, Zero detects gap, clarification requested; conflicting sources -> both assertions remain in the Knowledge State with a detected Conflict; unknown value -> Assertion(Unknown)) through the new admission model. States the redefined meaning of 'the single source of truth': Truth = 'this is what we currently represent, with this degree of support, uncertainty, and validity', NOT 'this is factually correct in reality' — the formalization of Knowledge ≠ Reality. Six constitutional invariants listed: Assertion≠Proven Truth; admission does not require verification; Unknown is a valid epistemic state (not absence of an assertion); epistemic status can evolve; multiple epistemic states can coexist (Conflicting is valid); provenance is preserved. Declares the Epistemic Admission Boundary computationally closed and proceeds to 'Computational Closure 3 — The Knowledge State'.

b_rows_sample.anchor: A \not\equiv Truth(P)
b_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes Assertion A=(P,E,Σ,Π,τ,C,ID) with A≢Truth(P): A is 'KnowledgeOS's governed representation of P'. Two assertions of the identical proposition 'Nexus.version=3.69' can carry different epistemic states (Σ_A=(Observed,Strong,Low,Current) vs Σ_B=(Reported,Weak,High,Unknown)) and are 'not epistemically equivalent', giving Assertion⇏StrongEvidence, Assertion⇏Certainty, Assertion⇏Truth.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Admit(P,\Pi_1) \neq Admit(P,\Pi_2)
b_rows_sample.statement: Introduces admission policy Π_adm with Admit(P_c,E,C,Π_adm)->{Assertion|Reject|Defer|RequestMoreEvidence}; admission is purpose-dependent, Admit(P,Π_1)≠Admit(P,Π_2) (an exploration policy may allow Weak support, a production-migration policy may require Strong support) — connecting directly to the Ideal State theory: an assertion can exist with Σ_K=Weak while the Ideal State requires Σ_I=Strong, producing a discrepancy rather than an invalid assertion. Distinguishes Admission ('may this proposition exist as governed knowledge?', Candidate->Assertion) from Validation ('does this assertion satisfy a particular requirement?', Assertion×Constraint->ValidationResult): Admission ≠ Validation — an assertion can be admitted (e.g. during discovery) yet later FAIL a validation (e.g. a migration requiring verified version) WITHOUT being deleted; it 'remains useful historical knowledge'.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Assertion \in KnowledgeState ... KnowledgeState \neq SetOfAssertions
b_rows_sample.statement: Corrects an earlier equation Assertion=Knowledge (too strong) to Assertion∈KnowledgeState while KnowledgeState≠SetOfAssertions: the Knowledge State is a structured object K_t=(Assertions,Evidence,Relationships,Conflicts,Gaps,Provenance,Context,History,Constraints), 'a structured state, not simply a bag of claims' — called 'an important DDD correction'.

b_rows_sample.anchor: \text{Evidence is not a property of a document.}
b_rows_sample.statement: Central correction: Evidence is not a property of a document but 'a relationship between an observation and a proposition under a context and an evaluation rule' — Evidence(O,P,C,R). Prevents the mistake 'the document says X, therefore X is evidence [for whatever P]'. Gives Evidence≠Observation, Evidence≠Source, Evidence≠Support, Evidence≠Truth as four fundamental distinctions, and shows the SAME observation can be evidence for one proposition and not another (Evidence(O,P_1)≠Evidence(O,P_2)) — 'evidence is therefore relational'. E=(O,P,R,C,T,Q,Π): observation, target proposition, evaluation rule, context, temporal applicability, quality assessment, provenance.

type_signature.domain: observation x proposition x context x rule

b_rows_sample.anchor: Conclusion = Inference(Premises,Rule,Context)
b_rows_sample.statement: Rejects 'the evidence voted for 3.69' informal aggregation, requiring Conclusion=Inference(Premises,Rule,Context) via an explicit inference rule (worked example: APIResponse.version=3.69 plus rule 'APIResponse(source=NexusProduction)=>CurrentVersion(NexusProduction)' yields the conclusion). Distinguishes four conclusion kinds: Deductive (Γ⊨P, entailed), Inductive (evidence increases support for a generalization without entailing it), Abductive (select the best explanation among hypotheses {H_1,...,H_n} — 'extremely relevant to KnowledgeOS'), Computational/derived (e.g. a version-vs-required-version comparison rule). Formalizes Conclusion object C_n=(P,Γ,R,κ,Σ,Π,t) (proposition, premises/evidence, inference rule, inference method, epistemic assessment, provenance, derivation time), letting KnowledgeOS answer 'why did you reach this conclusion?' not just 'what did you conclude?'.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Adopted Constitutional Core -- the smallest possible set (11 laws)
a_rows_sample.statement: The 11-law Adopted Constitutional Core (P5's validated recommendation, NOT adopted law here): 1 Identity Law; 2 Dimension Law; 3 Authority Law; 4 Decision Law; 5 Projection Law; 6 Verification Law; 7 Failure-state Law; 8 Contradiction Law; 9 Unknown Law; 10 Agency Law; 11 History Law -- each independently failure-tested (removing it opens a distinct, named corruption not covered by any other law's removal-test); the 4 Established rows appear unchanged as the spine of laws 3-5; the 22 surviving candidate rows render into the 11 laws without loss of content.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Selected kernel law (final wording) ... Failure signature (if removed)
a_rows_sample.statement: The 11 laws given final selected wording with their rendered rows and failure signatures, reproduced from the P5 Decision Matrix (Identity Law renders INV-KOS-002+Context-001+Context-002+Relationship-001+Relation-001; Dimension Law renders INV-KOS-001+NonInterference-001 with NonInterference merged per Decision 2a; Authority Law renders INV-001+INV-003+Pramana-001; Decision Law renders INV-002+Decision-001; Projection Law renders INV-004; Verification Law renders Inference-001+Justification-001+Reasoning-Separation-001+Reasoning-Provenance-001+Vyapti-001+EvidenceAuthenticity-001+Pramana-001; Failure-State Law renders Fallacy-001(state)+Failure-001; Contradiction Law renders Contradiction-001+Dialogue-001(boundary); Unknown Law renders H-ZERO-001+Uncertainty-001+Abhava(requirement); Agency Law renders Agent-001+Relationship-001(knower-side); History Law renders Revisability-001+Temporal family). Verdict: ACCEPTED -- all eleven.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Article 3 -- Authority: 1. Evidence SHALL NOT constitute authority ... 2. Authority SHALL be assigned ... 3. Sources SHALL NOT be interchangeable
a_rows_sample.statement: Article 3 (Authority), 3 clauses: evidence/assessment/source SHALL NOT constitute authority; authority SHALL be assigned -- a recorded reference to a human act, never intrinsic or content-emergent; sources SHALL NOT be interchangeable (the means of acquisition SHALL be preserved -- sensor != expert statement != AI inference != historical document). Renders INV-001, INV-003, INV-KOS-Pramana-001. Failure if removed: a recorded reference self-authorizes; assessment becomes binding; source-role collapse.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Adopted Constitutional Core -- the smallest possible set (11 laws)
b_rows_sample.statement: The 11-law Adopted Constitutional Core (P5's validated recommendation, NOT adopted law here): 1 Identity Law; 2 Dimension Law; 3 Authority Law; 4 Decision Law; 5 Projection Law; 6 Verification Law; 7 Failure-state Law; 8 Contradiction Law; 9 Unknown Law; 10 Agency Law; 11 History Law -- each independently failure-tested (removing it opens a distinct, named corruption not covered by any other law's removal-test); the 4 Established rows appear unchanged as the spine of laws 3-5; the 22 surviving candidate rows render into the 11 laws without loss of content.
