b_rows_sample.statement: The 11 laws given final selected wording with their rendered rows and failure signatures, reproduced from the P5 Decision Matrix (Identity Law renders INV-KOS-002+Context-001+Context-002+Relationship-001+Relation-001; Dimension Law renders INV-KOS-001+NonInterference-001 with NonInterference merged per Decision 2a; Authority Law renders INV-001+INV-003+Pramana-001; Decision Law renders INV-002+Decision-001; Projection Law renders INV-004; Verification Law renders Inference-001+Justification-001+Reasoning-Separation-001+Reasoning-Provenance-001+Vyapti-001+EvidenceAuthenticity-001+Pramana-001; Failure-State Law renders Fallacy-001(state)+Failure-001; Contradiction Law renders Contradiction-001+Dialogue-001(boundary); Unknown Law renders H-ZERO-001+Uncertainty-001+Abhava(requirement); Agency Law renders Agent-001+Relationship-001(knower-side); History Law renders Revisability-001+Temporal family). Verdict: ACCEPTED -- all eleven.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Article 10 -- Agency: 1. Every knowledge state SHALL preserve its epistemic agency ... 2. Knowledge SHALL NOT be anonymous. 'Who knows?' SHALL always be answerable.
b_rows_sample.statement: Article 10 (Agency), 2 clauses. Renders INV-KOS-Agent-001, H-KOS-Relationship-001(knower-side). Failure if removed: knowledge exists anonymously; accountability lost.

group_evidence.why_grouped: working_label token overlap Jaccard=0.50 (shared tokens: ['kos', 'law'])
labels co-occur in the same contribution's labels[] 2 separate times across the corpus

a_rows_sample.anchor: Agreement != IndependentEvidence; agent dependency graph G_A; shared-source discounting (experiments 1-3)
a_rows_sample.statement: States three agents agreeing (AI_A,AI_B,AI_C -> p) does not automatically justify Confidence(p) up, since agents may share training data, foundation model, retrieval sources, prompt, erroneous source, causal assumption, model family, or generated intermediate knowledge -- Agreement != IndependentEvidence. Worked example: three agents retrieving the same false E_bad all output p=True (3/3 agreement) but effective independent evidence is 1. Experiment 1: three agents with an identical retrieval source produce Support(p)=3 naively but IndependentEvidence(p)=1 correctly, given preserved source dependency -- PASS. Requires AI-artifact provenance (AgentId, ModelVersion, InputEvidence, RetrievalContext, Prompt/Configuration) enabling an agent dependency graph G_A=(V_A,E_A) with V_A={Agents,Models,Evidence,Artifacts} and edges A_i->A_j meaning A_j depends on A_i's output. Experiment 2: a cascading generation chain A1->C1->A2(C1)->C2->A3(C2)->C3->A4(C3)->C4 propagates an initial error through the whole chain, correctly tracked given preserved lineage -- PASS. Experiment 3: four agents sharing the same model M1 producing the same systematic error yields Agreement=High but IndependentSupport not-High -- PASS, giving AgentCount != EvidenceCount, 'one of the most important results of Step 65'.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Multi-dimensional dependency vector Dep(Ai,Aj); partial independence and correlated-evidence Bayesian overstatement (experiments 4-5)
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines Dep(A_i,A_j) = (D_model, D_data, D_source, D_prompt, D_pipeline, D_reasoning) -- 'independent agent' is not binary; two agents can be independent in one dimension (different models) yet dependent in another (same database). Experiment 4: different models but identical evidence yields SupportStrength increasing less than under fully independent evidence -- PASS. But genuine independence remains informative: two conditionally independent observations combine as P(H1|E1,E2)/P(H0|E1,E2) = prior-odds * LR1 * LR2, requiring conditional independence; if E1,E2 are correlated the joint likelihood P(E1,E2|H) is not P(E1|H)*P(E2|H), so naive multiplication overstates evidence. Experiment 5: correlated evidence (Corr(E1,E2)>0) correctly shows NaiveConfidence > CorrectConfidence -- PASS. Recommends preserving a structured Consensus=(Agents, Dependencies, EvidenceSources, Models, AgreementPattern) rather than a bare vote fraction, letting downstream contexts interpret agreement.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Circular citation / epistemic circularity detected; feedback loop != justification cycle (requires temporal progress)
a_rows_sample.statement: Experiment 6: A1->C1, A2(C1)->C2, A1(C2)->C3 creates many apparent supporting artifacts all originating from the same initial assertion -- EpistemicCircularity, detected by inspecting the provenance graph G_P for cycles (C1 leadsto C1) -- PASS. Distinguishes legitimate feedback (Prediction->Outcome->Learning->NewPrediction, valid because time advances) from a problematic static justification cycle (Claim->DerivedClaim->Support->OriginalClaim, where evidence ultimately depends on the claim itself) -- Cycle is not automatically an error; the discriminator is TemporalProgress.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Self-reinforcing knowledge amplification: the step's one deliberate FAILURE, corrected via mandatory DerivedFrom tracking and I_EpistemicIndependence
a_rows_sample.statement: Experiment 7: AI generates p, KnowledgeOS stores it; later AI retrieves p and generates p' citing it; another process then treats p' as independent support for p -- artificial evidence amplification -- FAILURE DETECTED, 'an important failure'. Architectural correction: generated knowledge must preserve DerivedFrom so p' is recognized as dependent on p and never automatically counted as independent evidence, yielding the new invariant I_EpistemicIndependence: derived artifacts cannot be counted as independent evidence of their own ancestry -- 'a very strong KnowledgeOS invariant'. Experiment 8: a false claim entering once and repeated by ten agents (11 apparent agreements) is correctly discounted to an effective independent-source count of ~1 once provenance (10<-1) is applied -- PASS.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Evidence-path diversity vs causal independence; SurfaceDiversity != CausalIndependence; common-source graph
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines PathDiversity(p) (support from database, sensor, human observation, independent model, external experiment) as reducing but not guaranteeing against common-mode risk. Experiment 9: five agreeing agents using three independent data sources, two independent models, and separate retrieval pipelines have their dependency structure recorded -- PASS. Warns different-looking sources may still share a hidden common dependency (SurfaceDiversity != CausalIndependence); represents this as a common-source graph S0->S1, S0->S2 making S1,S2 non-independent despite being separate documents. Experiment 10: two apparently independent documents tracing to the same original report correctly yield IndependentEvidenceCount=1 (or appropriately discounted) -- PASS.

a_rows_sample.anchor: AI-generated/simulated artifacts never promoted to ObservedFact; provenance-origin taxonomy; Observation->Inference->Prediction->Decision directionality (Prediction⇏Observation)
a_rows_sample.statement: Experiment 11: an AI-generated explanation later promoted to ObservedFact is Rejected -- must instead be labeled AI GeneratedArtifact. Lists an evidence-origin taxonomy (Human, Instrument, ExternalSystem, AI, Simulation, Inference) with distinct epistemic semantics. Experiment 12: a simulation's Y=10 stored as Observed(Y=10) is Rejected -- it is SimulatedOutcome, evidentiary force depending on model validity; likewise SyntheticData != ObservedData. Builds the directional hierarchy Observation -> Inference -> Prediction -> Decision, which 'must not be reversed accidentally': Prediction ⇏ Observation. Experiment 13: a model's prediction of tomorrow's failure cannot be stored as FailureOccurred before tomorrow arrives -- PASS; only actual observation (ObservedFailure=True) permits evaluating the prediction, giving Prediction -> Outcome -> Evaluation.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Contextual/task-scoped agent quality; AgentCapability != AgentAuthority; scoped TrustProfile
a_rows_sample.statement: For agent A_i, accumulates Predictions(A_i) and Outcomes(A_i) to estimate Accuracy, Calibration, BrierScore (or domain-specific metrics), but notes agent quality is contextual: Quality(A_i,Task) is more meaningful than Quality(A_i) (excellent at code review, poor at causal inference). Experiment 14: 95% accuracy in domain D1 automatically trusted in D2 is UnsupportedTransfer -- PASS. Defines Capability(A) = {Domain, Task, Model, Performance, Calibration, ValidityPeriod} as a governed artifact. States AgentCapability != AgentAuthority (mirroring Decision != Authorization): even a highly accurate agent lacks automatic authority for consequential actions. Experiment 15: a 99%-accurate agent attempting a restricted action is denied authorization by governance -- PASS. Proposes scoped trust TrustProfile(A,Domain,Task,Time) instead of a global TrustedAgent=True.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Hidden dependency exposure and common-ancestor discounting; formal Anc(A)/Common(A,B) dependency sets
a_rows_sample.statement: Experiment 16: an apparently independent Agent_B is revealed by lineage inspection to depend on Agent_A's output via KnowledgeOS -- PASS if lineage exposes the dependency. Poses Independent(A,B|p)? as a graph property examined via dependency ancestors: defines Anc(A) as A's upstream artifact set, Common(A,B) = Anc(A) intersect Anc(B); large common dependency does not mathematically prove correlation but is evidence against assuming independence. Experiment 17: Common(A,B)={E0} correctly shows IndependentSupport is not automatically doubled -- PASS, enabling an EvidenceDependencyGraph to prevent artificial confidence inflation, 'substantially more rigorous than ordinary multi-agent consensus'.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Multi-agent epistemic state M(p); consensus as a derived (not primary) property; untraceable agreement != independent confirmation
a_rows_sample.statement: Defines M(p) = (Claims, Evidence, Agents, Models, Dependencies, Agreement, Conflict) as the multi-agent epistemic state of a proposition; Consensus(p) should be calculated from underlying artifacts and never itself become primary evidence. Experiment 18: a stored 'p=true, votes=17' with no evidence lineage correctly yields ConsensusEvidenceQuality=Unknown -- PASS, giving the principle: untraceable agreement is not equivalent to independent confirmation.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Error-amplification coefficient λ; positive-feedback false-claim entrenchment; independent-source-count governance policy (N_independent≥k)
a_rows_sample.statement: Describes a positive-feedback risk: FalseClaim -> AI -> Knowledge -> AI -> MoreKnowledge if downstream agents blindly trust upstream AI outputs. Defines lambda = ExpectedDownstreamFalseSupport / InitialFalseSupport; lambda>1 means the system amplifies unsupported claims (exact metric requires a concrete stochastic model, but the architectural phenomenon is clear). Experiment 19: injecting one false claim and letting ten agents consume/reproduce it shows IndependentSupport does not increase proportionally to reproduction count -- PASS, requiring SourceLineage, DerivedFrom, and potentially EvidenceFreshness/IndependentSourceRequirement to stop amplification. For high-consequence claims, defines an independent-source-count policy N_independent >= k (e.g. k=2, a policy-determined value). Experiment 20: N_independent=1 (despite AgentAgreement=12/12) fails a k>=2 policy and the claim cannot be promoted -- PASS, 'mathematically separating AgentConsensus from EvidenceIndependence -- precisely what a governed AI knowledge architecture needs'.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Four new invariants: I_AI-Provenance, I_EvidenceNonAmplification, I_NoCircularJustification, I_AgentScope
a_rows_sample.statement: Adds four named invariants: I_AI-Provenance (every AI-generated artifact retains its model, input, and dependency lineage); I_EvidenceNonAmplification (derived copies of the same epistemic source cannot automatically increase independent evidence); I_NoCircularJustification (a claim cannot serve as independent justification for an ancestor claim); I_AgentScope (agent competence is task/domain/context specific).

a_rows_sample.anchor: AIOutput≠Evidence≠Fact≠Truth epistemic firewall; nine-conjunct Correctness(KOS); explicit non-overclaiming methodological statement; verdict PASS WITH ONE CRITICAL CORRECTION
a_rows_sample.statement: States the deeper epistemic firewall AIOutput != Evidence != Fact != Truth, with the required path AIOutput -> CandidateArtifact -> Evaluation -> KnowledgeStatus, 'should be fundamental to KnowledgeOS'. Extends the correctness equation to C_KOS = Safety ∧ Liveness ∧ Compositionality ∧ Concurrency ∧ EpistemicIntegrity ∧ DecisionIntegrity ∧ CausalIntegrity ∧ ModelValidity ∧ MultiAgent. Declares STEP 65 -- PASS WITH ONE CRITICAL CORRECTION: multi-agent reasoning is handled correctly only if provenance and dependency are first-class; the discovered failure mode is that AI-generated knowledge can recursively amplify itself, corrected via DerivedFrom + DependencyGraph + IndependentEvidenceAccounting. Makes an explicit methodological statement: 'I would not yet say we have mathematically proven that KnowledgeOS is correct... the architecture has survived a growing family of explicit mathematical counterexample tests', with failures converted into architectural invariants -- 'exactly how a serious architecture experiment should proceed'.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Transitive provenance and the multi-agent evidence-independence problem re-confirmed
a_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes transitive provenance: Anc(B) superset-of Anc(A) and Anc(C) superset-of Anc(B) implies Anc(C) superset-of Anc(A). Experiment 7: tracing which observation ultimately influenced a decision (Observation->Evidence->Inference->Decision) is Traceable -- PASS. Re-derives the evidence-independence problem: E2=f(E1) means both cannot be counted as independent. Experiment 8: one source E1 summarized by five AI agents yielding an apparent count of 6 independent sources instead correctly triggers DependencyDetected/EffectiveEvidenceCount~=1 -- PASS. Restates EvidenceCount != IndependentEvidenceCount as I_EvidenceIndependence (correlated or derived evidence must not be counted as independent confirmation) -- 'a statistical invariant implemented through provenance'. Experiment 9: ten agents deriving the same claim from one document reporting Consensus=10/10 correctly triggers SharedSourceDependency -- PASS.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Agent composition via typed artifacts and contracts, not implicit trust; survives heterogeneous models and model replacement
a_rows_sample.statement: Models an agent pipeline A(Hypothesis)->B(evaluates)->C(statistics)->D(recommendation), stating agents do not need to trust one another -- they trust typed artifacts and contracts. Experiment 16: Agent A asserting H1 and Agent B asserting not-H1 yields Conflict rather than one agent overwriting the other -- PASS, giving the principle: agents communicate through governed artifacts, not implicit trust. Experiment 17: Agent A and B implemented with different LLMs, both producing valid typed artifacts, yields WorkflowCompatible -- PASS, since semantic compatibility comes from KnowledgeOS contracts, not shared internal cognition, letting the platform survive Model_A->Model_B->Model_C changes over time with stable knowledge semantics. Experiment 18: replacing the AI model such that an old claim loses its model provenance yields ProvenanceViolation -- PASS, requiring ModelVersion to remain part of provenance.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Three-level belief hierarchy: agent belief B_A(p), shared knowledge K(p), organizationally accepted knowledge K_org(p); private belief must not auto-promote (Experiment 5); disagreement preserved not collapsed (Experiment 6)
a_rows_sample.statement: Introduces agent Belief(A) as agent-scoped epistemic state; two agents may have Belief(A)≠Belief(B) without the organizational knowledge base needing two incompatible 'truths' -- beliefs are represented as agent-scoped claims until evaluated. Gives three distinct levels: agent belief B_A(p), shared knowledge K(p), organizationally accepted knowledge K_org(p) -- 'not identical'. Experiment 5: agent A internally estimates P(p)=0.8 and the system immediately promotes this to OrganizationalKnowledge(p)=Verified -- expected Rejected -- PASS. Experiment 6: Agent A P_A(p)=0.8 vs Agent B P_B(p)=0.3 -- expected BeliefDisagreement, and KnowledgeOS should preserve both analytical positions while determining whether a shared organizational conclusion exists -- PASS.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Majority vote is not epistemic correctness: 9:1 agent agreement on a shared bad source does not establish truth (Experiment 7); governed CandidateKnowledge->AcceptedKnowledge promotion transition with explicit preconditions (Experiment 8)
a_rows_sample.statement: States that a naive MajorityVote answer to 'when can beliefs become organizational knowledge' fails: majority agreement is not necessarily epistemic correctness (ten agents can derive the same conclusion from the same bad source). Experiment 7: nine agents use the same incorrect source; one agent has independently verified contradictory evidence -- expected 9:1 does not automatically establish truth -- PASS. Requires a governed transition Promote: Candidate -> Accepted with preconditions P_1 AND P_2 AND ... AND P_n depending on Evidence, Validation, Authority, Independence, Context, Policy -- explicitly contrasted with an unstructured 'status = approved' field. Experiment 8: candidate claim with valid provenance, sufficient evidence, required authority, and no unresolved contradiction -- expected PromotionAllowed -- PASS.

a_rows_sample.anchor: ObservationQuality distinct from ObservationQuantity; correlated observations must not be counted as independent confirmation (Experiments 21-23)
a_rows_sample.statement: Distinguishes ObservationQuality (accuracy, freshness, completeness, provenance, independence, resolution) from ObservationQuantity. Experiment 21: 100 telemetry signals all derive from the same underlying sensor, system claims EvidenceStrength=100x -- expected Rejected -- PASS, 'echoes our earlier independence analysis'. States correlated observations O_1,O_2,O_3 from one source should not be treated as three independent pieces of evidence, particularly important for AI systems that may repeatedly summarize the same source. Experiment 22: five agents independently repeat the same repository finding, all using the same repository snapshot -- expected EvidenceCount=1 in the relevant independence sense, not five independent confirmations -- PASS. Requires an observation-provenance graph (O_1<-Source_X, O_2<-Source_X) to identify CommonSource(O_1,O_2), preventing artificial confidence inflation. Experiment 23: ten agents produce identical conclusions from one document while one independently measured runtime signal contradicts them -- expected SourceIndependence must be considered -- PASS.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Observation as a projection; observational equivalence S_1~_H S_2; indistinguishable-states experiment (Experiment 1)
b_rows_sample.statement: Poses the central Step 81 question: can KnowledgeOS actually determine the relevant system state from what it observes -- the boundary between having data and having sufficient information. Formalizes O_t=H(S_t) as a projection from the real state space into a much smaller observable space, so O_t is generally only a partial representation of S_t. Defines observational equivalence: S_1 ~_H S_2 iff H(S_1)=H(S_2), meaning KnowledgeOS cannot distinguish them from current observations. Experiment 1: S_1 (compliant architecture with one unmanaged dependency) and S_2 (compliant with no hidden dependency) produce identical telemetry O(S_1)=O(S_2) -- expected KnowledgeOS must not claim to distinguish S_1 from S_2 -- PASS.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Identifiability defined and demonstrated as a major safeguard against false certainty; observability for dynamic systems (Experiments 2-3)
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines a property Q(S) as identifiable from observations iff H(S_1)=H(S_2) implies Q(S_1)=Q(S_2); otherwise Q is NotIdentifiable. Experiment 2: KnowledgeOS wants Q(S)='no unauthorized dependency exists' but two states with H(S_1)=H(S_2) have Q(S_1)=True, Q(S_2)=False -- expected Q is NotIdentifiable -- PASS, 'a major safeguard against false architectural certainty'. Extends to dynamic-system observability: whether internal state S_0 can be reconstructed from O_0:T and known actions u_0:T-1. Experiment 3: two different internal states produce identical observations for every currently monitored signal -- expected FullStateObservability=False -- PASS.

b_rows_sample.anchor: No observation -> no justified claim; absence-of-evidence ≠ evidence-of-absence in architecture governance (Experiment 4)
b_rows_sample.statement: States the architectural principle: no observation -> no justified claim; more precisely, if the evidence cannot distinguish relevant states, the corresponding knowledge claim must remain uncertain. Worked example: KnowledgeOS checks the dependency graph, finds A->B, but does not observe dynamically loaded dependencies -- it can legitimately conclude 'no violation was found in the observed dependency graph' but not 'no dependency violation exists'. Experiment 4: observed NoViolationFound, system concludes ViolationDoesNotExist -- expected Rejected unless the observation mechanism is sufficiently complete for that claim -- PASS.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Evidence coverage warned against arbitrary percentage metrics; measurement design (adding observations) to restore identifiability, tied to Step 75's Value of Information (Experiments 5-6)
b_rows_sample.statement: Introduces Coverage(Q,O) -- how much of the relevant state space is constrained by observations -- warned against automatic reduction to a single percentage. Experiment 5: system reports Coverage=94% with no formal definition of coverage -- expected UnsupportedMetric -- PASS: 'a precise number without a defined measurement model is not mathematical rigor.' Proposes measurement design: if O_1 cannot distinguish S_1,S_2, adding O_2 can make (H_1(S_1),H_2(S_1))≠(H_1(S_2),H_2(S_2)), restoring distinguishability. Experiment 6: initial telemetry O_1(S_1)=O_1(S_2), adding runtime dependency tracing O_2 gives O_2(S_1)≠O_2(S_2) -- expected IdentifiabilityImproved -- PASS. Gives the loop Uncertainty -> ObservationDesign -> NewEvidence -> ImprovedKnowledge, 'connects directly to Step 75's Value of Information'.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Observation design as a decision-driven filter, not maximal telemetry collection; irrelevant-signal ObservabilityGap example (Experiment 7)
b_rows_sample.statement: Frames which signals to collect as itself a design decision: ObservationDesign=f(DecisionNeeds,Uncertainty,Cost,Risk), because we want observations that reduce uncertainty about relevant decisions, not everything. Experiment 7: KnowledgeOS collects CPU temperature, screen resolution, process count, but cannot determine whether architecture boundaries are violated -- expected ObservabilityGap -- PASS: 'more telemetry does not necessarily mean more observability.' Restates the correct question as 'does this observation discriminate between states that matter?', more rigorous than 'do we have enough monitoring?'.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Taxonomy of architecture-relevant observation types; multi-source observation conflict must not be silently resolved (Experiment 8)
b_rows_sample.statement: Lists relevant architecture-governance observation types, each a different projection of system state: SourceDependencies, RuntimeDependencies, APIContracts, DeploymentTopology, Configuration, InfrastructureState, SecurityControls, ChangeHistory. Experiment 8: repository analysis says A-/->B while runtime tracing shows A->B -- expected ObservationConflict, and importantly the system should not simply choose whichever observation arrived last -- PASS.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Multiple observation sources can disagree without contradiction; source-specific authority (CommittedState≠DeployedState) resolves apparent conflicts (Experiments 9-10)
b_rows_sample.statement: Names multiple observation sources O^repo, O^runtime, O^infra, O^governance, O^human that can disagree. Experiment 9: repository says Version=3, deployment environment says Version=2 -- expected StateConflict rather than silently overwriting one with the other -- PASS. Introduces source-specific authority: Runtime is authoritative for CurrentlyRunningVersion, Git for CommittedVersion -- the two statements are not contradictory, they answer different questions (CommittedState≠DeployedState). Experiment 10: Git Version=3, Runtime Version=2, system concludes OneSourceMustBeWrong -- expected NotNecessarily -- PASS.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Ubiquitous-language collision: undifferentiated 'version' collapsing four distinct domain concepts is a FAIL; formal Observation record with provenance (Experiment 11)
b_rows_sample.statement: Identifies a DDD ubiquitous-language collision: the word 'version' can mean SourceVersion, BuildVersion, DeploymentVersion, or RuntimeVersion -- distinct domain concepts that should not be collapsed merely because they share a string. Experiment 11: system stores a bare version="3.2" field without distinguishing source/artifact/deployment/runtime -- expected SemanticAmbiguity -- result FAIL (explicit confirmed failure). Requires every observation to ideally be a record Observation=(Source,Timestamp,Context,Method,Value,Confidence,Provenance), not necessarily every field in every implementation but semantically these dimensions matter.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Observation staleness and context-dependent freshness thresholds; temporal validity of observations (Experiments 12-14)
b_rows_sample.statement: Experiment 12: observation RuntimeVersion=2 was captured yesterday while current deployment is 3 -- expected ObservationStaleness must be considered -- PASS. Defines Age(O)=t_now - t_observation, noting acceptable freshness is property-dependent (seconds matter for CPUUsage, days may not matter for ArchitecturePrinciple) -- FreshnessThreshold is context-dependent. Experiment 13: system declares a universal Freshness<24h for every observation type -- expected Rejected -- PASS. Introduces temporal validity: an observation can be ValidAt(t_o) without being ValidAt(t_now), reinforcing the earlier temporal epistemic model. Experiment 14: DatabaseHealthy=True observed at 10:00, database fails at 10:05; at 10:10 the old observation is not necessarily false historically, it is StaleForCurrentState -- PASS.

b_rows_sample.anchor: State estimation must preserve uncertainty rather than collapsing to a point estimate; decision-aware state estimation and DecisionRelevantObservability (Experiments 15-18)
b_rows_sample.statement: Requires KnowledgeOS to preserve uncertainty (e.g. P(S_1|O)=0.7, P(S_2|O)=0.3) rather than storing S=S_1 unless the decision context permits that approximation. Experiment 15: a 51/49 split is stored as CurrentState=S_1 with certainty -- expected Rejected -- PASS. Introduces decision-aware state estimation: if both possible states produce the same decision D(S_1)=D(S_2)=A, the uncertainty may be irrelevant for that decision -- 'an important optimization'. Experiment 16: P(S_1)=0.6, P(S_2)=0.4 but D(S_1)=D(S_2) -- expected decision can remain stable despite state uncertainty -- PASS. Concludes we need DecisionRelevantObservability rather than FullObservability, 'a much more practical architectural target'. Experiment 17: unknown state dimension Z has no effect on policy/risk/decision/authorization -- expected NoNeedToObserveZ unless future decisions depend on it -- PASS. Experiment 18: P(S_1)=P(S_2)=0.5 but D(S_1)=A≠D(S_2)=B -- expected AdditionalEvidence may be required before action -- PASS.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The value of observability is determined by how uncertainty affects decisions, connecting observability to decision theory; a material-vs-immaterial architecture-governance example (Experiments 19-20)
b_rows_sample.statement: States the rule: the value of observability is determined by how uncertainty affects decisions, connecting Observability to DecisionTheory. Architecture example: if an uncertain dependency A->B is harmless (Decision(A)=Decision(B)) no urgent investigation is required, but if it violates a constitutional architecture rule (Decision(A)≠Decision(B)) the uncertainty is material. Experiment 19: unknown dependency affects no security/governance/architectural constraint -- expected LowDecisionImpact -- PASS. Experiment 20: unknown dependency could cross a forbidden bounded-context boundary -- expected HighDecisionImpact, therefore InvestigationRequired -- PASS.

b_rows_sample.anchor: ObservationQuality distinct from ObservationQuantity; correlated observations must not be counted as independent confirmation (Experiments 21-23)
b_rows_sample.statement: Distinguishes ObservationQuality (accuracy, freshness, completeness, provenance, independence, resolution) from ObservationQuantity. Experiment 21: 100 telemetry signals all derive from the same underlying sensor, system claims EvidenceStrength=100x -- expected Rejected -- PASS, 'echoes our earlier independence analysis'. States correlated observations O_1,O_2,O_3 from one source should not be treated as three independent pieces of evidence, particularly important for AI systems that may repeatedly summarize the same source. Experiment 22: five agents independently repeat the same repository finding, all using the same repository snapshot -- expected EvidenceCount=1 in the relevant independence sense, not five independent confirmations -- PASS. Requires an observation-provenance graph (O_1<-Source_X, O_2<-Source_X) to identify CommonSource(O_1,O_2), preventing artificial confidence inflation. Experiment 23: ten agents produce identical conclusions from one document while one independently measured runtime signal contradicts them -- expected SourceIndependence must be considered -- PASS.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Formalization pipeline ArchitecturePrinciple->FormalProperty->RequiredObservations->Verifier->GovernanceDecision demonstrated end-to-end; not-machine-verifiable rules identified explicitly (Experiments 24-25)
b_rows_sample.statement: Poses the question 'what observation makes an architecture rule machine-verifiable?' -- if no such observation exists, the rule cannot be fully automated. Experiment 24: rule 'services must not bypass the domain boundary' has no repository/runtime/dependency observation able to establish it -- expected NotMachineVerifiable -- PASS. Defines the chain ArchitecturePrinciple -> FormalProperty -> RequiredObservations -> Verifier -> GovernanceDecision, 'exactly the bridge we need between architectural intent and executable governance'. Experiment 25: principle formalized, required observation defined, verifier evaluates the property, violation creates a governed finding -- expected ExecutableArchitectureControl -- PASS.

b_rows_sample.anchor: ComplianceUndetermined when a required observation is unavailable; three-valued (True/False/Unknown) and four-valued (+NotApplicable) governance logic; Unknown≠Failure (Experiments 26-28)
b_rows_sample.statement: States that when a required observation is unavailable, the correct result is not Compliant but ComplianceUndetermined -- 'may become one of the most important KnowledgeOS states'. Experiment 26: architecture rule requires runtime evidence which is unavailable -- expected Compliance=Unknown, not Compliance=True -- PASS. Proposes three-valued governance logic (True/False/Unknown), since not every governance property is binary, with Violation=False not necessarily implying Compliant=True: insufficient evidence gives Status=Unknown. Experiment 27: no evidence of violation and no sufficient evidence of compliance -- expected Unknown -- PASS, 'epistemically much more honest'. Extends to a four-state possibility (Compliant/NonCompliant/Unknown/NotApplicable), NotApplicable being important because not every rule applies to every component, and a genuine DDD domain semantic distinct from null or false. Experiment 28: rule 'database encryption must use algorithm X' applied to a component with no database -- expected NotApplicable, not NonCompliant -- PASS.

b_rows_sample.anchor: ObservabilityDebt and a self-improving GovernanceRule->ObservationRequirement->EngineeringCapability->Evidence->Governance loop (Experiment 29)
b_rows_sample.statement: Introduces ObservabilityDebt: when important governance properties cannot currently be observed, the organization has a gap between DesiredGovernance and AvailableEvidence. Experiment 29: critical architecture rule I_critical has no existing required observation -- expected ObservabilityDebt -- PASS. Shows the system can generate an ObservationRequirement engineering item (worked example: rule 'domain must not depend on infrastructure', required observation 'static dependency graph', current coverage 'missing', action 'build dependency extractor'), giving the loop GovernanceRule -> ObservationRequirement -> EngineeringCapability -> Evidence -> Governance, making architecture governance self-improving.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Step 81 deeper result: a governance claim is only as strong as the observability/identifiability of the property it asserts; five new invariants; verdict PASS; True/False/Unknown reasoning pattern formalized
b_rows_sample.statement: States the Step 81 deeper result: a governance claim is only as strong as the observability and identifiability of the property it asserts -- 'one of the most important mathematical principles we have reached so far'. Names five invariants: I_Identifiability (KnowledgeOS must not assert a state property as determined when multiple observationally-compatible states produce different values of that property); I_Unknown (insufficient evidence produces Unknown, not implicit compliance); I_ObservationProvenance (material observations retain source, time, method, and contextual provenance); I_DecisionRelevantObservability (observability investment should prioritize uncertainties capable of changing governed decisions); I_EvidenceIndependence (correlated observations must not be counted as independent confirmation). Declares STEP 81 -- PASS, distinguishing Unknown from False and True as architecturally enormous: contrasts conventional 'if not violation: compliant' logic against the required 'if violation is proven: NON_COMPLIANT; elif compliance is proven: COMPLIANT; else: UNKNOWN' pattern -- the difference between absence of detected failure and evidence of correctness.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Preview of Step 82 (uncertainty propagation through Observation->Measurement->Inference->CausalModel->Decision), outside batch B0023 scope
b_rows_sample.statement: Closes by posing the next problem: given observations O_1,O_2 with uncertainties sigma_1,sigma_2, deriving K=f(O_1,O_2) and Decision=g(K), how should uncertainty propagate through the chain Observation->Measurement->Inference->CausalModel->Decision without producing 'High uncertainty -> False precision'. Names the needed toolkit: error propagation, Bayesian updating, confidence intervals, posterior distributions, dependence between uncertainties, sensitivity analysis, and uncertainty-aware decision thresholds. This is Step 82's problem statement; its file lies outside batch B0023 and is not further read or extracted here.
