a_rows_sample.anchor: Finding table: Successor-state semantics YES strong candidate ... Situation Calculus ontology itself NO ... Sat=truth in situation NO too strong ... Zero=executable situation NO explicitly reject ... Gap=non-entailed fluent NO too narrow ... Contr=inconsistency NO ... Boundary=frame axiom NO
a_rows_sample.statement: Classifies seventeen situation-calculus findings by whether they can enter KnowledgeOS theory: strong-candidate YES for successor-state semantics, persistence/frame problem, action preconditions/executability, history-vs-snapshot (with correction), transition composition, regression, progression, sensing, temporal actions, concurrency, natural/forced transitions; derived-capability YES for planning; NOT-yet-core for probability/MDP and policies; explicit NO for adopting Situation Calculus ontology itself, and NO for Sat=truth-in-situation, Zero=executable-situation, Gap=non-entailed-fluent, Contr=inconsistency, Boundary=frame-axiom.

a_rows_sample.anchor: KR-DELTA-2026-09 Successor-State/Persistence Experiment ... KR-EXEC-2026-09 Executable History Experiment ... KR-COMP-TRANS-2026-09 Transition Composition Experiment ... KR-SENSE-2026-09 Epistemic Sensing Experiment
a_rows_sample.statement: Commissions four new experiments: KR-DELTA-2026-09 (test 10 successor-state effect patterns including conditional/contradictory/concurrent/invalid effects against Effect+/Effect-/Persistence representability), KR-EXEC-2026-09 (test Poss(e,K) against authorized/unauthorized/impossible/unknown-precondition/contradictory-precondition/externally-forced/failed/simulated execution, linking delta to the Authority model without conflating them), KR-COMP-TRANS-2026-09 (test delta2(delta1(K)) against sequence/failure/partiality/rollback/conflicting-effects/concurrent/repeated events, kept separate from evaluation-composition experiments), KR-SENSE-2026-09 (test whether Sense(O,K) changes epistemic state without subject-state change while preserving provenance/time/context/contradiction/evidence-status).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Epistemic lane: Observation\rightarrow Evidence\rightarrow Evaluation\rightarrow Determination ... Dynamic lane: Event\rightarrow Possibility\rightarrow Effect\rightarrow Persistence\rightarrow\delta\rightarrow K_{t+1} ... Connected by K_t ... create a KR-DYN / Situation-Calculus Integration evidence-to-theory artifact, mark each item [FACT]/[DERIVED]/[PROP]/[OPEN]
a_rows_sample.statement: Proposes separating KnowledgeOS theory into two orthogonal mechanisms connected by K_t: an epistemic lane (Observation->Evidence->Evaluation->Determination) and a dynamic lane (Event->Possibility->Effect->Persistence->delta->K_{t+1}), with Reasoning (Regression/Progression) operating over both and Planning operating over the dynamic model; final recommendation is to create a KR-DYN/Situation-Calculus-Integration evidence-to-theory artifact tagging every item [FACT]/[DERIVED]/[PROP]/[OPEN] and running the delta/persistence/executable-history experiments, rather than declaring Theory v1.3, to avoid 'importing a mathematically elegant external formalism and silently treating its constructs as KnowledgeOS semantics'.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The Situation Calculus provides the formal backbone for KnowledgeOS's dynamic semantics. It does not provide the epistemic semantics (Contr, Zero, Sat, Evaluation) or the decision semantics (R_req, ≡sem, Lifecycle, Kernel). ... Next Step: Proceed to the epistemic lane experiments: KR-CONTR-2026-09 ... KR-ZERO-2026-09 ... KR-SAT-2026-09 ... KR-REQ-2026-09 ... Action: Ratify dynamic lane; proceed to epistemic lane experiments
a_rows_sample.statement: Formal HPA Supervisory ratification ('Status: [DERIVATION] Complete', 'Action: Ratify dynamic lane') declaring the dynamic lane substantially complete while Contr, Zero, Sat, R_req, ≡sem, Lifecycle, cross-frame divergence, Factivity, and Kernel selection remain explicitly OPEN/BLOCKED; commissions four new epistemic-lane experiments distinct from S2526's dynamic-lane experiments: KR-CONTR-2026-09 (contradiction semantics), KR-ZERO-2026-09 (Zero as boundary examination), KR-SAT-2026-09 (evaluation semantics), KR-REQ-2026-09 (required distinctions R_req).

b_rows_sample.anchor: Table: what I would actually add to KnowledgeOS Theory v1.3 (T1-T5) vs What I would NOT adopt
b_rows_sample.statement: Recorded editorial recommendation: five candidate theoretical commitments (T1 explicit/implicit knowledge, T2 reasoning is semantics-dependent Cn_S(K), T3 evaluation may consume implicit knowledge Eval_c(Cn_S(K),r,Gamma), T4 state transition needs persistence semantics Succ_S, T5 explanation is not determination) proposed for Theory v1.3 as strong candidates, none yet kernel-promoted; explicitly rejects Sat=FOL-entailment, Zero=CWA, Zero=Delta=empty universally, Boundary=frame axioms, delta=situation calculus, Identity=unique-names+domain-closure, DL=Boundary-taxonomy, mandatory default reasoning, FOL-as-representation-language, and YES/NO/UNKNOWN-sufficiency.

b_rows_sample.anchor: I would create a new research artifact: KR-KRR-2026-09 — Knowledge Representation and Reasoning Integration ... KR-EXP-IMPLICIT ... KR-ENTAIL ... KR-ABD ... KR-DELTA ... KR-FRAME ... KR-NONMON ... KR-CWA
b_rows_sample.statement: Recommends creating research artifact KR-KRR-2026-09 with four sections (source-established results; KnowledgeOS-compatible hypotheses; rejected translations; experiments required) and seven planned experiments: KR-EXP-IMPLICIT, KR-ENTAIL, KR-ABD, KR-DELTA, KR-FRAME, KR-NONMON, KR-CWA, to update the TODO register based on results.

b_rows_sample.anchor: KR-EXP-IMPLICIT | Explicit vs implicit knowledge | Test the K^E \rightarrow K^{I,S} distinction ... KR-CWA | Zero vs closed-world reasoning | Test Zero against CWA
b_rows_sample.statement: Restates (Recommendation 4, with explicit per-experiment purpose statements) the seven required experiments proposed earlier in the same research session: KR-EXP-IMPLICIT (test K^E->K^{I,S}), KR-ENTAIL (test Eval_content), KR-ABD (test abduction as explanation), KR-DELTA (test delta as Succ_S), KR-FRAME (test Boundary as persistence), KR-NONMON (test nonmonotonic lifecycle), KR-CWA (test Zero against CWA).

b_rows_sample.anchor: Summary: Strategic Reading Order ... The Immediate Action: Read Williamson's "Knowledge and Its Limits" first. ... Then read Levesque & Lakemeyer's ... Then proceed to the lifecycle, nonmonotonicity, and governance books
b_rows_sample.statement: Final strategic reading-order recommendation: Williamson (Factivity/Contr/Sat/Evidence) first, then Levesque & Lakemeyer (Sat/TELL-ASK/explicit-implicit belief), then belief-revision, nonmonotonic-reasoning, and deontic-logic texts in that order, each mapped to specific open TODOs.

group_evidence.why_grouped: explicit agent-stated uncertainty: 'kr-dyn-situation-calculus-integration-thread' POSSIBLY relates to 'kr-krr-2026-09-knowledge-representation-integration-thread' (batch B0061). Note: Recommended next artifact (parallel to KR-DL-2026-09) marking every item [FACT]/[DERIVED]/[PROP]/[OPEN] and running the delta/persistence/executable-history experiments (KR-DELTA-2026-09, KR-EXEC-2026-09, KR-COMP-TRANS-2026-09, KR-SENSE-2026-09), rather than folding Situation Calculus directly into Theory v1.3.

a_rows_sample.anchor: NextEpistemicAct(K_t,Q_t,Delta_t,R_t,Pi) ... a_t in {Clarify, Search, Observe, ConsultResource, AssessEvidence, Determine, Defer, Act}. ... EA1..EA7
a_rows_sample.statement: Specifies a four-layer Epistemic Agency Execution Loop (front-end interaction; gap detection & classification via K_t|=Q; epistemic agency selection via a*=argmax[ExpectedGapReduction/(Cost+Risk)]; determination & output) and seven hypotheses EA1-EA7: EA1 observation!=interpretation; EA2 intent as unconfirmed hypothesis; EA3 typed gap resolution over {Semantic,Epistemic,...}; EA4 epistemic action optimization a*=argmax[E[DeltaRed]/Cost]; EA5 resource-bounded actions A_t=Filter(A,Resources_t); EA6 Lord/Sarathi duality (generate vs select); EA7 Determine(Evidence) before Act.

a_rows_sample.anchor: K_t |= Q ... This notation is dangerous. ... Adeq(K_t,Q,C,EC,S,R) ... or Determine(K_t,Q,C,E_C,S,R) ... should not become a new KnowledgeOS primitive. Use the existing vocabulary.
a_rows_sample.statement: Corrects the dangerous overloading of logical entailment notation K_t|=Q (which normally means semantic entailment, much stronger than intended) to the existing Adequacy/Determination vocabulary Adeq(K_t,Q,C,EC,S,R) or Determine(K_t,Q,C,E_C,S,R), so as not to introduce a redundant new primitive, consistent with the established Determination!=Knowledge and Adequacy!=Determination!=Knowledge distinctions.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Delta_t in {Semantic, Epistemic, Resource, Policy} ... I would not call these the four gap types yet ... ClassifyGap: Delta_Q -> G where G is itself still research-open.
a_rows_sample.statement: Rejects freezing the four-way gap taxonomy {Semantic,Epistemic,Resource,Policy} as exhaustive; recommends Delta_Q(K_t) as a typed collection of unsatisfied requirements with a ClassifyGap:Delta_Q->G mapping where G remains research-open, illustrated by four metro-scenario gap readings (inquiry gap, knowledge gap, resource gap, decision/policy gap).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Gap -> Opportunity -> Decision -> Authorization -> Execution ... Proposal != Decision != Authorization != Action. That distinction should remain intact.
a_rows_sample.statement: Separates four conflated concerns in the original design (what is missing, what can be done, what should be done, what is allowed) into an explicit chain Delta_t -> A_t^possible -> A_t^feasible -> a_t* -> Authorization(a_t*) -> Execute(a_t*), preserving the existing Proposal!=Decision!=Authorization!=Action distinction.

a_rows_sample.anchor: a_t^* = argmax_{a in A_t^feasible} EU(a|K_t,Q_t,C_t,S_t) ... KnowledgeOS should not assume that epistemic information gain is always the objective.
a_rows_sample.statement: Corrects EA4's argmax[E[DeltaRed]/Cost] formula as an insufficient decision rule (pure info-gain/cost could select an unsafe action, and sometimes not acting is optimal), generalizing to a_t*=argmax EU(a|K_t,Q_t,C_t,S_t) without freezing the exact utility formula, and abstracting the capability as NextEpistemicAct:(K_t,Q_t,Delta_t,R_t,C_t,EC_t)->A_t to be determined experimentally.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Resource_t(r) = (Avail,Quality,Cost,Risk,Latency,Authority,...) ... Feasible(a|R_t,C_t,EC_t) becomes meaningful.
a_rows_sample.statement: Corrects EA5's simple Filter(A,Resources_t) model to a richer per-resource state Resource_t(r)=(Availability,Quality,Cost,Risk,Latency,Authority,...), making Feasible(a|R_t,C_t,EC_t) meaningful and connecting to the existing evidence-channel work.

a_rows_sample.anchor: unless your actual observation included a specified probability model, that inequality is not established. Likewise "maintaining eye contact" was not part of the original factual description. ... Never move directly O -> P(H) without specifying the inference model.
a_rows_sample.statement: Flags that the worked human trace contains invented (unobserved) details treated as facts (e.g. an unstated probability inequality, 'maintaining eye contact', 'language barrier'), violating the very Observation!=Interpretation discipline KnowledgeOS is meant to enforce; recommends explicitly labeling O(observed)/I(interpretation)/H(hypothesis)/P(probability output) and never moving directly from O to P(H) without a specified inference model.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Q_0 -> Clarification -> Q_1 -> Clarification -> Q_2 ... until WellFormed(Q_n,C) and only then Gap(Q_n,K_t). ... Inquiry Formation ... distinct from Inquiry Resolution.
a_rows_sample.statement: Extends the pipeline with a multi-cycle Inquiry Formation stage (Q0->Clarification->Q1->...->WellFormed(Q_n,C)) preceding gap analysis, explicitly distinguished from Inquiry Resolution; illustrated by the metro example needing a follow-up clarifying question ('Where are you going?') before the direction question is answerable.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Determine(Evidence) BEFORE Act. ... I would not make this universal. ... Required epistemic determination precedes authorized operational action, when the action contract requires determination.
a_rows_sample.statement: Corrects EA7 (universal Determine-before-Act) by distinguishing three action classes (epistemic actions like search/inspect/ask which may precede determination; operational actions requiring determination+authorization; safety/emergency actions taken under uncertainty), giving the conditional rule 'required epistemic determination precedes authorized operational action, when the action contract requires determination', preserving Epistemic Decision != Operational Decision != Authorization.

a_rows_sample.anchor: a metaphor can expose a structure without proving that the metaphor names an architectural component. ... [PROP] Lord/Sarathi is an interpretive naming lens for the two functions; not a canonical architectural name.
a_rows_sample.statement: Demotes EA6's Lord/Sarathi naming to CandidateGenerator(K_t,Delta_t,R_t)->A_t and ActionSelector(K_t,Delta_t,A_t,C_t,EC_t)->a_t, tagging Lord/Sarathi as merely [PROP] interpretive naming, invoking the prior Gita governance lesson that a metaphor can expose a structure without naming an architectural component.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Does epistemic action selection expose a capability that cannot be semantically derived from the existing theory under the frozen contract? ... A new primitive is admissible only if it changes the semantic contract, exposes a required capability absent from the current model, or defeats an existing irreducibility result.
a_rows_sample.statement: Reframes the kernel question from 'should Epistemic Agency become a kernel operator' to 'does epistemic action selection expose a capability that cannot be semantically derived from the existing theory under the frozen contract', restating the standing rule that a new primitive is admissible only if it changes the semantic contract, exposes a required absent capability, or defeats an existing irreducibility result.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Observation equivalence not-implies Intent equivalence ... Good action selection not-implies Correct knowledge ... Resource availability not-implies Resource reliability.
a_rows_sample.statement: Proposes a controlled factorial benchmark (fixed K_t,Q,Delta while varying resources R_t across cases A-D, then epistemic standards/risk/inquiry across cases E-G, expecting A*_A!=A*_B!=A*_C!=A*_D when resources materially differ) plus two adversarial experiments: a 'wrong assumption' test with four worlds sharing an identical observation but different underlying intent, giving Observation equivalence does not imply Intent equivalence; and a 'wrong resource' test where good action selection leads to a wrong search result, giving Good action selection does not imply Correct knowledge and Resource availability does not imply Resource reliability.

a_rows_sample.anchor: EU(a) = E[U_gap(a)] - C_resource(a) - Omega_risk(a) + U_task(a) ... the additive form is not theoretically established. ... EU = F(U_gap,C,Omega,U_task) as the general specification, and treat the additive version as [PROP] EU_additive.
a_rows_sample.statement: The draft's additive four-term utility decomposition EU(a)=E[U_gap(a)]-C_resource(a)-Omega_risk(a)+U_task(a) is corrected to a general (unestablished-form) specification EU=F(U_gap,C,Omega,U_task), with the additive version relegated to [PROP] EU_additive pending experimental validation, since e.g. risk may interact with epistemic benefit rather than subtract independently.

a_rows_sample.anchor: ||Delta_Q(K_t)||_G ... This is currently underdefined ... These don't naturally form a vector space. ... U_gap(a) = V(Delta_t,Delta_{t+1}^a; Q,C,EC,S) where V is a candidate gap-value/reduction function.
a_rows_sample.statement: Rejects assuming a generic norm ||Delta||_G over the gap space, since typed gaps (missing value, missing dimension, contradiction, insufficient evidence, unobservable quantity, underdetermination, model insufficiency, semantic ambiguity) do not naturally form a vector space; replaces it with a general candidate gap-value/reduction function U_gap(a)=V(Delta_t,Delta_{t+1}^a;Q,C,EC,S), with an actual metric d(Delta_t,Delta_{t+1}) introduced only if experiments establish a numerical structure.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Reduction != Validation != Determination != Knowledge ... U_gap must not silently become KnowledgeGain. I recommend the term Expected Gap Resolution Value rather than Expected Epistemic Value
a_rows_sample.statement: Argues raw gap-cardinality reduction (|Delta_{t+1}|<|Delta_t|) does not imply epistemic improvement, via a worked example (3 hypotheses reduced to 1 surviving hypothesis that is false), extending Reduction!=Validation!=Determination!=Knowledge; recommends renaming 'Expected Epistemic Value' to 'Expected Gap Resolution Value' to prevent gap reduction being silently equated with knowledge gain.

a_rows_sample.anchor: rho(a) * E[DeltaRed] ... This risks double counting ... E[U(a)] = sum_o P(o|a,K_t,M) U(a,o) where reliability belongs in the observation/evidence model
a_rows_sample.statement: Corrects the draft's reliability multiplier rho(a)*E[DeltaRed] as risking double-counting reliability (since it may already shape the observation distribution P(O|a,K)); recommends the cleaner E[U(a)]=sum_o P(o|a,K_t,M)U(a,o), moving resource reliability into the observation/evidence model P(O|a,R_t,...) instead.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Constraint != Preference. ... PrivacyViolation(a)=1 may mean a not-in A^feasible rather than EU(a)-1000. ... A^safe = {a: P(harm|a) <= epsilon} and only then a* = argmax_{a in A^safe} EU(a).
a_rows_sample.statement: Corrects the draft's treatment of safety/risk as a soft utility penalty (Omega_risk subtracted, beta(R_t) scaling) to a hard feasibility constraint where appropriate: Constraint != Preference, e.g. a privacy violation should remove an action from A^feasible rather than merely penalize its utility, giving A^safe={a: P(harm|a)<=epsilon} filtered before a*=argmax_{a in A^safe}EU(a); likewise the draft's 'high-precision mode' weight adjustment is reframed as a hard safety constraint rather than a mere utility-weight change.

a_rows_sample.anchor: EU(a1) approx EU(a2) does not mean a1 equiv_sem a2. So I would call it: candidate deterministic tie-break policy not: selection invariant.
a_rows_sample.statement: Corrects the draft's tie-breaking rule (favor lower latency when utilities are approximately equal) from a 'selection invariant' to a 'candidate deterministic tie-break policy', noting approximately-equal expected utility does not imply semantic equivalence of the two actions, and that the tie-break policy should itself be configurable under the active decision regime.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Stop or NoFurtherInvestigation ... Suppose Adeq(K_t,Q,...) = True. Continuing to investigate can have negative utility. ... This prevents KnowledgeOS from becoming an agent that always searches.
a_rows_sample.statement: Adds a Stop/NoFurtherInvestigation candidate action to the action set A^possible, so that once Adeq(K_t,Q,...)=True continuing investigation can legitimately have negative utility and EU(Stop) can win, preventing KnowledgeOS from becoming an agent that always searches.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Agreement(Selection,Validation) not-implies Truth. ... ActionDecisionRecord_t containing at minimum: Inquiry, Current Knowledge State, Typed Gap, Candidate Actions, Resource States, Feasibility Results, Utility Model, Utility Parameters, Risk Policy, Selected Action, Rejected Alternatives, Decision Reason, Authorization.
a_rows_sample.statement: Proposes a counterfactual-action-quality experiment (estimate P(Adeq(K_{t+1}^a,Q)=1 | K_t,Q,R_t) for every candidate action and compare to the selected action, using a candidate Regret(a)=U(a*)-U(a) or outcome proxies) and an adversarial reliability test giving Agreement(Selection,Validation) does not imply Truth; requires an ActionDecisionRecord_t (inquiry, state, typed gap, candidates, resource states, feasibility, utility model/parameters, risk policy, selected action, rejected alternatives, decision reason, authorization) for inspectability.

b_rows_sample.anchor: M = <W,approx,sim,V> ... approx: issue/question relation, sim: epistemic indistinguishability, V: valuation ... KnowledgeState != InquiryState, or more precisely K_t != QState_t.
b_rows_sample.statement: Reads the thesis's core model M=<W,approx,sim,V> (a possible-worlds model with a distinct issue/question relation approx and an epistemic-indistinguishability relation sim) as structural support for KnowledgeState != InquiryState (K_t != QState_t), where K_t is what the system currently represents/attributes and QState_t is what is currently being investigated and which alternatives/questions are active; proposes a richer Inquiry = Question + IssueStructure + EpistemicState + Purpose/Contract in place of a bare tuple Q=(T,P,C,R,Gamma,Sigma).

b_rows_sample.anchor: ZoomIn approx Issue Refinement -- not as an identity, but as a research hypothesis. ... questioning actions ... do not themselves give information immediately; they raise/manage issues ... almost exactly our ZF5: ZoomIn != FactFinding
b_rows_sample.statement: Proposes ZoomIn approx Issue Refinement as a research hypothesis (not identity), and reports that the thesis's characterization of questioning actions as knowledge-seeking actions that do not themselves supply information gives an external theoretical analogue for the already-adopted ZF5 (ZoomIn != FactFinding) and DiscoverySuccess does not imply Determination.

b_rows_sample.anchor: There is no question composition principle ... sequential questioning can produce structures that cannot be represented by one equivalent question. ... Dynamic questioning systems exhibit order-sensitive composition ... KnowledgeOS inquiry operations may require order-sensitive semantics.
b_rows_sample.statement: Reports the thesis's finding that many apparent composition laws fail for questioning actions (sequence order matters; no general question-composition principle exists) as an external research precedent for taking non-commutativity of KnowledgeOS inquiry operations seriously, connecting to the corpus's own empirical Zero(C1oC2)!=Zero(C2oC1) findings, while explicitly refusing to claim the source 'proves' KnowledgeOS non-commutativity ([EXT] dynamic questioning systems exhibit order-sensitive composition -> [PROP] KnowledgeOS inquiry operations may require order-sensitive semantics).

b_rows_sample.anchor: Define observable/question-relevant behavior first -> define equivalence -> minimize structure. ... That does not solve KnowledgeOS semantic equivalence. But it gives us a very strong research direction.
b_rows_sample.statement: Extracts a three-step methodological pattern from the thesis's behavioral-equivalence-then-minimization work (define observable/question-relevant behavior first, then define equivalence, then minimize structure) as a candidate strategy relevant to the corpus's unresolved semantic equivalence (equiv_sem) and capability-preorder (<=_cap) problem, explicitly not itself a solution.

b_rows_sample.anchor: KR-DELQ-INQUIRY-LENS-2026-09 ... Issue/Knowledge Separation ... Question as State-Changing Object ... Issue Refinement ... Resolution ... Inquiry Composition ... Behavioral Equivalence ... Inquiry Strategy -> Epistemic Agency
b_rows_sample.statement: Proposes KR-DELQ-INQUIRY-LENS-2026-09 with six research questions (issue/knowledge separation; question as state-changing object; issue refinement for Zoom-In; determination as contract-relative issue resolution; inquiry-operation commutativity; question-relative behavioral equivalence contributing to equiv_sem) plus a seventh bridge Inquiry Strategy -> Epistemic Agency via the thesis's local-property querying-strategy chapter, all tagged [EXT]/[PROP], Theory v1.2 frozen, kernel untouched, no new primitive.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Epistemic Information != Current Issue/Question Structure ... M = <W,approx,sim,V> ... approx: issue/question relation, representing the alternatives currently relevant to investigation.
b_rows_sample.statement: States the thesis's central distinction Epistemic Information != Current Issue/Question Structure via the model M=<W,approx,sim,V> (possible worlds W, epistemic indistinguishability sim, issue/question relation approx representing alternatives currently relevant to investigation, valuation V), extremely close to the corpus's own emerging Zoom-In problem.

b_rows_sample.anchor: soft announcements that cut epistemic links while keeping the whole model available for further reference ... contrasted with eliminative announcements. ... Focus != Delete ... Inquiry transformation != Knowledge destruction.
b_rows_sample.statement: Extracts the thesis's 'soft announcement' operator (cuts epistemic links while keeping the whole model available, contrasted with eliminative announcements) as an established formal precedent closely resembling the corpus's own ZF1 (Focus != Delete, Inquiry transformation != Knowledge destruction), explicitly not treated as proof of ZF1 within KnowledgeOS.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Question and resolution are different operations ... Question changes the issue structure. Resolution changes the epistemic relation in response to the issue. ... Yes: K_b phi, No: K_b neg phi, Don'tKnow: neg K_b phi and neg K_b neg phi. ... Question Raised not-implies Knowledge Acquired.
b_rows_sample.statement: Extracts the thesis's Question != Resolution separation (question changes issue structure, resolution changes the epistemic relation) and its tripartite answer structure (Yes: K_b(phi); No: K_b(not-phi); Don'tKnow: not-K_b(phi) and not-K_b(not-phi), a legitimate epistemic outcome, not an error) as external formal support for the corpus's own ZoomIn!=FactFinding->Determination pipeline and for Question Raised does not imply Knowledge Acquired / Discovery of an Issue does not imply Determination -- described as almost exactly the Case B witness already designed for KR-ZOOM-FACTFINDING-01, while warning not to copy the three-valued structure directly into KnowledgeOS.

b_rows_sample.anchor: a candidate may be excluded only when the local property provides a justified reason that it cannot be a solution. ... SearchSpaceReduction != ArbitraryCandidateDeletion. ... Excludes(h | E,Q,C,S,R) with a warrant for exclusion. ... Zero != SearchPruning.
b_rows_sample.statement: Extracts the thesis's query-strategy safety condition (a candidate may be excluded from the search space only when a local property provides a justified reason it cannot be a solution) to propose Excludes(h|E,Q,C,S,R) with an explicit exclusion warrant, giving SearchSpaceReduction != ArbitraryCandidateDeletion; separates this Query Strategy/SearchPruning question ('which parts of the search space can safely be ignored while preserving the possibility of finding the solution') from the Zero Lens question ('can this structure be eliminated while preserving the contract'), Zero != SearchPruning, with only a possible (not assumed) relation Zero -> Safe Reduction -> Query Strategy under a suitable contract.

type_signature.domain: hypothesis h, evidence E, inquiry Q, context C, standard S, regime R

b_rows_sample.anchor: ordinary bisimulation was insufficient ... developed a richer behavioral equivalence -- intersection bisimulation/intersimulation -- to preserve exactly the distinctions relevant to the language. ... Define observable language -> define behavioral equivalence -> minimize while preserving it. ... Truth preservation != Full semantic preservation.
b_rows_sample.statement: Extracts the thesis's discovery that ordinary bisimulation was insufficient (it could erase strategically relevant information while preserving modal truth) and its development of a richer intersimulation/intersection-bisimulation equivalence, as a concrete formal precedent for the corpus's unresolved equiv_sem problem and kernel-minimality programme (Define observable language -> define behavioral equivalence -> minimize while preserving it), giving Truth preservation != Full semantic preservation and Observable equivalence depends on what the observer/contract can observe, reinforcing 'minimality is semantic, not syntactic.'

b_rows_sample.anchor: Which source should be queried? ... different information sources, including agents and objective sources/oracles ... SourceSelection != FactFinding. It is an agency/query-planning decision. ... query-available information can be limited by subjective knowledge, measurement instruments, experimental design, computing power, missing resources ... Available != Feasible != Useful != Sufficient.
b_rows_sample.statement: Extracts the thesis's source-selection and resource-limitation discussion to propose S_t^available={Human,Log,Instrument,Database,Network,Agent,Oracle,...} and SelectSource(Q,K,C,S,R), giving SourceSelection != FactFinding (an agency/query-planning decision) and connecting resource limitations (subjective knowledge, instruments, computing power) to the already-established Available != Feasible != Useful != Sufficient chain from the Epistemic Agency resource-state work.

b_rows_sample.anchor: 'Why' questions concern reasons for behavior ... What? -> How? -> Why? -> Why act? ... The last question is already Action Warrant. So this thesis gives additional support for our F_t != W_t != Decision_t.
b_rows_sample.statement: Extracts the thesis's identification of 'why' questions (concerning reasons for behavior) as external support connecting to the corpus's Action Fact-Finding work: a What?->How?->Why?->Why-act? hierarchy where the last question is already Action Warrant, reinforcing F_t != W_t != Decision_t.

b_rows_sample.anchor: a realistic inquiry does not merely contain an unordered set of questions. It maintains a structured agenda whose issues can be raised, resolved, reprioritized, inserted, deleted. ... Inquiry_t = structured, evolving agenda of epistemic issues.
b_rows_sample.statement: Extracts the thesis's structured-inquiry-agenda concept (issues can be raised, resolved, reprioritized, inserted, deleted; being good at research includes asking good questions, not only answering them) to propose Inquiry_t as a structured, evolving agenda of epistemic issues rather than a single question Q_t, and recursive sub-question generation Q_0->Q_1,...,Q_n with Q_i->E_i->Q_{i+1}.

b_rows_sample.anchor: I_t = <Q_t, approx_t, D_t^cand, S_t^source, A_t> ... Factivity Separation: I_t carries no truth assertions ... Non-Destructive Focus: Focus(I_t,w) not-implies w not-in K_t ... State Evolution Autonomy: Delta I_t != empty not-implies Delta K_t != empty (Question Raised not-implies Knowledge Acquired).
b_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes the candidate Inquiry State schema I_t=(Q_t,approx_t,D_t^cand,S_t^source,A_t) (active question DAG with per-question id/target/status/priority; issue-partitioning relation approx_t over states; candidate dimension set; source-dependency map; inquiry agenda/history) with three explicit separation rules: Factivity Separation (I_t carries no truth assertions), Non-Destructive Focus (focusing does not remove states from K_t), and State Evolution Autonomy (Delta I_t!=empty does not imply Delta K_t!=empty), giving ZF5 a clean formal witness Delta I_t!=empty AND Delta K_t=empty.

b_rows_sample.anchor: ZoomIn: (K_t,I_t,O_t) -> (I_{t+1}, D^cand_{t+1}) ... K_t: Current frozen Epistemic State (Unmutated). ... KR-DYNAMIC-QUESTION-INQUIRY-LENS-2026-09 ... DQ1 ... DQ5 ... Does KnowledgeOS require a distinct evolving Inquiry State in order to model fact-finding correctly?
b_rows_sample.statement: Finalizes the ZoomIn operational interface as ZoomIn:(K_t,I_t,O_t)->(I_{t+1},D^cand_{t+1}) leaving K_t unmutated, with a five-step execution sequence (trigger binding, issue-structure restructuring via soft update, candidate dimension discovery, agenda/sub-question generation, source-dependency assignment feeding downstream FactFinding); registers KR-DYNAMIC-QUESTION-INQUIRY-LENS-2026-09 with DQ1-DQ5 (is a dedicated I_t strictly required; how do soft issue updates re-partition alternatives without destroying context; can safe candidate pruning be bounded by exclusion warrants; how does intersimulation bound equiv_sem minimality; how should hierarchical agendas manage recursive sub-questions); poses the deeper research question of whether KnowledgeOS requires a distinct evolving Inquiry State to model fact-finding correctly, while explicitly keeping KR-ZOOM-FACTFINDING-01 as the sole active experiment and using this thesis only as an interpretive lens for its results.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The attached book is not Gila Sher's Epistemic Friction. It is Stefan A. Minica's 2011 PhD thesis, Dynamic-Epistemic Logic of Questions and Inquiry. The file itself identifies that title and author... The previous Sher attribution should therefore not be carried forward for this file.
b_rows_sample.statement: Self-declared source-attribution correction (extracted here as a claim, per the corpus's standing rule that self-declared statuses require independent verification rather than acceptance on citation): the volume most recently analyzed in the preceding thread, previously attributed to Gila Sher's Epistemic Friction, is stated to actually be Stefan A. Minica's 2011 PhD thesis Dynamic-Epistemic Logic of Questions and Inquiry, identified from the file's own title page and Chapter 2 heading; the prior Sher attribution is explicitly withdrawn for this file going forward.

b_rows_sample.anchor: R = sim intersect approx ... What remains possible when we consider both what the agent cannot distinguish and what the current issue considers relevant. ... this intersection is not reducible to either relation alone. ... A_t^rel = A_t^epi intersect A_t^issue.
b_rows_sample.statement: Extracts the thesis's intersection relation R=sim∩approx (what remains possible given both epistemic indistinguishability and current issue relevance, not reducible to either relation alone) as inspiration for a candidate A_t^rel=A_t^epi ∩ A_t^issue representing currently relevant epistemic alternatives that must actually be investigated, tagged [PROP].

b_rows_sample.anchor: Known != Issue != Candidate != Determined ... A gap is not necessarily simply 'something missing.' It can be an unresolved issue over a structured set of alternatives. ... Issue(Q,K_t) = partition/distinction structure over admissible alternatives.
b_rows_sample.statement: Extracts a four-way separation Known != Issue != Candidate != Determined from the thesis's formulas distinguishing facts neither known nor settled that would become known upon resolution, warning that the corpus's existing Gap concept risks carrying too much responsibility (a gap can be an unresolved issue over a structured alternative set, not merely 'something missing'), proposing Issue(Q,K_t) as a candidate partition/distinction structure, [PROP] only.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Questioning != Answering != Resolution which translates very naturally into: ZoomIn != FactFinding != Determination. This is one of the strongest external correspondences we have found so far. But it remains [EXT] -> [PROP], not [PROVED].
b_rows_sample.statement: States that Minica's Questioning != Answering != Resolution translates naturally into ZoomIn != FactFinding != Determination, describing it as the strongest external correspondence found so far for ZF5, explicitly kept at [EXT]->[PROP], not [PROVED]; separately notes Issue Refinement != Information Elimination reinforces the triad ZoomIn != Zero != FactFinding.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Minica explicitly demonstrates that many apparently intuitive composition laws for question/announcement actions do not hold... there is no general question-composition principle for the richer system. ... phi?;phi? != phi? in general. ... we explicitly decided not to assume projection properties for Zoom-In. So the book independently reinforces that decision.
b_rows_sample.statement: Extracts the thesis's demonstration that composition and iteration are not automatically well-behaved for questioning/announcement actions (sequential compositions are not generally equivalent under swap; asking the same question twice need not equal asking it once, phi?;phi? != phi? in general) as independent external reinforcement of the corpus's own methodological rule (do not infer algebraic laws from intuitive operator meaning; test composition explicitly) and of the earlier decision not to assume idempotence/projection properties for Zoom-In, connecting to the corpus's own Zero(S1) and Zero(S2) not implying Zero(S1 union S2) finding.

a_aliases: From Knowledge State to Next Epistemic Act
b_aliases: Dynamic Epistemic Logic of Questions and Inquiry (thesis) as a KnowledgeOS research lens

group_evidence.why_grouped: labels co-occur in the same contribution's labels[] 3 separate times across the corpus

a_rows_sample.anchor: Zero = What are we missing? ... Lord = What else could exist? ... Sārathi = What should the Knower investigate/do next?
a_rows_sample.statement: Establishes a three-way division of epistemic responsibility: Zero asks what is missing, Lord asks what else could exist (expanding the investigation space beyond currently known candidate dimensions), and Sarathi determines what the Knower should investigate or do next -- with the Knower retaining the roles of understand/decide/act.

a_rows_sample.anchor: KnowledgeOS = Knowledge Model + Epistemic Operations ... Epistemic Operations: Zero Lens, Lord Lens, Krishna/Sarathi
a_rows_sample.statement: Proposes a preliminary two-part KnowledgeOS architecture: a Knowledge Model (Observation, Knowledge, Evidence, Dimension, Relationship, Ideal State) plus Epistemic Operations (Zero Lens, Lord Lens, Krishna/Sarathi), sitting beneath the Human Knower/Decision layer.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Zero does not necessarily 'detect missing dimensions' ... Zero cannot generally say: 'There exists an unknown dimension d that you don't know.' That is precisely where Lord Lens becomes important.
a_rows_sample.statement: Restricts Zero's claim about missing dimensions: Zero may only say dimension d is unrepresented if d is already a known candidate dimension; Zero cannot assert the existence of an as-yet-unknown dimension -- that expansion capability belongs to Lord Lens (Zero(K_t) -> known gaps/boundaries; Lord(K_t) -> candidate dimensions/horizons).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Z_t=(U_t,C_t,A_t,M_t) ... I would split this: Z_t=(U_t,C_t,A_t,R_t) where R_t = unresolved/requires-investigation findings. Then Lord can separately produce L(K_t) -> D^{candidate}_t
a_rows_sample.statement: Revises the Zero output tuple from Z_t=(U_t unknowns, C_t conflicts, A_t assumptions, M_t missing dimensions) to Z_t=(U_t,C_t,A_t,R_t) with R_t as unresolved/requires-investigation findings, moving candidate-dimension expansion to a separate Lord function L(K_t) -> D^candidate_t.

a_rows_sample.anchor: D^{known} \subseteq D^{candidate} \subseteq D^{possible} \subseteq \mathcal D ... We should not assume all of those sets are finite or even fully enumerable.
a_rows_sample.statement: Reformulates Lord(K_t) to output D^possible (possible dimensions worth considering) rather than D^true, nesting a chain D^known subset-of D^candidate subset-of D^possible subset-of the potentially unbounded/non-enumerable dimension space D.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Invariant 4: Zero and Lord are Sources, Not Authorities ... Both suggest dimensions; neither establishes them.
a_rows_sample.statement: States four mathematical invariants of the parsing/discovery pipeline: Parsing != Knowledge, Discovery != Validation (candidates require observation to confirm), recursive refinement (D_{t+1} typically differs from or extends D_t), and Zero/Lord are sources of candidates rather than authorities that establish dimensions.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Zero(H_{0:t}) meaning Zero can inspect the evolution of knowledge, not just its current state... Lord can ask: What dimensions were never investigated? ... exposes unexplored regions of the knowledge space
a_rows_sample.statement: Extends Zero and Lord to operate over the entire knowledge history H_{0:t}, not just the current state K_t: Zero can ask when uncertainty first appeared/disappeared, and Lord can identify dimensions that were never investigated across the whole timeline (unexplored regions of the knowledge space), useful for KnowledgeOS governance and auditability.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Lord's role is not: make the existing model coherent. Lord's role is: expand the horizon beyond the current model ... Lord \neq CoherenceRepair
a_rows_sample.statement: Corrects a drift where Lord's suggestions were framed as 'improving coherence'; reasserts Lord != CoherenceRepair -- Lord's role is horizon expansion, and new dimensions it suggests may make the model more complete without making it more coherent.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Lord is really: Hypothesis-space expansion... Lord: (K,I,Z) -> H where H is a hypothesis/candidate space. Candidates can include dimensions, propositions, interpretations, relationships, evidence sources, investigation paths.
a_rows_sample.statement: Generalizes Lord from 'suggest dimensions' to full hypothesis-space expansion producing a candidate space H (dimensions, propositions, interpretations, relationships, evidence sources, investigation paths), with L_t as a selected subset of H_t.

a_rows_sample.anchor: | **Krishna** | Source of Knowledge / Lord Lens | $L: \Omega \rightarrow \mathcal{P}(\Omega)$ |
a_rows_sample.statement: A nine-row core correspondence table maps Gita concepts to KnowledgeOS concepts and formal notation: Krishna -> Source of Knowledge / Lord Lens (L: Omega -> P(Omega)); Arjuna -> the Knower (Actor State A_t); Wisdom/Jnana -> Knowledge State K_t; Action/Karma -> Epistemic Action/Assertion (a_t in A); Doubt/Samsaya -> Gap/Discrepancy (Delta_t); Faith/Sraddha -> Epistemic Trust/Policy (rho); Teacher/Guru -> Source/Evidence (S in S); Liberation/Moksa -> Decision Readiness (DR_t = 1); Attachment/Raga -> Epistemic Bias (b: K_t -> K_t').

a_rows_sample.anchor:
class GitaKnowledgeOS:
    """Complete KnowledgeOS derived from Bhagavad-gītā Chapter 4."""
a_rows_sample.statement: An integrated GitaKnowledgeOS class composes all twelve verse-derived components (lineage, memory, intervention, reward, duty, attachment, dual_analyzer, wise_state, evidence_paths, benefit, learning, closure) alongside the existing Zero/Lord/Sarathi lenses, with an evolve(event) method implementing an eight-step pipeline: observe (Sanjaya) -> interpret (semantic) -> evaluate (Zero, detect_gaps) -> generate (Lord, generate_candidates) -> guide (Sarathi, recommend) -> act (Arjuna, conditional on closure.is_ready_to_act()) -> learn (apply learning.learn()) -> purify (apply learning.purify()). A semantic-extraction helper (_extract_semantics) pattern-matches on literal substring presence in observation content ('action', 'teacher'/'wisdom', 'offering'/'sacrifice') to route to different SemanticStructure types, falling back to a generic 'GeneralObservation' type otherwise.

Elaborates the earlier Zero/Lord/Sarathi/Transition division with explicit role definitions: Zero detects gaps/conflicts/boundaries; Lord expands the possibility space; Sarathi navigates/guides; Transition actually changes state. The earlier Sarathi formalization is given a full function signature: Sarathi(K_t, Z_t, L_t, I_t, Q_t, C_t) -> a_t, where a_t is the next epistemic action -- described as remarkably close to what is now called action selection/guidance, though the modern formal model deliberately avoids promoting the old lens vocabulary into architectural objects. Confirms the earlier KnowledgeOS-as-Epistemic-Sarathi formulation (rather than an answer engine) and its See != Guide != Decide principle, noting it later became compatible with the modern formal chain Evidence != Determination != Proposal != Decision != Authorization != Action.

type_signature.domain: K_t, Z_t, L_t, I_t, Q_t, C_t

a_rows_sample.anchor: The Bayesian formalism provides a complete mathematical foundation for KnowledgeOS's epistemic state, updating mechanism, confirmation theory, decision theory, and justification.
a_rows_sample.statement: The document's culminating 'complete formal system for KnowledgeOS': Sigma_t = {cr_t(P): P in L} as the epistemic state; Sigma_{t+1} = Sigma_t(.|E_t) (or Jeffrey Conditionalization for uncertain evidence) as the transition; confirmation as E confirms H iff Sigma_t(H|E) > Sigma_t(H); decision as a_t = argmax_A sum_i u(A&S_i)*Sigma_t(S_i|A) (EDT) or the CDT analogue; and the Three Lenses re-stated as Zero (regularity/confirmation-measures/Scott Axiom), Lord (Bayes's theorem/likelihood ratios), Sarathi (decision theory/Conditionalization). Final claim: 'These are now formally available to KnowledgeOS' -- asserted without independent derivation or proof of fit to the prior KnowledgeOS kernel formalizations.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Lord(K_t,Z_t,G,H_t) -> Proposal. It does not own the epistemic frame. ... S_t(K_t,Z_t,G,H_t,Proposal) -> Decision. Proposal != Decision.
a_rows_sample.statement: Gives refined typed signatures for Lord (Lord(K_t,Z_t,G,H_t) -> Proposal, explicitly not owning the epistemic frame) and Sarathi (S_t(K_t,Z_t,G,H_t,Proposal) -> Decision), re-affirming Proposal != Decision as an important invariant, and situates both within a full epistemic control loop Observation -> Evidence -> Extraction -> Determination -> K_t -> {IdealState, Zero} -> Gap Delta_t -> Lord -> Proposal -> Sarathi -> Decision -> authorization -> Action -> new Observation -> K_{t+1}.

a_rows_sample.anchor: d* = argmax_d E[Delta G_t | investigate d]. ... a_t* = argmax_a E[epistemic improvement|a] / cost(a)
a_rows_sample.statement: Gives Lord a concrete dimension-discovery objective -- choose the new dimension d expected to most reduce the epistemic-gap vector, d*=argmax_d E[Delta-G_t | investigate d] -- and Sarathi a concrete cost-normalized action-selection objective a_t*=argmax_a E[epistemic improvement|a]/cost(a), framed as deriving the architecture from the mathematics rather than the reverse.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Zero Lens is a KnowledgeOS epistemic capability ... I would not say that Zero Lens is itself a domain object such as Dimension, Observation, or Knowledge.
b_rows_sample.statement: Classifies Zero Lens as an epistemic capability/operation rather than a domain object: Zero != Knowledge, Zero != Dimension, Zero != Observation; formally Zero: K (knowledge states) -> Z (epistemic findings/boundaries).

b_rows_sample.anchor: Known Dimension, Unknown Value | Dimension Not Represented | Dimension Assessed as Absent | Conflicting Values | Unresolved Issue | Assumption Unvalidated
b_rows_sample.statement: Enumerates six distinct types of epistemic gap Zero can detect and insists Zero preserves the distinctions rather than collapsing them: (d,?) unknown value, d not in D^K_t unrepresented, (d,ABSENT) assessed absent, (d,{v1,v2,...}) conflicting, (d,UNRESOLVED), (d,ASSUMED).

b_rows_sample.anchor: KnowledgeOS = Knowledge Model + Epistemic Operations ... Epistemic Operations: Zero Lens, Lord Lens, Krishna/Sarathi
b_rows_sample.statement: Proposes a preliminary two-part KnowledgeOS architecture: a Knowledge Model (Observation, Knowledge, Evidence, Dimension, Relationship, Ideal State) plus Epistemic Operations (Zero Lens, Lord Lens, Krishna/Sarathi), sitting beneath the Human Knower/Decision layer.

b_rows_sample.anchor: D^K_0 = {Person, Side, Role} ... D^K_1 = D^K_0 \cup {Relative, Teacher, Grandfather, Friend, Kinsman, ...} ... Zero(K_1) -> Z_1 = {New Gaps, Unresolved Questions}
b_rows_sample.statement: Worked Arjuna example applying Zero: initial dimension set D^K_0={Person,Side,Role} expands to D^K_1 after observing relatives/teachers, and Zero(K_1) surfaces missing relationship dimensions, unresolved moral conflict, and unassessed consequences as gaps.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Observation -> Knowledge -> Zero -> Missing/Unresolved -> Further Observation ... Zero is not merely a quality-control mechanism at the end.
b_rows_sample.statement: Places Zero inside an investigation loop rather than as a terminal quality-control step: Observation -> Knowledge -> Zero -> Missing/Unresolved -> Further Observation, cycling through Zero -> Lord -> Sarathi -> new inquiry.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Zero does not necessarily 'detect missing dimensions' ... Zero cannot generally say: 'There exists an unknown dimension d that you don't know.' That is precisely where Lord Lens becomes important.
b_rows_sample.statement: Restricts Zero's claim about missing dimensions: Zero may only say dimension d is unrepresented if d is already a known candidate dimension; Zero cannot assert the existence of an as-yet-unknown dimension -- that expansion capability belongs to Lord Lens (Zero(K_t) -> known gaps/boundaries; Lord(K_t) -> candidate dimensions/horizons).

b_rows_sample.anchor: Z_t=(U_t,C_t,A_t,M_t) ... I would split this: Z_t=(U_t,C_t,A_t,R_t) where R_t = unresolved/requires-investigation findings. Then Lord can separately produce L(K_t) -> D^{candidate}_t
b_rows_sample.statement: Revises the Zero output tuple from Z_t=(U_t unknowns, C_t conflicts, A_t assumptions, M_t missing dimensions) to Z_t=(U_t,C_t,A_t,R_t) with R_t as unresolved/requires-investigation findings, moving candidate-dimension expansion to a separate Lord function L(K_t) -> D^candidate_t.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Zero(K)=EpistemicBoundaryAnalysis(K) is, in my view, a better long-term definition ... Zero should not become merely: missing-data detector.
b_rows_sample.statement: Broadens Zero from a mere missing-data detector to a general epistemic boundary analysis over unknown, undefined, unrepresented, unresolved, conflicting, and assumed content.

b_rows_sample.anchor:
Zero detects, but Zero does not prioritize ... Knowledge 
eq Priority ... Conflict 
eq Falsehood ... Unknown 
eq False ... Unresolved 
eq Invalid
b_rows_sample.statement: Establishes two hard constraints on Zero: it detects gaps but does not prioritize them (relevance/priority is a separate contextual evaluation), and it does not determine truth (a detected conflict is not thereby a falsehood, an unknown is not thereby false, and unresolved is not thereby invalid).

b_rows_sample.anchor: Zero Lens is an epistemic capability of KnowledgeOS that examines a knowledge state for epistemic boundaries... without collapsing them into falsity, absence, invalidity, or low confidence ... Zero does not claim to enumerate the unknown unknown.
b_rows_sample.statement: Records the final working specification of Zero Lens for this exchange (status: 'Strong Working Definition') and the explicit limit that Zero does not claim to enumerate unknown unknowns -- that capability belongs to Lord Lens / the infinite knowledge-space hypothesis.

b_rows_sample.anchor: We should not move to Phase 3 yet. We have just discovered something important about the ordering: before defining the relationship between Zero, Lord and Sārathi, we should finish defining the knowledge primitives—especially Dimension
b_rows_sample.statement: Decides to defer formalizing the Zero/Lord/Sarathi relationship (originally planned as 'Phase 3') until the Dimension primitive is fully defined, since Zero can only operate meaningfully once a knowledge state's dimensional structure is known.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Zero can compare D_{observed} with D_{represented} and identify D_{observed}\setminus D_{represented} as a newly exposed epistemic boundary. So Zero doesn't invent the dimension.
b_rows_sample.statement: Refines Zero's role in the presence of Dimension Discovery: Zero detects the set-difference between what observation exposed and what the current model represents (D_observed \ D_represented), rather than inventing or predicting new dimensions itself.

b_rows_sample.anchor: "Show me those." The parser can identify that "those" has an unresolved referent. That is not a dimension yet. It is an epistemic/inquiry gap... this is where Zero becomes part of the language/inquiry pipeline, not merely a post-processing check.
b_rows_sample.statement: Uses an intentionally incomplete question ('Show me those') to argue an unresolved linguistic reference is an epistemic/inquiry gap, not itself a dimension; revises the pipeline to Question -> Semantic Reconstruction -> Open Variables -> Candidate Dimensions -> Inquiry Assessment -> Observation/Clarification, moving Zero into the language pipeline itself (asking the Knower to clarify 'those' when incomplete) rather than only auditing post-hoc knowledge states.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Invariant 4: Zero and Lord are Sources, Not Authorities ... Both suggest dimensions; neither establishes them.
b_rows_sample.statement: States four mathematical invariants of the parsing/discovery pipeline: Parsing != Knowledge, Discovery != Validation (candidates require observation to confirm), recursive refinement (D_{t+1} typically differs from or extends D_t), and Zero/Lord are sources of candidates rather than authorities that establish dimensions.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Z(K) \rightarrow gap \rightarrow question \rightarrow D_{candidate}. Thus Zero can trigger dimension discovery indirectly, without itself being the dimension generator.
b_rows_sample.statement: Reaffirms and slightly extends the Zero/Lord separation: Zero can indirectly trigger dimension discovery via gap->question->D_candidate without itself generating dimensions, preserving Zero-detects-gaps vs Lord-suggests-candidates as the operative division.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Zero should report: 'These two assertions cannot currently be reconciled under the selected model.' But it should not automatically conclude: 'One of them is false.' ... CONFLICT \neq CONTRADICTION
b_rows_sample.statement: Extends the Zero Lens constitutional principle set with CONFLICT != CONTRADICTION (alongside the earlier UNKNOWN != FALSE): Zero must report that two assertions cannot currently be reconciled without concluding either is false, distinguishing 'no logical contradiction detected, potential normative/decision conflict detected' from an outright falsification.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Zero(H_{0:t}) meaning Zero can inspect the evolution of knowledge, not just its current state... Lord can ask: What dimensions were never investigated? ... exposes unexplored regions of the knowledge space
b_rows_sample.statement: Extends Zero and Lord to operate over the entire knowledge history H_{0:t}, not just the current state K_t: Zero can ask when uncertainty first appeared/disappeared, and Lord can identify dimensions that were never investigated across the whole timeline (unexplored regions of the knowledge space), useful for KnowledgeOS governance and auditability.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Z(K,P,C,t) -> (G, C, B) where B = epistemic boundaries/conditions ... 'This conclusion cannot be determined from currently accessible evidence' is an epistemic boundary, not a gap or conflict.
b_rows_sample.statement: Extends Zero's output from a pair (Gaps,Conflicts) to a triple (Gaps, Conflicts, epistemic Boundaries), adding a third category for findings that are neither a missing/insufficient requirement nor a tension between assertions but a fundamental limit on what can currently be determined.

type_signature.domain: KnowledgeState x Purpose x Context x Time

b_rows_sample.anchor: Zero should say: the current model is insufficient to determine the normative implications relevant to Arjuna's decision. Then Zero -> Gap and potentially Lord -> CandidateDimension(MoralObligation). Do not let Zero invent dimensions.
b_rows_sample.statement: Reinforces the Zero-cannot-invent-dimensions constraint in the gap context: Zero must report insufficiency ('the current model cannot determine X') rather than naming a specific missing dimension (e.g. 'Moral_Obligation') outright -- naming a not-yet-considered candidate dimension is Lord's job, preserving the Zero/Lord separation established earlier.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Compute != Change ... Decision != Commitment ... Only committed domain events change the Knowledge State ... Zero(K_t,I_t) -> Z_t, not K_{t+1} ... Zero should not automatically mutate K.
b_rows_sample.statement: Establishes Compute != Change and Decision != Commitment: analytical operations (Query, Compare, Evaluate, DetectConflict, DetectGap) must be pure computations returning results, never automatically mutating K_t; only an explicitly committed event changes the Knowledge State, reaffirming that Zero findings and Lord candidates are computed outputs, not knowledge mutations.

a_rows_sample.anchor: K-1 K_t over 8 primitives ... RATIFIED -- '50 attack classes, no counterexample', COMPUTATIONALLY TESTED ... [NEG] 'Four rival K vocabularies' is WITHDRAWN. K_t is RATIFIED. (A,R) is a projection of it, not an alternative.
a_rows_sample.statement: Section 5: re-audits the seven 'rival K vocabularies' (K-1 through K-7 plus Theory 01's separately-scoped carrier) and reclassifies all as projection/refinement/superseded/rejected/intentionally-different-context, finding no category-G (genuinely incompatible) member, withdrawing the prior 'four rival K vocabularies' framing; per the document's own self-declared status, K-1 (K_t over 8 primitives {Entity,State,Event,Observation,Proposition,Relation,Policy,Action}) is claimed RATIFIED and COMPUTATIONALLY TESTED, (A,R) is claimed as a lossy semantic projection pi_K(K_t) rather than a rival; what the document says genuinely survives is narrower: K-CANONICAL-DECISION is prepared but not taken, K_core (the operational kernel) is not determined (canonical state relationship established =/= canonical operational kernel established), pi_K is not computable (blocked by Qualify) so observational equivalence is refuted, and the 8 ratified primitives have never been shown minimal against an operation space.

b_rows_sample.anchor: (A,R) =_semantic pi_K(K_t). Lossy (replay, policy-eval, authorize unanswerable), definable but not computable (Qualify has no body) ... I wrote that 'which K is canonical is the only blocker no derivation can resolve.' A derivation resolved the relation. What remains is a canonicity choice -- a gove
b_rows_sample.statement: Result 1: characterizes the (A,R)-to-K_t relationship as a lossy semantic projection ((A,R)=_semantic pi_K(K_t), unable to answer replay/policy-eval/authorize questions), definable but not computable since Qualify has no body, and explicitly neither structurally nor observationally equal to K_t; withdraws and replaces the author's earlier, stronger claim that 'which K is canonical is the only blocker no derivation can resolve' with the narrower finding that a derivation actually resolved the relation, leaving only a canonicity choice as a governance act.

group_evidence.why_grouped: explicit agent-stated uncertainty: 'primary-blocker-characterized-and-corrected' POSSIBLY relates to 'oq1-carrier-falsified-k-t-ratified' (batch B0067). Note: Characterization of (A,R) as a lossy, non-computable semantic projection of K_t, correcting an earlier stronger claim about K-canonicity being irresolvable; related to the later OQ-1 carrier findings (S2784).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Pratyaksa Perception ... Anumana Inference ... Upamana Comparison ... Sabda Testimony ... KnowledgeOS Parallel: Observation, Reasoning from evidence, Pattern matching/analogical reasoning, Authority/expert testimony
a_rows_sample.statement: Presents the four Nyaya pramanas with a proposed KnowledgeOS parallel mapping and notes perception is treated as fundamental because the other three depend on prior cognition; concludes KnowledgeOS's existing Evidence/Authority/Reasoning distinctions could be given a structured epistemological framework via this mapping.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Stage 1 Performance: 100% semantic correctness (10/10 examples) with 95% CI [0.510, 1.0]. Zero structure abandonment... Dissociation between semantic correctness (100%) and format adherence (40%) reveals models internalize reasoning content even when strict schema compliance fails.
a_rows_sample.statement: Cites a 2026 preprint (Sathish, University of York, via Zenodo) fine-tuning an LLM on a six-phase Navya-Nyaya methodology (Samshaya/Pramana/Pancha Avayava/Tarka/Hetvabhasa/Nirnaya), reporting 100% semantic correctness on 10 examples but only 40% strict format adherence, interpreted as evidence the methodology teaches genuine reasoning rather than template-filling.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Unlike Western formal logic (divorced from epistemology), Nyaya integrates logic with explicit knowledge sources.
a_rows_sample.statement: Comparative table contrasting Tarka Shastra/Nyaya against Western epistemic logic across knowledge sources, reasoning structure, contradiction handling, authority, doubt, and goal, concluding Nyaya offers a more integrated epistemology+logic+authority framework than Western formal logic alone.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Candidate TARKA-001: Pramana Grounding — Every knowledge claim must be explicitly grounded in valid knowledge sources... Strong candidate — requires validation against EKS/PKS/AIP.
a_rows_sample.statement: Candidate invariant TARKA-001: every knowledge claim must be explicitly grounded in a valid knowledge source (perception/inference/comparison/testimony); classified 'strong candidate', pending validation against EKS/PKS/AIP evidence.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Forbidden Transitions: Knowledge claim without pramana grounding; Inference without vyapti; Tarka treated as independent knowledge source; Unstructured doubt; Reasoning contrary to authority without governed transition; Circular reasoning
a_rows_sample.statement: Tabulates six forbidden transitions derived from Tarka Shastra, each paired with the Nyaya parallel that forbids it (apramana, hetvabhasa, tarka-is-apramana, unclassified samsaya, dustarka, the five circular-tarka fallacies).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Unknown: Whether EKS/PKS/AIP already implement pramana-like distinctions; Whether Nyaya reasoning should be component or separate system; Format adherence challenges in neural implementations (40% in 2026 study)
a_rows_sample.statement: An evidence-boundary table classifies research strength (Strong/Moderate/Weak-No/Unknown); the 'Unknown' bucket explicitly names whether EKS/PKS/AIP already implement pramana-like distinctions, whether Nyaya reasoning should be a component or a separate system, and the 40% format-adherence result as open questions.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The system must not flatten: Sensor observation = Expert statement = AI inference. That would violate epistemic identity.
a_rows_sample.statement: Restates the four-pramana mapping (Pratyaksa/Anumana/Upamana/Sabda -> Observation/Reasoning-derived/Analogy/Authority) and derives a constraint: knowledge sources have different epistemic roles and must not be flattened into equivalence.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Sensor reading != Expert assessment != Logical inference != Historical document ... INV-KOS-Pramana-001: KnowledgeOS SHALL preserve the means by which knowledge was acquired because validity depends on the epistemic method of acquisition.
a_rows_sample.statement: Restates the four pramanas and proposes INV-KOS-Pramana-001, arguing evidence must include Evidence Type + Acquisition Method + Reliability Conditions.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Many AI systems collapse: Observed and Inferred. KnowledgeOS cannot... INV-KOS-InferenceBoundary-001: KnowledgeOS SHALL preserve the distinction between directly observed knowledge and knowledge derived through reasoning.
a_rows_sample.statement: Uses the smoke/fire anumana example to argue inference is a transformation, not a source, and proposes INV-KOS-InferenceBoundary-001 to keep Observation and Inference structurally distinct.

a_rows_sample.anchor: KnowledgeOS should be built around Pramana (Knowledge Sources), not Knowledge Objects... Knowledge is not primarily a stored thing. Knowledge is the output of a reliable process.
a_rows_sample.statement: Contrasts a modern Data->Information->Knowledge model with a Nyaya-inspired Object->Knowledge Source(Pramana)->Valid Cognition->Successful Action pipeline, arguing this book gives 'the runtime architecture of epistemic operations' as opposed to the prior book's 'logic of justification'.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Knowledge Source Registry ... perception: reliability: high_for: [infrastructure_state, runtime_metrics] ... The book identifies four knowledge sources: perception, inference, analogy, testimony
a_rows_sample.statement: Proposes adding a 'Pramana Registry' / Knowledge Source Registry with a YAML schema recording per-source reliability conditions, alongside existing Evidence/Observations/Decisions/ADRs/Governance records.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Word is what is instructed by a trustworthy person (apta)... Word + Reliable Source + Correct Understanding = Knowledge ... KnowledgeTransmission: source, utterance, semantic_context, receiver, cognition, trust
a_rows_sample.statement: Proposes 'Sabda-Pramana as KnowledgeOS Communication Protocol': a message becomes knowledge only when the source is trustworthy, communication succeeds, and the receiver correctly understands it; models this as a KnowledgeTransmission schema.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Knowledge claims must be traceable to their generation process ... Error is a modified version of truth, not a distinct state ... Default trust is the epistemic default ... trust by default and doubt only on reason.
a_rows_sample.statement: Traceable Generation pattern (Nyaya pramana): every knowledge unit records its source/generation conditions; error is modeled as a misplacement rather than a distinct category; the epistemic default is trust, with doubt requiring a reason.

a_rows_sample.anchor: `EvidenceLinks` (l. 209) carries *"evidence references + **acquisition method** + reliability conditions."* **Acquisition method is already there.**
a_rows_sample.statement: Session 1 claims three separate carriers an evidence/claim reference may need: route (S1-F035, by what epistemic means was this obtained, e.g. pratyaksa vs upamana), acquisition procedure (S1-F030), and role (S1-F029). This review disputes the count: EvidenceLinks (l.209) already carries evidence references plus acquisition method plus reliability conditions -- acquisition method is already in law -- and route is very close to acquisition method, so whether they are one carrier or two is the same semantic-denotation question left open at two prior reviews (S2-R-F029, S2-R-F030). The defensible composite is smaller: one carrier already in law (acquisition/route, possibly one thing) plus one genuinely absent carrier (role).

b_rows_sample.anchor: How does a knowledge system distinguish source, means, validation, and realization? ... Knowledge is not one entity -- it has an epistemic pipeline.
b_rows_sample.statement: The Veda-Upanishad-Vedanta analysis is framed as distinct from prior lenses (Topology/Vani/Zero/Gita-Tripuisi/ECS) because it asks how a knowledge system distinguishes source, means, validation, and realization -- introducing the claim that knowledge is not one entity but has an epistemic pipeline.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Source -> Essence extraction -> Interpretation / validation method ... A common mistake in AI systems: Document = Knowledge. Vedanta would reject that.
b_rows_sample.statement: The Veda->Upanishad->Vedanta structure is abstracted as Source->Essence extraction->Interpretation/validation method; warns against the common AI-system mistake of equating Document with Knowledge (better model: Expression->Meaning extraction->Understanding->Validated knowledge).

b_rows_sample.anchor: Pramata (Knower) / Pramana (Validation method) / Prameya (Object known) / Prama (Valid knowledge). This is almost a missing KnowledgeOS primitive.
b_rows_sample.statement: Pramana (means of knowledge) is proposed as the biggest useful concept from Vedanta: it separates Pramata (Knower), Pramana (Validation method), Prameya (Object known), Prama (Valid knowledge). Proposes a 'Knowledge Claim' primitive with fields Object (what is claimed), Source (origin), Method (how established), Validator (who/what validated), State (current epistemic status), replacing a naive Knowledge{content, metadata} structure.

b_rows_sample.anchor: KnowledgeOS may need: Operational Knowledge / Meta-Knowledge ... A system that only stores operational knowledge becomes a documentation system. KnowledgeOS needs knowledge about knowledge.
b_rows_sample.statement: Structural (not literal) borrowing of the Apara Vidya (lower knowledge: facts/sciences/methods/texts) vs Para Vidya (higher knowledge: knowledge of underlying principle) distinction, yielding Operational Knowledge vs Meta-Knowledge; warns that a system storing only operational knowledge degenerates into a documentation system.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Reality -> Observation -> Evidence -> Validation method -> Knowledge claim -> Authority decision -> Published knowledge
b_rows_sample.statement: Combines ECS ('epistemic systems govern belief, not reality') with Vedanta ('knowledge requires a valid means of knowing') into a stronger seven-stage pipeline: Reality->Observation->Evidence->Validation method->Knowledge claim->Authority decision->Published knowledge.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Vedanta adds: Meaning != Valid Knowledge. Because a statement can have meaning but still not be valid. Example: "The server is healthy"
b_rows_sample.statement: Extends the Vani lens (Expression != Meaning) with a Vedanta addition (Meaning != Valid Knowledge). Worked example: "The server is healthy" separates Expression (text exists), Meaning (a health condition is described), Validation (monitoring evidence confirms it), Authority (authorized person/system accepts it) as four distinct, separable layers.

b_rows_sample.anchor: INV-KOS Candidate: Knowledge Requires Provenance of Knowing. A KnowledgeOS knowledge state SHALL preserve not only what is known, but the means by which it became knowable. Forbidden collapse: Statement -> Truth / Source document -> Valid knowledge. Strength: Candidate.
b_rows_sample.statement: New candidate invariant proposed (not yet established): 'Knowledge Requires Provenance of Knowing' -- a KnowledgeOS knowledge state should preserve not only what is known but the means (Claim/Evidence/Method/Validator/Authority) by which it became knowable; forbids collapsing a Statement into Truth or a Source document into Valid knowledge.

b_rows_sample.anchor: How does a knowledge system distinguish source, means, validation, and realization? ... Knowledge is not one entity -- it has an epistemic pipeline.
b_rows_sample.statement: Finalized/placed version of S0213's framing: the Vedanta lens distinguishes source, means, validation, realization, adding an epistemic-pipeline view of knowledge.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Pramata (Knower) / Pramana (Validation method) / Prameya (Object known) / Prama (Valid knowledge). Almost a missing KnowledgeOS primitive.
b_rows_sample.statement: Pramana/Knowledge Claim primitive restated in the placed document (Object/Source/Method/Validator/State fields).

b_rows_sample.anchor: KnowledgeOS may need: Operational Knowledge / Meta-Knowledge
b_rows_sample.statement: Apara Vidya/Para Vidya-derived Operational Knowledge vs Meta-Knowledge distinction restated in the placed document.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Vedanta adds: Meaning != Valid Knowledge. Example: "The server is healthy"
b_rows_sample.statement: Meaning != Valid Knowledge extension restated with the 'server is healthy' worked example (Expression/Meaning/Validation/Authority as separable layers).

b_rows_sample.anchor: Reality -> Observation -> Pramana (valid method) -> Knowledge state -> Authority/publication
b_rows_sample.statement: Combined ECS+Vedanta pipeline restated in the placed document.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Vedanta | Knowing requires a valid means
b_rows_sample.statement: Final lens-contributions synthesis table (EKS/PKS/AIP/Topology/Vani/Zero/Gita/Vedanta/ECS) restated, with Vedanta's row bolded as 'Knowing requires a valid means'.

b_rows_sample.anchor: A knowledge space can contain fundamentally different modes of knowing, not merely more or fewer dimensions.
b_rows_sample.statement: Reads Para Vidya vs Apara Vidya (higher/lower knowledge) not as a ranking to import into KnowledgeOS, but as evidence that a knowledge space can hold fundamentally different MODES of knowing (e.g. knowing phenomena vs knowing substrate/principle) — a change in kind, not merely 'Knowledge = dimensions × values'.

group_evidence.why_grouped: an UNKNOWN-OBJECT-CANDIDATE row (batch B0013, source S0498) named these as alternative candidates for one piece of evidence. why_uncertain: Uses a six-pramana taxonomy (adding Arthapatti and Anupalabdhi) distinct from the four-pramana Nyaya taxonomy indexed as pramana-four-knowledge-sources and from the Pramata/Pramana/Prameya/Prama pipeline of vedanta-pramana-epistemic-pipeline (both B0006); may be a related recurring pramana theme or a genuinely distinct six-source system (closer to Mimamsa/Advaita epistemology).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Superforecasters don't simply look at the immediate case. They first ask: What is the base rate among comparable cases? Then they update using the specifics of the current situation. ... OUTSIDE VIEW -> Reference Class -> Base Rate -> INSIDE VIEW -> Case-specific evidence -> Posterior.
a_rows_sample.statement: ReferenceClass capability formalized (e.g. 'will project X fail?' answered via 500 similar-technology/size/complexity/delivery-model projects' base failure rate updated by current-project deviations), described as much stronger than an LLM saying 'based on my experience, this project looks risky.'

a_rows_sample.anchor: priors cannot simply be pulled from thin air; reasonable priors can be checked, crowdsourced and tested for robustness. ... Prior ≠ arbitrary opinion.
a_rows_sample.statement: PriorAssessment object formalized (proposition/reference class/historical evidence/assumptions/prior distribution/justification/source/date) with the invariant that priors are not arbitrary opinion but checkable/crowdsourceable/testable for robustness; identical evidence can produce very different posteriors depending on the prior (medical-testing examples).

a_rows_sample.anchor: eliminating an external standard can remove relevance, making intercomparison a two-edged sword. ... Internal comparison must not replace External reality. ... The internal comparison does not make 3 acceptable.
a_rows_sample.statement: ReferenceComparison object (Subject -> ComparisonClass -> Internal distribution -> Relative position -> Assessment) allows internal-only assessment (e.g. a service's 3% error rate vs peers' 0.8% median/2.1% 95th-percentile), but the analysis warns internal comparison is a 'two-edged sword' and must not replace an external standard (example: peers averaging 3 critical vulnerabilities does not make 3 acceptable against a policy requiring <1).

b_rows_sample.anchor: the same mathematical distribution can represent different things depending on what it is about. A PDF could represent speed, size, distance, etc. ... We must never store: probability = 0.73 without knowing 0.73 of WHAT?
b_rows_sample.statement: Credal State vs bare Probability Distribution/PDF distinction: the mathematical object alone does not identify its semantic content, so a stored probability must always carry its hypothesis space, evidence, model, time and purpose (NoProbabilityWithoutSemanticReference).

b_rows_sample.anchor: Bayesian models often postulate priors without explaining their etiology, and that explaining where priors come from remains an important open issue. ... PriorBelief: hypothesisSpace, distribution, origin, calibrationContext, timestamp, provenance. ... Every material prior should ideally have provenance.
b_rows_sample.statement: PriorBelief made a first-class epistemic object with explicit origin/provenance (example: prior 'most services are REST' with origin=historical project data, scope, last-calibrated date, evidence count, known exceptions), because Bayesian models often postulate priors without explaining etiology; introduces 'assumption provenance' as a new category alongside evidence provenance.

b_rows_sample.anchor: AI confidence without an explicit epistemic object is not KnowledgeOS evidence. ... A model-generated confidence = 0.91 is merely a claim about its own confidence unless backed by hypothesis, evidence, method, context, calibration, provenance.
b_rows_sample.statement: New AI governance rule following directly from the credal-state/mathematical-representation distinction: a bare AI-reported confidence number is not itself KnowledgeOS evidence unless backed by an explicit hypothesis/evidence/method/context/calibration/provenance package, illustrated by an inspectable 'Architecture Constitution compliance' worked example (prior 0.65 -> posterior 0.91 with evidence, likelihood model, assurance, decision) contrasted with a bare 'I am 91% confident.'

b_rows_sample.anchor: Epistemic quantities are meaningless without semantic identity. ... Epistemic state is a stateful object, not merely a scalar assessment. ... An epistemic transition must be distinguishable from the mathematical mechanism used to calculate it.
b_rows_sample.statement: Three principles called 'probably the most important architectural additions from this book': epistemic quantities are meaningless without semantic identity; epistemic state is a stateful object, not merely a scalar assessment; an epistemic transition must be distinguishable from the mathematical mechanism used to calculate it.

b_aliases: a probability distribution is not itself an epistemic state
