a_rows_sample.anchor: This is experimental, not final … Assessment with an authority field … defined and then unused
a_rows_sample.statement: AF-F-32's Commit-rule crossing (step 025a-2 §36, five conjuncts, no authority conjunct) is verified verbatim and sharpened: the same source, two sections earlier, defines an Assessment object with an authority field that is defined and then left unused in the Commit rule; §23 explicitly boxes 'Authenticity ≠ Authority' and §36 then fails to encode it; §37 admits authority only as an adjective on the observation ('one current authoritative direct observation') -- exactly the collapse Article 3.1 forbids. The finding stands scoped to the PROPOSED-OPEN corpus layer only, not the ratified/authorized surface (GN-29: archaeology outputs are historical evidence, never authority).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Operations are not currently canonical … Reject is not a proven architectural contradiction … Article 8.3 does not solve the operation problem
a_rows_sample.statement: Diagnoses three findings from Step 284: no ratified operation registry exists and candidate registries disagree (Operations NOT ESTABLISHED); the earlier AF-F-31 'Reject is a proven contradiction' claim is judged too strong — the real issue is semantic underdetermination plus governance dependency, not a contradiction in the ratified architecture; and Article 8.3 governs conflict resolution only, it does not define the operation universe or establish A6 transition semantics.

a_rows_sample.anchor: ZONE 3 — ARCHITECTURALLY PRESENT BUT UNDER-SPECIFIED … REJECTED requires a governed, never silent act whose guard is specified nowhere (P-1)
a_rows_sample.statement: Zone 3 holds constructs the architecture requires but does not sufficiently define: the eight primitives are named not typed; REJECTED's guard is unspecified (P-1); CONFLICTED's governed-resolution return rung is unstated (P-2); Committed is a status with no operation to confer it; DC has no ratified admissibility conjunction over its six components.

a_rows_sample.anchor: AF-F-31 · Reject … in the core of all six minimal registries … its specification violates I-12 and Article 8
a_rows_sample.statement: Reject is the only operation reaching the ratified-required REJECTED state and appears in the core of all six candidate minimal registries, yet its specification violates I-12 and Article 8; classified as a tension within the ratified surface, not a defect of the candidate operation set, and explicitly not to be solved while defining operations.

a_rows_sample.anchor: 'Reject' is the one element classified CONTRADICTORY rather than absent
a_rows_sample.statement: In the transformation-semantics audit table, Reject is uniquely classified CONTRADICTORY (a ratified-required state reachable only by an operation that breaches two ratified rules) rather than merely ABSENT like every other transformation-semantics element.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Reject ↓ must reach a required state ↓ but doing so appears to breach I-12 / Article 8 ... whether Reject is a state transition, a non-transition, a failed transformation, a typed result, an exception, an event, or a governance-controlled disposition ... TransformResult { Accepted(K'), Rejected(reason, evidence) } — But we should not invent this now as canon.

a_rows_sample.statement: Distinguishes intrinsic property, assigned status, and observer-relative use as three separate ways a phenomenon/object can be characterized, arguing status is not intrinsic to the object it is assigned to.

a_rows_sample.statement: Connects Searle's institutional layer to the earlier O'Connor Persons and Causes work by distinguishing natural/physical capacity from institutional power, and introduces 'deontic power' (rights, obligations, duties, privileges, permissions, requirements, authorizations, entitlements) as the content that institutional status can generate.

a_rows_sample.anchor:
Those are not physical powers.

They are **institutional powers**.
a_rows_sample.statement: Distinguishes causal/natural power from institutional/deontic power as two fundamentally different kinds of power an agent or role-holder may have.

a_rows_sample.anchor: # 9. And this connects directly to your KnowledgeOS Constitution
a_rows_sample.statement: Connects the deontic-power concept to the project's existing Constitution/governance architecture via an Election -> Mandate -> Role -> Institutional powers -> Rights/obligations cascade.

a_rows_sample.anchor:
WORLD CHANGE
EPISTEMIC CHANGE
INSTITUTIONAL CHANGE
a_rows_sample.statement: Introduces a three-way knowledge-transition distinction: WORLD CHANGE, EPISTEMIC CHANGE, and INSTITUTIONAL CHANGE, as separate kinds of transition a KnowledgeOS event may represent.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Searle argues that some social/institutional facts depend on **collective intentionality** rather than simply a sum of individual beliefs.
a_rows_sample.statement: Introduces collective intentionality as distinct from individual intentions, arguing it feeds into institutional reality and connecting it to Fagin et al.'s common/distributed knowledge constructs.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Money -> exchange system -> property -> contract -> institutional recognition
a_rows_sample.statement: Analyzes institutional facts as relational rather than isolated: institutional facts form networks of dependency (e.g. money depends on an exchange system, which depends on property, which depends on contract, which depends on institutional recognition).

a_rows_sample.anchor: Searle explicitly argues for the **primacy of social acts/processes over social objects**.
a_rows_sample.statement: Argues for the primacy of process over object in the institutional domain, directly extending the earlier Merricks 'is Assertion really an object?' question: Marriage, Government, Election, Corporation, Money, Contract, and Office are argued to be maintained practices/processes rather than inert objects.

a_rows_sample.anchor:
Institutional Object
=
maintained configuration of
statuses + rules + practices + recognition
a_rows_sample.statement: Proposes a candidate institutional-state model for 'Corporation X' as a maintained configuration of statuses, rules, practices, and recognition, but explicitly flags this as possibly a derived projection rather than a Kernel primitive.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Searle argues that language is **constitutive** for many institutional facts, because a symbolic/representational system is required to maintain status functions
a_rows_sample.statement: Revises the project's earlier conclusion that 'language is merely an expression layer', arguing instead that language is constitutive for many institutional facts (required to maintain and communicate status functions) while not claiming all social facts require sophisticated language, yielding a refined chain: Natural/brute reality -> Social intentionality -> Status assignment -> Symbolic representation -> Institutional reality.

a_rows_sample.anchor: ## Expressive language vs constitutive language
a_rows_sample.statement: Distinguishes expressive language (describes reality) from constitutive language (changes institutional reality), and correspondingly distinguishes a descriptive sentence from a constitutive/performative one.

a_rows_sample.anchor:
"I appoint you chairman."
"The meeting is adjourned."
"I declare the parliament in session."
a_rows_sample.statement: Gives performative-utterance examples that create institutional facts under appropriate constitutive rules: 'I appoint you chairman', 'The meeting is adjourned', 'I declare the parliament in session'.

a_rows_sample.anchor: descriptive assertion: 'Alice is President.' / constitutive act: 'Alice is hereby appointed President.'
a_rows_sample.statement: Distinguishes a descriptive assertion ('Alice is President') from a constitutive act ('Alice is hereby appointed President'), arguing the latter is not merely reporting a fact but may, under correct institutional rule and authority, create/change the status -- extending the project's prior generic definition of 'assertion = claim about something'.

a_rows_sample.anchor:
Therefore KnowledgeOS needs:

```text
utterance
+
speaker
+
authority
+
context
+
constitutive rule
+
institutional state
```
a_rows_sample.statement: Argues KnowledgeOS needs to preserve utterance + speaker + authority + context + constitutive rule + institutional state together in order to correctly interpret institutional claims/actions, since a statement like 'Alice is President' being true and 'I declare Alice President' successfully performing an institutional act depend on different conditions (valid appointment vs. speaker authority under constitutive rules).

a_rows_sample.anchor: He distinguishes explicit rules from **background capacities, abilities, dispositions and practices** that agents use to function within institutions.
a_rows_sample.statement: Adopts Searle's 'background' idea (explicit rules vs. background capacities, abilities, dispositions, and practices agents use to function within institutions) as a further reason the Knowledge Space cannot be reduced to explicit documents; e.g. a Constitution does not contain every practical competence required to execute the institution (explicit rules + procedural know-how + social practices + recognized conventions).

a_rows_sample.anchor: 1. A phenomenon/object can receive a status. ... 10. Some utterances are themselves institutional actions.
a_rows_sample.statement: Applies the Zero Lens (removing money, marriage, president, election, government, property, language, constitution) and derives a ten-item residual list of what survives: (1) a phenomenon/object can receive a status; (2) status is assigned relative to a context; (3) collective intentionality can support the assignment; (4) constitutive rules define what counts as what; (5) statuses can create powers, rights and obligations; (6) institutional facts form networks; (7) institutional facts depend on underlying brute facts; (8) some statuses persist through representation and recognition; (9) institutional processes create/change institutional states; (10) some utterances are themselves institutional actions.

a_rows_sample.anchor: I would add an **Institutional Space**:
a_rows_sample.statement: Proposes adding an Institutional Space branch alongside Natural Space and Semantic Space in the Knowledge Space diagram, containing statuses/roles/rights/obligations/powers/institutions, feeding into an epistemic space and agent/group states, which in turn feed Knowledge projections.

a_rows_sample.anchor: StatusFunction(X,Y,C)
a_rows_sample.statement: Proposes StatusFunction(X,Y,C) (not 'Institution') as the institutional layer's primitive candidate, associated with collective recognition, rule, authority, power, rights, obligations, context, and time; worked example StatusFunction(X=person, Y=President, C=Republic R) generating rights/obligations/powers/responsibilities, argued to be extremely compatible with the constitutional/governance architecture.

b_rows_sample.anchor: TRUE != BELIEVED != KNOWN / ASSERTED != ACCEPTED != TRUE / CONFIDENCE != TRUTH / UNKNOWN != FALSE ... Absence of knowledge must not be represented as falsehood.
b_rows_sample.statement: Williamson's contribution: knowledge is not whatever an agent believes, has epistemic requirements and intrinsic limits; motivates an explicit state vocabulary (UNKNOWN, ABSENT, INSUFFICIENT, QUESTIONABLE, CONFLICTED, REJECTED, VALIDATED, SUPERSEDED, WITHDRAWN) with the exact governed vocabulary left as a domain-law question.

b_rows_sample.anchor: KnowledgeOS must never silently turn "supported" or "probable" into "known."
b_rows_sample.statement: Knowledge is factive: a factive attitude can only be directed toward truths; Williamson treats knowing as the most general factive stative attitude, distinct from believed(P)/supported(P)/probable(P)/asserted(P), all of which 'may be false' while known(P) is factive. This should be a Kernel-level safeguard: never silently convert 'supported' or 'probable' into 'known'.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Williamson rejects the assumption that knowledge can be completely separated into an internal mental part and an external-world part... he explicitly describes knowledge as broad
b_rows_sample.statement: Knowledge is broad: K_A(P) depends not only on A's internal representation but on the external world, context, object of knowledge, and relevant environment. This revises the earlier Agent->projection->Knowledge Space model: the agent does not invent the space, the agent's knowledge is constitutively connected to the space (KNOWLEDGE SPACE Ω -> external world/social reality/semantic structures -> participant/agent -> capacity+access -> epistemic state).

b_rows_sample.anchor: Capacity is not knowledge.
b_rows_sample.statement: A Williamson-inspired correction to the earlier 'knowledge might be a capacity to write information and define its scope' idea: capacity is not knowledge. A system can have high representation capacity (an LLM generating text, a database storing petabytes) without knowing anything. Instead: capacity determines what a participant can potentially represent/investigate/distinguish/communicate; knowledge is a factive epistemic relation/state involving the participant and the external target (CAPACITY -> access/observation/reasoning -> epistemic state -> KNOWLEDGE).

b_rows_sample.anchor: He argues for the **primeness** of knowledge and warns against decomposing it into composite conditions when doing so loses explanatory generality.
b_rows_sample.statement: Knowledge may be prime (non-composite): a maximally detailed decomposition can make an explanation worse by destroying useful generalization. This strengthens the earlier Merricks 'non-redundant work' principle (a candidate primitive deserves first-class status if removing it destroys non-redundant capability) into two tests: the Reduction test ('Can X be reconstructed?') and the Primeness test ('Does treating X as a composite destroy explanatory/general structure?').

b_rows_sample.anchor: Williamson argues that people are not always in a position to know whether they know something. He calls the mistaken assumption that important mental conditions are cognitively transparent **luminosity** and argues against it.
b_rows_sample.statement: Knowledge is not luminous (anti-luminosity): KnowledgeOS cannot assume a participant can perfectly report the state of its own knowledge. 'Agent says I know P' is itself an assertion requiring evaluation; 'Agent says I don't know P' does not necessarily prove P is outside its epistemic capacity. This is a major correction to the previous model of UNKNOWN, requiring KnowledgeOS to distinguish KNOWLEDGE / KNOWLEDGE ABOUT KNOWLEDGE (K_A(K_A(P))) / SELF-ASSESSMENT / EXTERNAL ASSESSMENT / COMPUTATIONAL ESTIMATE as non-equivalent layers, with the second not automatically following from the first.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The agent's **self-report of knowledge** is therefore an object of analysis, not a privileged oracle.
b_rows_sample.statement: For an AI agent claiming 'I know that the architecture decision is valid', KnowledgeOS should be able to represent P, the AI's claim knows(P), the supporting evidence, an external assessment (e.g. 'insufficient'), and the actual status ('unresolved') separately — the agent's self-report of knowledge is an object of analysis, not a privileged oracle.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Williamson's Chapter 5 investigates margins and "close possibilities."
b_rows_sample.statement: Knowledge has a margin: an agent may know P under ordinary circumstances but not under arbitrary tiny variations, so knowledge is not simply a point (TRUE) but can have a 'neighbourhood of epistemic safety'. Proposed quantity M(P,A,C) represents the size/structure of the range of relevant variations under which the knowledge attribution remains stable (not a final formula) — high margin means knowledge remains stable under nearby changes, low margin means small changes may destroy knowledge. This connects the topological lens to epistemology: 'What kinds of changes would invalidate the knowledge attribution?'

b_rows_sample.anchor: Williamson discusses contextual variation in epistemic standards but does not reduce truth/knowledge to arbitrary subjective standards.
b_rows_sample.statement: Knowledge is contextual but not arbitrarily relative: different epistemic contexts (S_t^A, S_t^B, S_t^G) can differ in their knowledge attributions, but this does not mean 'everything is equally true' — different knowledge attributions still point to the same underlying Knowledge Space, supporting the idea that different participants are oriented toward the same infinite space.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Williamson separates causal basis from evidential basis.
b_rows_sample.statement: Cause of belief is not the same as evidence for belief: a perceptual process can be probabilistically caused by the environment without the resulting evidence itself being probabilistic in the same way. This is a non-collapse rule — KnowledgeOS must preserve both relationships (causal basis, evidential basis) separately.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Williamson's Chapters 9–10 develop the idea that **knowledge itself can function as evidence**, and he explicitly identifies one's evidence with what one knows within his framework.
b_rows_sample.statement: Knowledge can be evidence (E=K): observation -> knowledge -> evidence for another proposition -> new knowledge, a recursive structure where the Knowledge Space is not simply 'evidence -> knowledge' but can contain 'knowledge -> evidence -> inference -> knowledge', making knowledge a participating element in reasoning, not merely a final storage state.

b_rows_sample.anchor: He explicitly shows that evidential probability 1 should not be treated as absolute certainty, and that treating evidence as permanently probability-1 creates an implausible monotonicity problem. New evidence can undermine something previously regarded as evidence.
b_rows_sample.statement: Evidential probability 1 must not be treated as absolute certainty; treating evidence as permanently probability-1 creates an implausible monotonicity problem since new evidence can undermine something previously regarded as evidence. This validates Gärdenfors's distinction between historical evidence and permanently-unquestionable evidence: KnowledgeOS evidence history should be immutable, but epistemic status may be revised.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Williamson's Chapter 11 argues for a **knowledge account of assertion**: the connection between knowing and asserting is not accidental.
b_rows_sample.statement: Assertion is downstream from knowledge (knowledge account of assertion): the earlier model 'knowledge -> language' is refined to KNOWLEDGE -> warrant to assert -> ASSERTION -> language/communication. The sentence itself is not the knowledge; the assertion act is a consequence of an epistemic state and a communicative norm, close to Searle's distinction between descriptive and constitutive/performative language.

b_rows_sample.anchor: ### K-INV-01 — Factivity cannot be silently violated
b_rows_sample.statement: Seven proposed Kernel invariants: K-INV-01 Factivity cannot be silently violated (a record labelled 'knowledge' cannot silently mean merely belief/claim); K-INV-02 Representation is not knowledge (storage alone confers no epistemic status); K-INV-03 Knowledge attribution is contextual (must identify participant, scope/context, time); K-INV-04 Self-report is not self-proof ('I know P' is not sufficient proof P is known); K-INV-05 Evidence can be revisable (historical evidence records remain, interpretation can change); K-INV-06 Knowledge history is reconstructible (a current projection must be traceable to its inputs/transformations); K-INV-07 No assumption of epistemic transparency (the system must permit 'I don't know that I don't know P' and incomplete metaknowledge generally).

b_rows_sample.anchor: ### Kernel should preserve
b_rows_sample.statement: Proposed Kernel boundary (inside/outside/above): Inside Kernel — identity, participant, context, boundary, time, representation provenance, observation/source, proposition/content reference, knowledge attribution, epistemic transition, evidence/history, relationships, conflict, revision/supersession, question/inquiry, assessment history, regime reference. Outside Kernel — words, sentences, documents, embeddings, LLMs, vector databases, specific statistical models, possible-world machinery, Bayesian machinery, Pramāṇa implementation, Pāṇinian grammar, topic taxonomy, UI, search algorithm, explanation algorithm. Above the Kernel — knowledge projections, topics, answers, explanations, reports, architecture views, governance views, AI-agent views. Knowledge is present in the Kernel not as Truth+Belief+Evidence but as a KNOWLEDGE ATTRIBUTION (participant -> knows -> proposition -> context/time/boundary/regime), respecting primeness while remaining operational.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The Kernel should not silently overwrite this into: P = KNOWLEDGE
b_rows_sample.statement: The Kernel should NOT decide whether P is 'knowledge' universally. Example: for P='System X is secure', KnowledgeOS may preserve 'Alice claims to know P', 'Audit A provides evidence E', 'Regime R assesses P', 'Verification V says unresolved', 'Bob says not proven' as a KnowledgeAttribution(participant, proposition, context, time, regime, provenance) without collapsing to P=KNOWLEDGE, allowing different epistemologies/regimes to coexist and evaluate independently.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Stop trying to construct "knowledge" bottom-up from representations.
b_rows_sample.statement: The biggest insight: stop trying to construct knowledge bottom-up from representations (words->sentences->propositions->evidence->truth->knowledge is conceptually backwards). Instead: Infinite Knowledge Space -> Knowledge relation/state, which can be represented, asserted, justified, serve as evidence, influence action, or be revised/lost. Representation is a downstream expression of a knowledge-bearing state, not what creates knowledge. This also re-interprets the earlier S_t=P(Ω|A,B,L,U,R,t,H) formula: it is not 'the state of Knowledge itself' but 'a projected epistemic representation of knowledge at t', and K_t^A(P) becomes a knowledge attribution 'Agent A knows P at time t under the relevant context/regime.'

b_rows_sample.anchor: We should not seek: KnowledgeScore ∈ [0,1] as the first objective. Instead quantify **properties of knowledge**
b_rows_sample.statement: Reject a universal KnowledgeScore ∈ [0,1]; instead quantify properties of knowledge Q(K,P,C,t) = (Evidence, Reliability, Margin, Coverage, Consistency, Relevance, Provenance, Stability). Candidate measurable properties: knowledge margin (how much nearby change before attribution fails), evidence contribution (removing evidence e, how much epistemic support changes — Williamson compares total-evidence hypothesis support against support after removing one item), explanatory value (how much knowing P improves prediction/explanation via probability/correlation), knowledge stability (how often an attribution is revised/lost under new evidence), projection coverage (how much declared scope has actually been represented).

b_rows_sample.anchor: KnowledgeOS must be able to represent uncertainty about its own epistemic boundary.
b_rows_sample.statement: Do not try to make the Kernel completely transparent to itself (anti-luminosity applied to the system itself); a system claiming to know exactly what it knows and does not know makes an extremely strong assumption. KnowledgeOS must represent uncertainty about its own epistemic boundary via states: KNOWN, UNKNOWN, UNKNOWN WHETHER KNOWN, DISPUTED, OUTSIDE CURRENT MODEL, UNASSESSED — with 'unknown whether known' being particularly important.

b_rows_sample.anchor: The Knowledge Space is an unbounded space of reality, meaning, institutional structures, events, relations and propositions.
b_rows_sample.statement: Final synthesis: 'The Knowledge Space is an unbounded space of reality, meaning, institutional structures, events, relations and propositions. Persons, machines and organizations have limited capacities and therefore form bounded, contextual, time-dependent projections of that space. Knowledge is a factive relation/state within such a projection—not merely information, representation, belief, evidence or truth alone. KnowledgeOS preserves the identities, contexts, provenance, temporal histories, epistemic transitions and knowledge attributions necessary for those projections to be reconstructed and evaluated under different regimes.' Capstone principle: KnowledgeOS must not confuse the projection with the space, the representation with the knowledge, or the epistemic assessment with reality — supported by McGinn, Floridi, Dretske, Fagin, Gärdenfors, Searle, and Williamson jointly.

a_rows_sample.anchor: FORMAL OBJECTS: Architectural Principle != Architectural Property; V_i=(I_i,O_i,E_i,M_i,T_i,F_i); Referential Integrity < Semantic Historical Integrity
a_rows_sample.statement: Step 210 ('Invariant Verification Matrix') defines a 6-tuple V_i=(I_i,O_i,E_i,M_i,T_i,F_i) per invariant; boxes 'Architectural Principle != Architectural Property' and 'No claim of architectural compliance without identifiable evidence'; defines Reachable(D,E)!=empty; boxes 'Referential Integrity < Semantic Historical Integrity' and 'Epistemic state cannot be silently strengthened'; states Strength(T(x))>Strength(x) requires Justified(T); boxes 'Quantitative value without relevant uncertainty may constitute semantic loss'; defines a statistical-result 8-tuple A=(theta-hat,Estimator,Sample,Population,Model,Assumptions,Uncertainty,Validity); boxes 'Documentation < ExecutableEvidence < FormalProof'; a conceptual Assurance(I)=f(Evidence,Coverage,Independence,Repeatability,Criticality); an E_1..E_5 evidence hierarchy (documentation..formal verification); the target for-all-s-in-S_reachable: I(s)=True; and boxes 'AI may assist assurance; AI should not be the sole source of assurance', plus the 15-row invariant-verification matrix itself (60/60 cells filled).

a_rows_sample.anchor: LATER RESPONSE IN SCOPE: Step 211 reverses Test/Evidence order; Step 212 drops the Owner column and recalibrates E_n
a_rows_sample.statement: Step 210 cites only Step 209 by number ('up to Step 209, we have asked...'). Later response: Step 211 Section 211.2 restates the assurance chain with Test before Evidence, contradicting Step 210's own Section 210.40; Step 212 Section 212.4 reprints I1-I15 minus the Owner column; Step 212 Section 212.6 re-mints an E_0..E_5 scale with different rung definitions than Step 210 Section 210.30's E_1..E_5.

a_rows_sample.anchor: EVOLUTION/DEFINITION VERDICT: CLEAR on the principle/property distinction, CONTRADICTORY on E_1..E_5 (twice)
a_rows_sample.statement: Step 210 answers 'where' (role names) and 'how proven' (test names) but not 'is it true' for any invariant. CLEAR: the principle/property distinction (its best contribution), Referential Integrity < Semantic Historical Integrity, the three assurance levels. INCOMPLETE: V_i is 6-ary, only 3 components ever instantiated. AMBIGUOUS: 'Owner' is used as bounded context, layer, pattern, and team interchangeably. CONTRADICTORY: E_1..E_5 vs Step 212's E_0..E_5 (Contradiction #3), and E_1 bound to two incompatible types within Step 210 itself (Contradiction #4: Section 210.20's evidence-item E_1 vs Section 210.30's documentation-rung E_1).

a_rows_sample.anchor: FIRST INVALID INFERENCE: Section 210.30 vs 210.20 (E_n ambiguity); honest gaps in 210.26/210.28/210.29
a_rows_sample.statement: Section 210.20 uses E_1⇒P and E_2⇒¬P as evidence items; Section 210.30, ten sections later, binds E_1=documentation...E_5=formal verification as evidence-strength levels -- the same subscripted symbol carries two incompatible types with no disambiguation, and every downstream use of E_n in Steps 212-214 inherits the ambiguity. Section 210.29 honestly declines to scalarize Assurance and names fake precision (Assurance=97.3%) as a hazard, yet Section 210.28 immediately prior writes Critical(I)⇒HigherAssurance(I), a comparison requiring the very ordering Section 210.29 declines. Section 210.26 correctly concedes a test provides evidence, not proof (Test(I_8)=PASS does not prove I_8=True in all states), then Section 210.32's target for-all s in S_reachable: I(s)=True leaves S_reachable undetermined (Section 210.33 concedes this openly) -- an honest, correctly-labelled gap, not an invalidity.

a_rows_sample.anchor: COMPUTABILITY: highest rung reached is INPUTS_KNOWN, for I_i/O_i as strings only; 15 tests specified, 0 run
a_rows_sample.statement: V_i is DEFINED with 3/6 components at INPUTS_KNOWN (role-name granularity); the I1-I15 matrix is DEFINED->INPUTS_KNOWN (names) but not CONSTRUCTIBLE (no mechanism/code/test); Assurance(I) is DEFINED but explicitly barred from numeric evaluation; S_reachable is DEFINED but conceded as the open challenge, not CONSTRUCTIBLE. The highest rung reached anywhere in Step 210 is INPUTS_KNOWN, and only for I_i and O_i as strings. TEST VERDICT NOT_EXECUTED: 15 tests specified by name, 0 written, 0 run; Section 210.16's negative test ('can an AI-generated Assessment directly invoke an execution command? Expected: False') is designed in prose and never run against anything.

a_rows_sample.anchor: STATISTICAL VERDICT: STRONG (the 8-tuple A=(theta-hat,...,Validity) is the best statistical section in the band); two correct refusals and two measurement violations
a_rows_sample.statement: Section 210.13's 8-tuple statistical result A=(theta-hat,Estimator,Sample,Population,Model,Assumptions,Uncertainty,Validity) is correct and genuinely good statistical practice, rarely done in architecture documents, but never carried into the matrix (which collapses all eight back into one row) and never connected to the corpus's prior statistical steps (025N, 074, 082, uncited). Correct refusals: Section 210.29 declines to scalarize Assurance (names fake precision explicitly); Section 210.27's Documentation<ExecutableEvidence<FormalProof is a properly-used ordinal. Violations: Section 210.28's Critical(I)⇒HigherAssurance(I) compares assurance levels the same file declines to scale; the E_1<...<E_5 ladder (Section 210.30) is re-issued by Step 212 Section 212.6 with different rung contents and an added E_0 -- the same ordinal scale has two incompatible calibrations in the band, making any statement 'we have E_2 evidence' uninterpretable without knowing which file it was written under -- a scale-integrity failure that silently corrupts later aggregation. The 15-row matrix itself carries no scale at all (purely nominal, no arithmetic attempted -- correct).

a_rows_sample.anchor: DDD VERDICT: MIXED — strong distinctions (Architectural Principle != Property; Referential Integrity < Semantic Historical Integrity; Memory/Identity/History split), weak ownership
a_rows_sample.statement: Architectural Principle != Architectural Property is exactly the right DDD-governance move; Referential Integrity < Semantic Historical Integrity (Section 210.5, a foreign key proves existence not that this version was the artifact used) is a real and useful insight; Section 210.39's Memory/Identity/History separation, concluding the current domain object need not carry all history internally, is correct DDD (event sourcing / separate read model), well argued. Against this, the Owner column's category error means only 4/15 invariants have a single bounded-context owner, 7/15 are owned by a layer or pattern (which cannot be accountable), 5/15 are slash-shared, and I13/I14 are owned by 'Aggregate' -- a tactical pattern name is never the answer to 'who is accountable' in DDD.

a_rows_sample.anchor: ASSUMPTIONS / HIDDEN ASSUMPTIONS / UNDEFINED SYMBOLS — Step 210
a_rows_sample.statement: Stated: each invariant has exactly one owner; a test name determines a test; enforcement can be located by inspection. Hidden: that the 15 invariants are the right 15 (no derivation from I_KOS's 8, no completeness claim); that S_reachable is finite or tractable (required by the for-all quantifier, false for unbounded state); that Owner and Enforcement are separable -- the matrix drops Enforcement and keeps Owner, implicitly assuming Owner=Enforcement, which Step 211 Section 211.29 later denies ('Invariant->Owner present but Enforcement missing = a design gap'), meaning by Step 211's own criterion all 15 rows of Step 210's matrix are design gaps. Undefined symbols: Justified(T), Strength(x), Critical(I), HigherAssurance(I), Coverage/Independence/Repeatability, S_reachable, Estimator/Sample/Population/Validity, DA's codomain Result.

a_rows_sample.anchor: WHAT SURVIVES / WHAT DOES NOT SURVIVE — Step 210, including the word 'Matrix' itself
a_rows_sample.statement: Survives: Architectural Principle != Architectural Property; Referential Integrity < Semantic Historical Integrity; Documentation<ExecutableEvidence<FormalProof; the 8-component statistical result tuple; the refusal of test-as-proof; the refusal to scalarize assurance; the Memory/Identity/History split; the 15 invariant names as a working checklist. Does not survive: the Owner column (11/15 rows unusable); the Verification column as evidence of anything (0/15 executed); V_i as a realized 6-tuple (3/6 realized); E_1..E_5 as a stable scale; and the word 'Matrix' in the title -- a 4-column table realizing 3 of 6 declared dimensions, with no status and no results, is a checklist.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The most damaging collision is E-binding #2 vs #5, which occurs INSIDE ONE FILE (Step 210)
a_rows_sample.statement: Of the twelve distinct bindings of the glyph E catalogued across the band, the most damaging collision is internal to a single file: Step 210 Section 210.20 writes E_1⇒P (an evidence item entailing a proposition), and Step 210 Section 210.30, ten sections later, writes E_1=documentation (the weakest rung of an assurance ladder) -- same symbol, same file, incompatible types, no disambiguation, no notice.

a_rows_sample.anchor: The symbol I is silently rebound between Step 208 (information measure) and Step 209 onward (invariant) with no announcement
a_rows_sample.statement: Step 208 uses I exclusively for an information measure (I(E), I(A), I_required, I_preserved); Step 209 onward uses I exclusively for invariants (I_L, I_C, I_S, I_i, I_identity, I1-I15, I(s)). The rebinding is never announced -- a reader comparing I(C(A)) (Section 208.4, information) to I(s)=True (Section 210.32, an invariant predicate) is reading two different symbols under one glyph.

b_rows_sample.anchor: EL_i=(Step,Artifact,Observation,Fact,Derivation,Decision,Architecture,Invariant,Evidence,Status) ... EL=∪_i EL_i
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines the Evidence Ledger as a per-step 10-field record EL_i=(Step,Artifact,Observation,Fact,Derivation,Decision,Architecture,Invariant,Evidence,Status), with the overall ledger EL as the union across all steps, turning step 213's F/D/P/U discipline into a working data structure.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Observation -> Fact -> Derivation -> Architectural Principle -> Invariant ... Invariant -> Implementation -> Test -> Evidence
b_rows_sample.statement: States the ledger's two-directional fundamental chain (forward: Observation->Fact->Derivation->Architectural Principle->Invariant; feedback: Invariant->Implementation->Test->Evidence->New Knowledge), diagrammed as the architecture's epistemic feedback loop.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Knowledge_t != Knowledge_{t+1} ... The fact that H_2 is better does not mean H_1 never existed
b_rows_sample.statement: States that the ledger must preserve chronology (when a belief was held), not only its content, since a later, better hypothesis H2 does not erase the historical fact that an earlier hypothesis H1 was held -- essential to reconstructing the real engineering journey rather than a retrospectively idealized one.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Calendar chronology ... Engineering chronology ... Epistemic chronology ... The code may exist before the architectural concept has been named
b_rows_sample.statement: Distinguishes three non-identical chronologies (calendar: when it happened; engineering: what was built before what; epistemic: when it was understood), illustrated by Implementation->Observation->Understanding, where code can precede the naming of its own underlying architectural concept.

b_rows_sample.anchor: implementation -> repeated problem -> experiment -> pattern recognized -> concept named ... The later name should not be projected backward as though it had been consciously designed from the beginning
b_rows_sample.statement: Names the 'late naming' phenomenon: a pattern can exist implicitly in the implementation before it is given a formal concept name, and warns against projecting the later name backward as if it had been consciously designed from the start, since that would distort the history.

b_rows_sample.anchor: | Field | Purpose | ... Rejected alternative | What was not chosen |
b_rows_sample.statement: Gives a practical 15-field Evidence Ledger schema (Step ID, Artifact, Date/sequence, Observation, Fact, Interpretation, Derived principle, Decision, Rejected alternative, Architectural consequence, Invariant, Verification, Evidence status F/D/P/U, Confidence, Open question).

b_rows_sample.anchor: What we rejected ... as by: What we selected ... That rejection itself is architectural knowledge
b_rows_sample.statement: Argues architecture is defined as much by what was rejected as by what was selected (e.g. Alternative A rejected because SemanticLoss(A)>0), justifying a dedicated 'Rejected alternative' ledger field as architectural knowledge in its own right.

b_rows_sample.anchor: NegativeKnowledge ... knowledge about approaches, assumptions, transitions or interpretations that have been demonstrated to be unsuitable under specified conditions ... different from failure
b_rows_sample.statement: Introduces NegativeKnowledge as knowledge about approaches/assumptions/transitions/interpretations demonstrated unsuitable under specified conditions, distinguished from mere failure -- a failure becomes useful (negative) knowledge only once its cause ('why it failed') is understood.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Experiment=(Hypothesis,Setup,Observation,Result,Interpretation,Consequence) ... Result -> Knowledge
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines a six-field experimental-lineage record (Hypothesis, Setup, Observation, Result, Interpretation, Consequence) intended to let the eventual book demonstrate the scientific/engineering nature of the work.

b_rows_sample.anchor: A hypothesis says: X may be true ... An invariant says: X must remain true ... Hypothesis -[evidence]-> Pattern -[validation]-> Invariant. Not every hypothesis becomes an invariant
b_rows_sample.statement: Distinguishes hypothesis (X may be true) from invariant (X must remain true) and defines the promotion pipeline Hypothesis->(evidence)->Pattern->(validation)->Invariant, explicitly noting not every hypothesis is promoted.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Observed(H) does not imply Universal(H) ... AllAI -> InconsistentCode [is unwarranted from one tested workflow]
b_rows_sample.statement: States a statistical-discipline guardrail: evidence for H under tested conditions (Observed(H)) must not be generalized to Universal(H), illustrated by a prompt-strategy-specific inconsistency finding that must not be generalized to all AI.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Claim=(Proposition,Context,Conditions) ... Valid(C) should really mean: Valid(C | Context,Conditions)
b_rows_sample.statement: Proposes representing every conclusion as Claim=(Proposition,Context,Conditions) so that validity is always conditioned (Valid(C|Context,Conditions) rather than bare Valid(C)), framed as a connection between DDD and statistical reasoning; extends this to bounded knowledge (Knowledge_A != Knowledge_B across DDD bounded contexts, requiring an explicit ubiquitous-language-guarded translation when a concept crosses a context boundary).

b_rows_sample.anchor: p(C_A) => p'(C_B) ... where p' is the explicitly defined interpretation in the target context. If that implication does not hold, the contract may introduce semantic loss
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines a semantic-preservation condition for cross-context evidence transfer: a property p holding in context C_A after transformation T to C_B must imply the target-context-defined interpretation p' holds in C_B, or the contract introduces semantic loss; states evidence for a claim in one context does not automatically establish it in another without an explicit Mapping and evidence the property survives translation.

b_rows_sample.anchor: ELG=(V,E) ... V=Artifacts∪Facts∪Observations∪Hypotheses∪Decisions∪Principles∪Invariants ... substantially richer than a conventional requirements traceability matrix
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines the Evidence Ledger as a graph ELG=(V,E) with seven node types (artifacts, facts, observations, hypotheses, decisions, principles, invariants) and seven edge types (supports, contradicts, derives, motivates, rejects, implements, verifies), explicitly positioned as richer than a conventional requirements traceability matrix.

b_rows_sample.anchor: C_1 <-[contradicts]-> C_2 ... We should not immediately delete one. Instead record: Contradiction(C_1,C_2) ... Sometimes the contradiction disappears once context is made explicit
b_rows_sample.statement: Treats contradiction as a first-class graph edge to be recorded rather than resolved by deletion; investigating Context(C_1) vs Context(C_2) can dissolve an apparent contradiction, and more generally an apparent contradiction (ModelA accurate vs inaccurate) can resolve into conditional coherence once Context/Population/Time/Purpose dimensions are introduced -- framed as contradiction potentially revealing a missing dimension.

b_rows_sample.anchor: Generation != Adjudication ... Candidates -> Evidence -> Adjudication -> AcceptedKnowledge
b_rows_sample.statement: Applies the contradiction-as-evidence principle to AI-generated competing interpretations: rather than declaring one AI output true and another false, treats {AI_1,AI_2} as an explicit candidate knowledge set requiring adjudication, architecturally separating Generation from Adjudication via Candidates->Evidence->Adjudication->AcceptedKnowledge.

b_rows_sample.anchor: KState in {Observed,Hypothesized,Derived,Corroborated,Contested,Rejected,Accepted,Deprecated} ... should not automatically be treated as a single linear lifecycle ... Accepted + Contested
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines an eight-value knowledge-item epistemic state (Observed/Hypothesized/Derived/Corroborated/Contested/Rejected/Accepted/Deprecated), explicitly not a single linear lifecycle -- states may coexist, e.g. Accepted+Contested when knowledge is operationally accepted but still scientifically disputed; reiterates the anti-Boolean discipline (verified=true is insufficient; use KnowledgeState+Evidence+Context+Time).

b_rows_sample.anchor: UnderlyingPrinciple != CurrentManifestation ... The analogy helps us ask better architecture questions. It does not prove them
b_rows_sample.statement: Applies a Gita chapter-4 analogy (enduring knowledge vs changing manifestation) to DomainInvariant!=CurrentRuntimeState and HistoricalKnowledge!=CurrentRepresentation, explicitly bounding the analogy as interpretive/heuristic ('helps us ask better questions, does not prove them').

b_rows_sample.anchor: S_{t+1} does not contain all information about S_t ... S_{t+1} ⊉ S_t ... CurrentState + HistoricalRecord -> HistoricalUnderstanding
b_rows_sample.statement: Formalizes the 'new state does not know old state' principle as S_{t+1} not-superset-of S_t in general, requiring an additional historical mechanism H_t; concludes CurrentState alone is insufficient and CurrentState+HistoricalRecord is needed for HistoricalUnderstanding, distinguishing CurrentState, HistoricalRecord, and HistoricalInterpretation as three different things.

b_rows_sample.anchor: K_t=(CurrentKnowledge_t,HistoricalKnowledge,Uncertainty_t) ... Update does not necessarily erase prior knowledge ... KnowledgeVersion [distinct from] KnowledgeState ... Git commit != current working tree
b_rows_sample.statement: Defines a knowledge-continuity model K_t=(CurrentKnowledge_t,HistoricalKnowledge,Uncertainty_t) with K_{t+1}=Update(K_t,E_{t+1}), where Update may supersede/qualify/contradict/preserve/deprecate rather than erase prior knowledge; proposes distinguishing KnowledgeVersion from KnowledgeState by analogy to a git commit vs the current working tree, again explicitly flagged as analogy not proof.

group_evidence.why_grouped: labels co-occur in the same contribution's labels[] 6 separate times across the corpus

a_rows_sample.anchor: Step 215 named the objective ... but actually named only 6 of the 182 steps, quoted none, assigned no substantive verdicts to the steps, and left 176 completely absent. Therefore we must not accept Step 215 as the reconstruction we were about to use.
a_rows_sample.statement: First evidence-based finding: an audit artifact reports that Step 215 (which claimed the objective S1..S182->Evidence->Knowledge->Architecture) actually named only 6 of the 182 steps, quoted none, assigned no substantive verdicts, and left 176 completely absent -- Step 215 must therefore NOT be accepted as an actual reconstruction of Steps 1-182.

a_rows_sample.anchor: HistoricalCorpus from ClaimsAboutHistoricalCorpus. The latter cannot substitute for the former.
a_rows_sample.statement: The reconstruction itself becomes an audit subject, exposing a recursive problem: some later steps claiming to audit Steps 1-182 did not actually do so, requiring HistoricalCorpus to be strictly distinguished from ClaimsAboutHistoricalCorpus, since the latter cannot substitute for the former.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Step 212: 0 empirical acts; Step 213: 0 artifacts opened; Step 214: 0 ledger rows; Step 215: no actual reconstruction; Step 216: deferred again. ... EL=\varnothing.
a_rows_sample.statement: Strong evidence of methodological failure absorbed from the audit: Steps 212-216 repeatedly announced empirical work without executing it (0 empirical acts, 0 artifacts opened, 0 ledger rows, no actual reconstruction, deferred again), yielding an effectively empty evidence ledger EL=empty set -- a four-to-five-step deferral chain directly affecting confidence in every conclusion claiming derivation from Steps 1-182.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Steps_{1-182}\overset{?}{\longrightarrow}PhaseReconstruction. The arrow must remain provisional. We should not silently promote the previous conceptual reconstruction into established fact.
a_rows_sample.statement: Withdraws the assumption implicit in Steps 233-235 that Steps1-182->PhaseReconstruction->MathematicalKernel was an established chain; given the reconstruction is known incomplete, the arrow Steps1-182 ?-> PhaseReconstruction must remain marked provisional, not silently promoted to fact.

a_rows_sample.anchor: SemanticIntegrity\propto DistinctionPreservation. ... proportionality requires meaningful ratio scales, while semantic integrity had previously been represented as Boolean ... the expression was not merely unproven; it was ill-typed as a quantitative relationship.
a_rows_sample.statement: Second major finding, absorbed from the audit: the earlier SemanticIntegrity proportional-to DistinctionPreservation expression was not merely unproven but ill-typed, since proportionality requires meaningful ratio scales while semantic integrity had previously been represented as a Boolean SI(C,B)=True -- this is exactly why the audit had to precede further mathematical derivation.

a_rows_sample.anchor: SI(T,K,C)=1 iff L=\varnothing for critical distinctions or L\subseteq DeclaredLoss. The audit explicitly characterizes this final form as well-formed and falsifiable. That is a genuine improvement.
a_rows_sample.statement: Positive development: the corpus subsequently repaired the SemanticIntegrity formula through a documented progression (proportional-to form -> SI(K,T)=Preservation(CriticalSemantics(K)) -> set-theoretic SI(T,K,C)=1 iff L=empty for critical distinctions or L subseteq DeclaredLoss, with L(T,K,C) the set of context-relevant semantic distinctions lost) -- explicitly credited as well-formed and falsifiable, a genuine mathematical improvement.

a_rows_sample.anchor: SI(T,K,C)=1\iff\mathcal C(K,C)\subseteq R(T(K))\cup DeclaredLoss(T,K,C). This is substantially better than: SI\propto DistinctionPreservation.
a_rows_sample.statement: The repaired SemanticIntegrity is restated more rigorously for the Step 232 model: with C(K,C) the critical semantic distinctions of K in context C and R(T(K)) the distinctions recoverable after transformation T, SI(T,K,C)=1 iff C(K,C) subseteq R(T(K)) union DeclaredLoss(T,K,C).

a_rows_sample.anchor: SP(T,K,C) ... T\in\{\mathcal T_{preserving}, \mathcal T_{lossy}, \mathcal T_{invalid}\} depending on its semantic effect.
a_rows_sample.statement: The Step 232 transformation T:mathbb K -|-> mathbb K acquires a semantic-preservation predicate SP(T,K,C)=1 when C(K,C) subseteq R(T(K)) union DeclaredLoss(T,K,C), classifying every transformation into T_preserving, T_lossy, or T_invalid -- a meaningful mathematical development because it arose from an observed flaw and repair, not mathematical decoration.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Step 209 was called an Invariant Algebra, but did not actually provide the required mathematical structure: no clearly defined carrier set; ... Until these are defined, algebra is only a title.
a_rows_sample.statement: Warning absorbed from the audit: Step 209's 'Invariant Algebra' lacked the required mathematical structure -- no clearly defined carrier set, invariants used interchangeably as predicates/propositions/objects, only conjunction as an operation, no algebraic laws; a genuine algebra requires at least (A,Omega,L) (carrier, operations, laws), and until these are defined 'algebra' is only a title.

a_rows_sample.anchor: \mathcal T=\{T:\mathbb K\rightharpoonup\mathbb K\}. This does give us a legitimate candidate carrier ... a much more defensible route toward a transformation monoid/semigroup than Step 209's Invariant Algebra.
a_rows_sample.statement: By contrast, Step 232's transformation set mathcal T={T:mathbb K -|-> mathbb K} with composition o, associativity, and an identity transformation I(K)=K IS a legitimate candidate carrier for a transformation monoid/semigroup, rated a much more defensible mathematical route than Step 209's Invariant Algebra.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Transformation algebra (\mathcal T,\circ,I) from Invariant system \mathcal I=\{I_1,\ldots,I_n\}. The invariants constrain transformations: T\models I. They do not themselves automatically constitute an algebra.
a_rows_sample.statement: Crucial distinction proposed to become canonical: Transformation algebra (mathcal T, o, I) must be separated from Invariant system mathcal I={I_1,...,I_n} -- invariants constrain transformations (T |= I) but do not themselves automatically constitute an algebra.

a_rows_sample.anchor:
Step 210 did populate an invariant verification matrix: 17 rows; 0 TBD; 15 test names; 0 test results. It therefore represents design intent rather than empirical measurement. ... Intent
eq Implementation
eq Execution
eq Observation.
a_rows_sample.statement: Third major finding: Step 210's invariant verification matrix (17 rows, 0 TBD, 15 test names, 0 actual test results) represents design intent rather than empirical measurement -- generalized into the evidence-labeling principle Intent != Implementation != Execution != Observation, exactly the distinction needed for the Steps 1-182 audit.

a_rows_sample.anchor: E_0=assertion, E_1=design intent, E_2=documentary evidence, E_3=implementation evidence, E_4=executed/runtime evidence. ... E_historical for evidence about how a concept actually arose.
a_rows_sample.statement: Revised evidence hierarchy E0<E1<E2<E3<E4 (E0 assertion, E1 design intent, E2 documentary evidence, E3 implementation evidence, E4 executed/runtime evidence), with an added distinguished E_historical category for evidence about how a concept actually arose, especially important for the Gita analysis.

a_rows_sample.anchor: GitaInfluence\in\{None, Analogy, Interpretation, ExplicitDesignInfluence, DemonstratedFoundationalInfluence\}. ... the corpus sometimes asserted conclusions without performing the evidence collection required to substantiate them.
a_rows_sample.statement: New Gita discipline: GitaInfluence classification into 5 values (None, Analogy, Interpretation, ExplicitDesignInfluence, DemonstratedFoundationalInfluence), motivated directly by the audit's demonstration that the corpus sometimes asserted conclusions without performing the required evidence collection.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Step 221 proposed eight candidate concept families ... the supposed Concept Genealogy Map contained zero actual genealogy rows and that the eight families were a taxonomy rather than a demonstrated genealogy. ... ConceptFamilies remain Hypotheses until Steps 1-182 are actually traced.
a_rows_sample.statement: Fourth finding: Step 221's eight candidate concept families (e.g. Family A Identity!=State) are downgraded from an implied genealogy to explicit Hypotheses, since the audit found the Concept Genealogy Map contained zero actual genealogy rows -- a taxonomy, not a demonstrated genealogy.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Can we accept the mathematical architecture and align it with the historical/software architecture? ... Partially -- but not yet canonically.
a_rows_sample.statement: Direct self-assessment of the whole project's original objective: KnowledgeState, Transformation, Lineage, Context, Evidence, Governance, and SemanticIntegrity are currently strong candidates, but the historical derivation from Steps 1-182 has not yet been demonstrated -- the answer to whether the mathematical architecture aligns with the historical/software architecture is 'partially, but not yet canonically'.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Knowledge state | Candidate/strong ... Invariant algebra | Reject as currently formulated ... Concept genealogy | Not yet demonstrated ... Gita as architectural source | Not established ... Gita as interpretive lens | Plausible, requires step-level tracing.
a_rows_sample.statement: Revised canonical status table across 13 concepts: Knowledge state/State transformation/Provenance-lineage/Context/Evidence rated Candidate/strong, Governance constraints rated Strongly supported in later corpus, Semantic integrity rated Candidate now formally improved, Transformation composition rated Mathematically defensible candidate, Invariant algebra explicitly REJECTED as currently formulated, Concept genealogy and eight concept families rated Not yet demonstrated/Hypotheses, Gita as architectural source rated Not established, Gita as interpretive lens rated Plausible but requiring step-level tracing.

a_rows_sample.anchor: KnowledgeOS is a governed knowledge-state transformation system. ... The current evidence supports treating KnowledgeOS as a candidate governed knowledge-state transformation system; this model must be validated against the original Steps 1-182 and the actual implementation before being declared can
a_rows_sample.statement: The key architectural correction: the central thesis is revised from the unqualified assertion 'KnowledgeOS IS a governed knowledge-state transformation system' to the explicitly conditional statement 'the current evidence supports treating KnowledgeOS as a CANDIDATE governed knowledge-state transformation system; this model must be validated against the original Steps 1-182 and the actual implementation before being declared canonical' -- rated scientifically much stronger wording.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Steps 1-182 have not yet been genuinely reconstructed. ... Several later empirical steps were methodological announcements rather than empirical work. ... Do not proceed to further mathematical derivation yet.
a_rows_sample.statement: Step 236 verdict, consolidating five boxed findings: Steps 1-182 have not yet been genuinely reconstructed; several later 'empirical' steps were methodological announcements rather than empirical work; the earlier SemanticIntegrity formula was ill-typed but has since been repaired into a falsifiable set-theoretic form; 'Invariant Algebra' should not be accepted as mathematically established; therefore the programme must not proceed to further mathematical derivation yet.

a_rows_sample.anchor: Step 236 (written 10:13:01) reproduces this verification programme's findings and labels them direct evidence. ... Step 236 attributes these to 'one of the audit artifacts' and 'the corpus audit' -- this programme, unnamed.
a_rows_sample.statement: A systemic finding: Step 236 (primary corpus, written 10:13:01) reproduces this verification programme's own prior findings (from an artifact written 09:00:36) nearly verbatim -- the '6 of 182 steps named, 0 quoted, 176 absent' finding, the 'EL=empty set' notation, the 'four-to-five-step deferral chain' phrase -- attributing them anonymously to 'one of the audit artifacts'/'the corpus audit' without naming this verification programme.

b_rows_sample.anchor: FirstAppearance, FirstFormalization, FirstComputationalization, FirstEmpiricalTest, FirstRepositoryEvidence, CurrentStatus. ... Did the mathematical KnowledgeOS kernel actually emerge from the software/domain evidence, or was it constructed first and only later projected onto the software?
b_rows_sample.statement: Step 239 (tail) proposes a Claim Registry specialized to trace kernel-concept evolution via 6 fields per concept (FirstAppearance, FirstFormalization, FirstComputationalization, FirstEmpiricalTest, FirstRepositoryEvidence, CurrentStatus), aimed at finally answering the central question the whole programme has been approaching: did the mathematical KnowledgeOS kernel actually emerge from software/domain evidence, or was it constructed first and only later projected onto the software -- to be answered before declaring any final mathematical architecture canonical.

b_rows_sample.statement: Explicit warning against confusing recurrence with independence: repeated presence of all five components (pi,lambda,theta,sigma,G) establishes Presence(x_i) but not Independence(x_i,x_j) -- candidate hidden dependencies are proposed (lambda subseteq G since lineage may be graph structure; theta subseteq lambda since lineage already orders time; pi->sigma since policy determines epistemic admissibility), none yet tested.
